what_this_is: The formula in words for every function an outside model is asked to judge and test: how the function gets its answer, every number included. Written by reading the function. read_from is the fingerprint of the function it was read from; build-outside-test-cards.py stops when a function changes until its rule is read again (--reread <id>).

MK-CF-F-001.name: buildBudgetState
MK-CF-F-001.rule: No budget set — the stored monthly expenses missing (budgetFromOnboarding stores none when no expense plan was entered): projected to save is not given (null), never the whole take-home. Otherwise projected to save = monthly take-home − the stored monthly planned expenses; a stored $0 is a $0 plan and counts as $0.

figures_checked_by_hand.$0: not a figure: a stored $0 plan named as an answer

MK-CF-F-002.name: plannedMonthlySpend
MK-CF-F-002.rule: The year's planned expenses ÷ 12: the twelve months spendByMonth gives, added up, divided by 12. A bill with its own months counts once in the year, on top of the single monthly figure the person typed; with no such bill this equals the larger of the categories added up and that typed monthly figure.

MK-CF-F-003.name: categoryMonthly
MK-CF-F-003.rule: 0 when the amount is zero or less. A dollar category: the amount, per month — a once-a-year (non-monthly) category is the yearly amount ÷ 12. A percent category: that percent of the average monthly take-home (pctBaseMonthly) — for a non-monthly one the same, worked as a yearly amount and ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-004.name: spendBuckets
MK-CF-F-004.rule: The categories are in force once at least one has an amount above 0 (categoriesInForce); an empty list, or one whose categories are all 0, is no categories. With categories: each category's monthly amount (categoryMonthly) is added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible — any other bucket counts as flexible; rows of zero are skipped; and while no fixed or flexible category has an amount (only once-in-a-while categories), the typed bills and fixed total is added to fixed and the typed everyday total to flexible. With no categories: the three typed bucket totals. Monthly total = the three added. Dated = the part of non-monthly that is once-in-a-while categories given their own months, each as its monthly twelfth — handed back beside the rest, never inside the monthly figures; 0 with no categories.

MK-CF-F-005.name: actualMonthFlow
MK-CF-F-005.rule: Rows, in this order. Actual inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. One row for each debt with a payment logged against it this month, or with a payment that falls in this month (from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off; for a debt due in full, its whole balance in the month it is due, named "<debt> — due in full") and is not zero: minus what was logged as paid against it this month (0 when nothing was), marked paid or not — each payment given to one debt by debtPaymentsMatched: the debt whose id it names, else the one debt with its payee's name. Other debt payments = debt payments logged this month that match no debt on record, when above zero; and, for each name two or more debts share that a payment was logged under with no id, one more row Other debt payments, minus that payment, marked logged as "<name>" — two of your debts have that name, so it is given to neither. Expenses entered by hand = minus the month's logged expenses that were not imported, debt payments left out. Expenses imported from your card = minus the imported ones, shown only when there are any. Debts on the big-ticket radar (cards, lines of credit, debts due in full) are moved to the end. Surplus = every row added up. Inflow total = the inflow row. Outflow = monthOutflow of the month's expenses so far (minus the expense rows, added up) and its debt paid so far (minus the debt rows, added up) — their sum — so the surplus is the inflow total less the outflow.

MK-CF-F-006.name: allocatableThisMonth
MK-CF-F-006.rule: Surplus − what has already been set aside this month; never below 0.

MK-CF-F-007.name: nonMonthlyBasis
MK-CF-F-007.rule: True, with the percents added up, at full precision, only when there is at least one non-monthly category above zero and every one of them is entered as a percent. Otherwise false and 0.

MK-CF-F-008.name: spendByMonth
MK-CF-F-008.rule: Twelve calendar months: each month's figure is the three groups spendByMonthByBucket gives that month added up — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday — so a screen that shows the groups and one that shows the month read the same amount. Each monthly category adds its monthly amount to every month (a percent category = that percent of the average monthly take-home). Each non-monthly category adds its yearly amount spread evenly over the months it names — over all twelve when it names none (a percent one = percent × average monthly take-home × 12). While only non-monthly categories exist, the typed bills & fixed and everyday totals are added to every month. With no categories: the three typed buckets' total, every month. Then, when the single typed monthly figure is larger than what the plan puts in every month (the monthly categories, the typed totals counted, and a non-monthly category that names no month at its twelfth), the difference is added to every month; a non-monthly category that names its months is on top of the typed figure, in those months only.

MK-CF-F-009.name: monthlyEssentials
MK-CF-F-009.rule: With no categories in force (none with an amount above 0, categoriesInForce): the planned monthly expenses (plannedMonthlySpend). With categories: the monthly categories marked as needs — every one except those marked flexible, a category with no mark counting as flexible, and non-monthly ones left out — added up, each at its monthly amount (categoryMonthly: a percent one = percent of the average monthly take-home), plus the amount by which the typed monthly figure exceeds what the categories put in every month: every category with an amount above 0 at its monthly amount, except a non-monthly category that names its months, since such a bill is on top of the typed figure, in its own months.

MK-CF-F-010.name: emergencyTest
MK-CF-F-010.rule: Essentials = the figure handed in, $0 included, whenever a number is handed in; otherwise monthlyEssentials. Cash after = cash − the shock. Covers it when cash after is zero or more. With essentials above 0: months of cover after the shock = cash after (never below 0) ÷ essentials; months of cover with no shock = cash ÷ essentials; recommended fund = essentials × 3; gap = recommended fund − cash, never below 0. With essentials of 0, those four are not given (null): cash ÷ $0 is no count of months, and a $0 target is no fund.

MK-CF-F-011.name: savingsByMonth
MK-CF-F-011.rule: For each calendar month: the take-home that month (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) − the planned expenses that month (spendByMonth).

MK-CF-F-012.name: annualCashflow
MK-CF-F-012.rule: Gross for the year, after-tax for the year and take-home for the year = the twelve months of incomeMonthlyGrid in each of its three modes, added. Expenses for the year = spendByMonth added. Tax = gross − after-tax. 401(k) = after-tax − take-home. Saved = take-home − expenses.

MK-CF-F-013.name: budgetFromOnboarding
MK-CF-F-013.rule: No budget entered — no profile, or no monthly total, no total typed by group and no category with an amount above 0 (a typed $0 counts as entered): the monthly expenses and the three parts are not given (null). Otherwise the monthly expenses = plannedMonthlySpend (the year's planned expenses ÷ 12), and fixed, non-monthly and flexible = each group's twelve months from spendByMonthByBucket added up ÷ 12, so the three parts add up to the monthly expenses and a bill with its own months is in the total once.

MK-CF-F-014.name: budgetVsActual
MK-CF-F-014.rule: This calendar month's logged expenses — each by the day each record names, read where the person is (the app's one reader of a stored day: a calendar day is that day, a clock time with no zone its own day, an instant the day it was on the person's clock) — leaving out the category Debt payment, added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible by each expense's category. For each bucket: planned = this calendar month's amount in that group from spendByMonthByBucket (the dated plan — a bill with its own months counts only in those months, never as the year's average), spent, remaining = planned − spent. The totals the same way. Each category's spend this month, with the bucket it is counted in, is listed too (the rows under a bucket on the budget editor), so the categories add up to their bucket.

MK-CF-F-017.name: publishSurplus
MK-CF-F-017.rule: Announces the projected-to-save figure to the rest of the app, unchanged.

MK-CF-F-018.name: equityByMonth
MK-CF-F-018.rule: For one calendar year, January first: each vest with a value (equityVests — equityRowValue) whose date names that year and a month goes to that month, at its own value. A vest with a year but no month, or with no date, is in no month. Twelve amounts; all zero when nothing vests that year.

MK-CF-F-019.name: upcomingBills
MK-CF-F-019.rule: Bills = each non-monthly budget category that names at least one month, once for every month it names — a category that names no month has no date and is not a bill here (the month table counts it as a twelfth a month): amount = its yearly amount ÷ the number of months named (a percent one = percent × the take-home the month table carries over its twelve months), on its due day (the 1st when none; a day past the end of a shorter month is that month's last day), at its date this year, or next year when its month is past (nextOccurrence) — a date already passed this month is not returned — in the year it names, when it names one. Only bills due from today to the horizon (365 days when none is given) are returned, soonest first, counted in whole calendar days. Need-by date = due date − 2 calendar days; ask-by date = need-by − 10 calendar days. Money available by the need-by date = what the month table handed in has there by that day: the End of the month before the day's month (the starting balance — the first month's End − its In + its Out — when the day is in the first month; that starting balance for a day before the table, the last month's End for a day after it) + every item of the day's month dated on or before the day (an income with a day added; a bill that is not regular money taken away, on its day, the 1st when it has none) + the lower of 0 and that month's regular money (its In − its Out − the dated incomes + the dated bills). Regular money = the everyday expenses and the monthly debt payments, and every income with no day. Less every bill listed before this one that is due after its need-by date and on or before its due date. Shortfall = bill − available, never below 0. Who covers it = your family when family support is one of the income sources, otherwise your savings or a backup.

MK-CF-F-021.name: defaultPaymentType
MK-CF-F-021.rule: A credit card or a home-equity line: revolving. Every other kind of debt: instalment.

MK-CF-F-022.name: paymentShape
MK-CF-F-022.rule: The payment type recorded on the debt; when none is recorded, defaultPaymentType.

MK-CF-F-023.name: requiredPayment
MK-CF-F-023.rule: 0 for a debt due in full. Otherwise the larger of the minimum monthly payment and the payment the person says they make; a payment set with no minimum entered is that payment.

MK-CF-F-025.name: minimumDebtService
MK-CF-F-025.rule: Each debt's minimum monthly payment added; a debt due in full counts 0.

MK-CF-F-026.name: actualDebtPayment
MK-CF-F-026.rule: Not what was paid this month, whatever its name says: the payments set on each debt — requiredPayment, the payment the person set, never less than its minimum — added over the debts; the same as totalDebtMonthly. What was paid is what is logged against each debt (debtPaymentsByDebt).

MK-CF-F-028.name: loanPayment
MK-CF-F-028.rule: Months = years × 12, rounded to a whole number; monthly rate = the yearly percent ÷ 100 ÷ 12. All zero when the amount borrowed or the months are zero or less. Payment = amount × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate) to the power −months); with no interest, amount ÷ months. Total paid = payment × months. Total interest = total paid − amount.

MK-CF-F-029.name: monthsToClear
MK-CF-F-029.rule: 0 when nothing is owed. No answer when the payment is zero or less, or when it does not exceed the first month's interest (balance × yearly rate ÷ 12) — the debt would never clear. With no interest: balance ÷ payment, rounded up. Otherwise log(payment ÷ (payment − balance × monthly rate)) ÷ log(1 + monthly rate), rounded up to a whole month.

MK-CF-F-030.name: paymentToClearBy
MK-CF-F-030.rule: 0 when nothing is owed or the months are zero or less. Payment = balance × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate) to the power −months), monthly rate = yearly rate ÷ 12; with no interest, balance ÷ months. Rounded UP to the cent.

MK-CF-F-031.name: creditUtilization
MK-CF-F-031.rule: Share = balance ÷ limit (0 when the limit is zero or less), kept at full precision — it is rounded only where it is shown. Good at 30% or under; caution above 30% up to 50%; high above 50%.

MK-CF-F-032.name: creditScoreBand
MK-CF-F-032.rule: 800 and above Excellent; 740 and above Very good; 670 and above Good; 580 and above Fair; below 580 Poor. Good, Very good and Excellent count as good.

MK-CF-F-033.name: debtToIncome
MK-CF-F-033.rule: Share = monthly debt payments ÷ monthly gross income (0 when the income is zero or less), kept at full precision — rounded only where it is shown. Its caller hands it the minimum payments the debts oblige (minimumDebtService), never the payments chosen. Guideline: 36% for a homeowner, 20% otherwise. Good at or under the guideline; caution up to 1.4 × the guideline (50.4% for a homeowner, 28% otherwise); high above that.

MK-CF-F-034.name: payoffPlan
MK-CF-F-034.rule: Only debts with a balance above zero. Nothing is worked out from what was never entered: when any of them has a payment that is not a number (requiredPayment, a debt not due in full) or a rate never entered (rateNotEntered), the walk is not run — months, total interest and still owed are not numbers, never pays off and past the horizon are false, the order is empty, and each such debt is named with what is missing. A debt due in full is paid in its due month (never earlier than month 1; month 1 when it has no date), with interest = balance × ((1 + yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power of the months until then − 1). The others are walked month by month, for at most 12,000 months. Each month: every balance grows by balance × yearly rate ÷ 12; the money to pay = each started debt's payment — the payment the person set, never less than its minimum (requiredPayment; his DEC-0641) — including debts already cleared, whose payments roll on, plus the extra; each debt first gets its payment (never more than it owes); what is left goes to one debt at a time, highest rate first (avalanche) or smallest balance first (snowball). A debt is cleared when it owes a cent or less. A debt whose first payment date is in the future is not paid until that month, and grows meanwhile. Never pays off only when it is proven: once every payment has started, taking the debts still owed from the highest rate down, one more at a time, the money paid each month is no more than what those debts owe together × the lowest of their yearly rates ÷ 12 (what they owe can then never fall). Still owed at month 12,000 without that proof = past the horizon, with what is still owed. Months = the month the last debt is cleared (or the last lump-sum month, when later); when it never clears or is past the horizon, the month the walk stopped. Total interest = all the interest charged up to then; still owed = what is owed when the walk stops (0 when everything clears). Order = each debt with the month it is cleared and the interest it cost, earliest first.

figures_checked_by_hand.0641: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0641 that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-035.name: debtKind
MK-CF-F-035.rule: The label and icon recorded for a kind of debt, from the app's list of eight kinds: Mortgage 🏠, HELOC 🏡, Student loan 🎓, Credit card 💳, Auto loan 🚗, Personal loan 🧾, Medical 🏥, Other 📦; nothing for a kind that is not on the list.

MK-CF-F-036.name: buildDebtState
MK-CF-F-036.rule: Total = the balances that are known, added (totalDebtBalance) — a debt with no balance is left out, not counted as zero. Minimum in a month = minimumDebtService. Actual payment in a month = actualDebtPayment. Highest-rate debt = the one with the largest yearly rate, the first of equals. High-cost debt = the balances of the debts whose rate is ABOVE 7%, added.

MK-CF-F-037.name: inferDebtType
MK-CF-F-037.rule: From the debt's name, capitals ignored, first match wins: heloc or home equity → home-equity line; mortgage or home loan → mortgage; auto, car loan or vehicle → auto; student or tuition → student loan; credit card, visa, mastercard or amex → credit card; medical, hospital or dental → medical; personal → personal; anything else → other.

MK-CF-F-038.name: debtsFromOnboarding
MK-CF-F-038.rule: One debt when the balance entered at sign-up is above zero: its name (Debt when blank), its kind from the name (inferDebtType), the balance, yearly rate = the percent entered ÷ 100, and the minimum payment. None otherwise.

MK-CF-F-041.name: getDebtState
MK-CF-F-041.rule: Loads the stored debts and gives buildDebtState of them; nothing when none are stored.

MK-CF-F-042.name: mortgageOddsEffect
MK-CF-F-042.rule: Nothing when the extra is zero or less, or when the mortgage would never clear at either payment (monthsToClear). Payoff year = the calendar year of the last payment, counted from this month (the first payment): this year + the whole years in ((this month − 1) + (months − 1)) ÷ 12 — worked for the present payment and for payment + extra. Before = the retirement projection's chance of success with the present payment running through its payoff year. After = the chance with payment + extra running through the earlier payoff year, the yearly saving lowered by extra × 12 until then, and raised by (payment + extra) × 12 from the year after.

MK-CF-F-043.name: compareMortgageToTreasury
MK-CF-F-043.rule: Nothing unless the balance, the rate and the payment are all above zero. The Treasury yield used: after federal tax when the person's federal bracket is given (yield × (1 − bracket)), else before tax; the answer says which. Gap = (mortgage rate − the yield used) in percentage points, to two decimals. Too close to call when the gap is under 0.25 points either way; otherwise paying down wins when the gap is positive and Treasuries win when it is negative. Yearly difference = (mortgage rate − the yield used) × balance. Lifetime difference — only with an extra above zero and a mortgage that clears both ways — at the later payoff date, both routes spending payment + extra every month: paying down = what the early route's last payment did not need (payment + extra − that last payment), grown at the yield used over the months freed, plus what (payment + extra) a month grows to over those months; Treasuries = what the extra a month grows to over all the months the mortgage would otherwise run, plus what its last payment did not need (payment − that last payment); the difference is paying down − Treasuries (futureValue, amortise); at a 0% yield it is the interest saved; with no extra, or a payment that never clears, there is none and the answer says why. It also hands back the extra a month it ran on, for the card to name, and what each route comes to (paying down, Treasuries) when there is a lifetime figure. Example: $173,111.17 at 4.10% against a 4.30% Treasury at a 24% bracket → the Treasury keeps 3.268%, gap 0.83 points, paying down wins, about $1,440 a year; with no bracket, −0.20 points, too close to call. $412,000 at 5.5%, $2,400 + $500 a month, a 4.63% Treasury before tax → about $39,618 better off. Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24).

figures_checked_by_hand.$173,111.17: the first example's balance (the outside review's case)
figures_checked_by_hand.0.83: the gap by hand: 4.10 − 3.268 = 0.832 points, to two decimals
figures_checked_by_hand.0.20: the gap with no bracket: 4.10 − 4.30 = −0.20 points
figures_checked_by_hand.$2,400: the second example's payment a month
figures_checked_by_hand.$500: the second example's extra a month
figures_checked_by_hand.$39,618: the second example walked month by month both ways (FIX-ROOM, 2026-10-25); pinned in mortgageVsTreasury.test and MortgageRateCompare.test

MK-CF-F-044.name: annualNet
MK-CF-F-044.rule: The amount each period — for rent, rent less running costs each period — × the periods in a year: weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, quarterly 4, yearly 1, one-off 1.

MK-CF-F-046.name: employerMatchAnnual
MK-CF-F-046.rule: Each source's employer match each period × its periods in a year, added.

MK-CF-F-049.name: buildIncomeState
MK-CF-F-049.rule: Handed the profile (both screen callers hand it): each month is the month grid's (incomeMonthlyGrid) — gross; take-home = gross − tax at the rate in force − the 401(k) — and the year is the twelve added up; rate = the rate in force (rateInForce). Without the profile (the stored record only, getIncomeState): yearly gross = grossAnnualBaseline; rate = the record's own rate when it is switched on (held between 0 and 1), otherwise federal tax ÷ gross for the record's filing status (single when none), no state tax (effectiveRateOnGrossFor); each month = its sources' gross laid on the calendar (monthlyGrossOfSource) × (1 − that one rate); yearly take-home = gross × (1 − rate); monthly = that ÷ 12. Employer match for the year = employerMatchAnnual.

MK-CF-F-052.name: getIncomeState
MK-CF-F-052.rule: Loads the stored income and gives buildIncomeState of it; nothing when none is stored.

MK-CF-F-053.name: annual401kLimit
MK-CF-F-053.rule: 2026: $24,500. At age 50 or over, + $8,000. Ages 60 to 63 get + $11,250 INSTEAD of the $8,000. So $32,500 at ages 50 to 59 and from 64 on, and $35,750 at 60 to 63. With no age: $24,500.

MK-CF-F-054.name: annualIraLimit
MK-CF-F-054.rule: 2026: $7,500; + $1,100 at age 50 or over. With no age: $7,500.

MK-CF-F-055.name: annualHsaLimit
MK-CF-F-055.rule: Not enrolled in Medicare (or not said): 2026, $4,400 for self-only cover or $8,750 for family cover, + $1,000 at age 55 or over. Enrolled, with Medicare's first month in this year given (1–12): that limit × (first month − 1) ÷ 12 — the months before Medicare count (IRS Publication 969). Enrolled with no month given, or a month outside 1–12: 0. Example: 65, self-only, Medicare from July → (4,400 + 1,000) × 6 ÷ 12 = $2,700.

figures_checked_by_hand.969: not a figure: IRS Publication 969, the source named
figures_checked_by_hand.65: the example's age, not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.6: the months before a July start: 7 − 1 (the first month − 1)

MK-CF-F-056.name: k401Headroom
MK-CF-F-056.rule: Limit = annual401kLimit for the age. Used = the year's contribution as given (below zero counts 0) — never cut to the limit. Room = limit − used, never below 0. Excess = used − limit, never below 0 (IRC §402(g): money over the limit has to come out by April 15 or it is taxed twice). Catch-up flag at 50 or over. Example: age 60, $40,000 put in → limit $35,750, used $40,000, room $0, excess $4,250.

figures_checked_by_hand.402: not a figure: the section of the Internal Revenue Code named, §402(g)
figures_checked_by_hand.15: not a figure: the date April 15, named
figures_checked_by_hand.$40,000: the example's contributions, not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.$4,250: the example worked by hand: $40,000 − $35,750 = $4,250; pinned in part13 (MK-CF-F-056)

MK-CF-F-057.name: rothVsTraditional
MK-CF-F-057.rule: Top tax band now at 12% or under: lean Roth. Band now at 24% or over AND the band expected in retirement lower than now: lean Traditional. Anything else: either.

MK-CF-F-058.name: rothConversionWindow
MK-CF-F-058.rule: True when the age is at or past the retirement age AND below the earlier of age 73 and the Social Security claiming age (73 when there is no claiming age).

MK-CF-F-059.name: annualizedEnteredSalary
MK-CF-F-059.rule: Hourly: base pay × hours a week × 52 — no number when no hours a week are entered (a typed 0 is 0 hours). Otherwise base pay × the periods in a year from the one pay-frequency table (payPeriodsAYear: weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, yearly 1; monthly when no frequency is saved) — no number for a frequency the table does not hold.

MK-CF-F-060.name: salaryGrossByMonth
MK-CF-F-060.rule: Each earner's twelve months of gross pay (wageGrossByMonth), added month by month.

MK-CF-F-061.name: grossSalaryMonthly
MK-CF-F-061.rule: The LARGEST of the twelve monthly gross salary figures (salaryGrossByMonth).

MK-CF-F-062.name: equityRowValue
MK-CF-F-062.rule: An option: shares × (market price − strike price), never below 0. Any other grant: shares × price.

MK-CF-F-063.name: rowVestYear
MK-CF-F-063.rule: The year the row's date names (the app's one reader of a typed month and year); nothing when the row has no date — "vest date not entered" (2026-10-25; DEC-0296, tenet 3). It was this year when blank.

figures_checked_by_hand.0296: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0296 that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.3: not a figure: tenet 3 of DEC-3523, named

MK-CF-F-064.name: equityCashFlow
MK-CF-F-064.rule: Every vest with a value (equityVests) added by the year its date names; a vest with no date is in no year; earliest year first.

MK-CF-F-065.name: equityVestWeights
MK-CF-F-065.rule: For one calendar year (this year unless named): each vest of that year with a month goes to that month; each month's share = its value ÷ that year's dated total. Nothing when no vest of that year has a month. A vest of another year, with no month, or with no date is in no month here (2026-10-25: it read every year's vests into one year, and no date into December).

MK-CF-F-066.name: rsuAnnual
MK-CF-F-066.rule: With vesting rows: the value of every vest whose date names the calendar year (this year unless named) — one with a year and no month included, "vest month not entered" — added up; nothing at all when every vest with a value has no date ("vest date not entered"). With none: shares × price, as typed (one yearly figure). It was the total ÷ the number of vest years, a run-rate counted as each year's (2026-10-25; DEC-0012, DEC-0296).

figures_checked_by_hand.0296: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0296 that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-067.name: rentalList
MK-CF-F-067.rule: Each rent entry that names its property (a property identifier that is not blank), whose rent is entered (rentEntryMonthly), with rent or running costs above zero: long-term unless marked short-term, its monthly rent and its monthly running costs. An entry that names no property, or whose rent is not entered, is not counted (DEC-4059d; 2026-10-25, DEC-3768c). With no list of rent entries: nothing.

figures_checked_by_hand.4059: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-4059d (2026-10-10) that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.3768: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3768c that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-068.name: rentalNetAnnual
MK-CF-F-068.rule: (Monthly rent − monthly running costs) added over the rentals, × 12. A rental that loses money pulls the total down.

MK-CF-F-069.name: benefitActiveMonths
MK-CF-F-069.rule: The months, 1 to 12, in which the benefit is paid, in order; all twelve when none are named.

MK-CF-F-070.name: benefitAnnual
MK-CF-F-070.rule: The monthly benefit × the number of months it is paid (benefitActiveMonths).

MK-CF-F-071.name: extraIncome
MK-CF-F-071.rule: Taxed in a month = self-employment (yearly ÷ 12, or the monthly figure) + interest and dividends ÷ 12 + unemployment pay (unemploymentMonthly × the months benefits are paid ÷ 12; IRC §85(a), 2026-10-25) + other income when taxable (yearly ÷ 12, or the monthly figure). Untaxed in a month = the rest of the benefits for the year ÷ 12 + support + scholarships (monthly, or yearly ÷ 12) + other income when marked not taxable. A one-time other payment (landsOnce) goes to one-time taxed or untaxed only in the year it lands; until both its month and its year are on record it is nothing — "year not entered" / "month not entered" — never every year (2026-10-25; DEC-0447, DEC-7940). Reinvested = interest and dividends ÷ 12 unless paid to the bank.

figures_checked_by_hand.85: not a figure: the section of the Internal Revenue Code named, §85(a)
figures_checked_by_hand.0447: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0447 that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.7940: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-7940 that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-072.name: currentRetirementIncomeMonthly
MK-CF-F-072.rule: 0 when the person's chosen income sources are listed and retirement income is not among them; otherwise retirementIncomeMonthly less the Social Security answered "Not yet" (socialSecurityNotYetMonthly) — each source answers for itself (2026-10-25).

MK-CF-F-073.name: otherIncomeMonth
MK-CF-F-073.rule: The month typed for the other income, held between 1 and 12; January when none.

MK-CF-F-074.name: tipsAnnual
MK-CF-F-074.rule: Monthly tips × the number of months with any salary (salaryActiveMonths). Its domain: tips are one figure for the household, tied to no earner, and no screen writes it today — so it is 0 unless an older profile holds a figure.

MK-CF-F-075.name: retirementIncomeMonthly
MK-CF-F-075.rule: Social Security, pension, withdrawals, required distributions, annuities and other, each turned into a month — monthly as it is, quarterly ÷ 3, yearly ÷ 12 — and added.

MK-CF-F-076.name: guaranteedOutsideStreams
MK-CF-F-076.rule: Social Security, pension, annuity and other, each as a monthly amount (quarterly ÷ 3, yearly ÷ 12), only those above zero. Rises with prices: Social Security yes, the others no — unless the person said otherwise. Withdrawals and required distributions are not here.

MK-CF-F-077.name: scholarshipByCalendarMonth
MK-CF-F-077.rule: Twelve months. A monthly scholarship adds its amount every month. A yearly one is split evenly over the months it names, or over all twelve when it names none. With no list: the single typed amount — monthly, or ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-078.name: employerMatchMonthly
MK-CF-F-078.rule: Each earner's match in a month (wageMatchMonthly), added.

MK-CF-F-079.name: incomeFromOnboarding
MK-CF-F-079.rule: Builds the stored income list from the sign-up answers, one source for each amount above zero: base salary = the year's salary as a monthly figure, or — when months differ — the year with each month's share (2026-10-25, DEC-0003), with the employer match; the bonus, yearly, in its month (December when none); stock vesting of this year (rsuAnnual), split by its months; a signing bonus, once, only in the year its date names, in its month (landsOnce; no date: none); each rental, monthly, with its running costs; tips = yearly tips ÷ 12, monthly; retirement income received now, monthly; self-employment, monthly or yearly; interest and dividends, yearly; benefits = the year ÷ 12; support; scholarships; other income (a one-time payment only in its own year). The tax setting: the typed rate, or calculated.

MK-CF-F-080.name: jobActiveMonth
MK-CF-F-080.rule: True when that calendar month's gross salary is above zero.

MK-CF-F-081.name: salaryActiveMonths
MK-CF-F-081.rule: How many of the twelve months have gross salary above zero.

MK-CF-F-082.name: salaryAnnual
MK-CF-F-082.rule: The twelve months of gross salary (salaryGrossByMonth) added.

MK-CF-F-083.name: totalGrossAnnual
MK-CF-F-083.rule: Everything the year is taxed on (taxedSourcesAnnual) with the whole of the Social Security received in place of its taxed part, + untaxed extra in a month × 12 + one-time untaxed income of this year (none when its year is not entered).

MK-CF-F-084.name: taxableAnnual
MK-CF-F-084.rule: The sum of taxedSourcesAnnual's rows: each earner's wages for the year, tips, self-employment, rent net of costs (a loss kept), interest and dividends (the one yearly figure), the bonus, a signing bonus or one-time payment of this year, the stock that vests this year, other taxed income, unemployment pay, retirement income received now, and the part of Social Security IRS Publication 915 taxes (socialSecurityTaxedAnnual on everything else less the 401(k)s). The 401(k) is NOT taken off here (2026-10-25).

figures_checked_by_hand.915: not a figure: IRS Publication 915, the source named

MK-CF-F-085.name: filingStatusOf
MK-CF-F-085.rule: The filing status the person chose: married, married filing separately or head of household; anything else, single. When none is chosen: married when there is a spouse or the spouse earns; single otherwise.

MK-CF-F-086.name: stateRateOf
MK-CF-F-086.rule: The state rate typed, as a percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 15%.

MK-CF-F-087.name: monthlyTaxRates
MK-CF-F-087.rule: Twelve rates, all the same: the rate in force (rateInForce) — the person's own, or the calculated one. A steady income is taxed the same in every month.

MK-CF-F-088.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
MK-CF-F-088.rule: For each calendar month of the year: (gross salary + tips, only in months with salary, − the household's 401(k) that month, never below 0) + net rent ÷ 12 (a loss kept) + that month's stock vesting (equityByMonth for the year) + the level taxed extra (extraIncome less unemployment) + unemployment pay in the months benefits are paid + retirement income's taxed part (retirementIncomeTaxedMonthly) + money that lands once in its own year and month (landsOnce) + the bonus in its month (December when none). Not floored: a month whose rent loss is bigger than the rest is a loss (2026-10-25: it read $0).

MK-CF-F-089.name: over65CountOf
MK-CF-F-089.rule: When a joint return is used — answered, or assumed because a spouse is entered (filingStatusOf) — and the question is answered: both → 2, neither → 0, one → 1 (2026-10-25: the assumed joint return ignored it). Otherwise from the person's own birth year: 1 when this year − birth year is 65 or more, else 0; 0 with no birth year.

MK-CF-F-092.name: incomeMonthlyGrid
MK-CF-F-092.rule: For each calendar month. Earned before 401(k) = that month's taxed income (taxableByCalendarMonth) + that month's 401(k). Untaxed = support + that month's scholarships + the untaxed benefits in their months + a one-time untaxed payment in its own year and month + the part of Social Security that is not taxed. A vest kept as shares (vestsAreCash no) is taken back out of the month and out of its tax — shares are not money (2026-10-25). Gross = earned before 401(k) + untaxed − reinvested interest and dividends − a vest kept as shares. Tax = tax on the wages (each earner's own typed take-home share, or the rate in force) + the rate × the rest, less the rent and interest when the rate is the person's own. Net = gross − tax; available = net − the 401(k). A month with a loss is kept, never floored.

MK-CF-F-097.name: grossFromNet
MK-CF-F-097.rule: 0 when the take-home is zero or less. Otherwise it searches between the take-home and three times it, halving the range 50 times, for the gross at which gross − federal tax (taxOwedFor, no state tax) equals the take-home.

MK-CF-F-099.name: deductionFor
MK-CF-F-099.rule: The standard deduction for the filing status + the age-65 addition × the number of people 65 or over (2 at most) + the senior deduction (seniorDeductionFor). The amounts are in the 2026 table above the cards. Standard deduction only — itemised deductions are not modelled. The income handed in is the year's taxed income after each earner's 401(k), as its callers pass it.

MK-CF-F-100.name: taxableIncomeFor
MK-CF-F-100.rule: Gross − the deduction (deductionFor, with the gross itself used as the income for the senior deduction's phase-out); never below 0. The gross handed in is the year's taxed income after each earner's 401(k), as its callers pass it; standard deduction only.

MK-CF-F-101.name: taxOwedFor
MK-CF-F-101.rule: Taxable income (taxableIncomeFor) taxed band by band on the filing status's 2026 table — each slice at its own rate — plus taxable income × the state rate (held between 0 and 15%).

MK-CF-F-102.name: effectiveRateOnGrossFor
MK-CF-F-102.rule: taxOwedFor ÷ gross; 0 when the gross is zero or less.

MK-CF-F-103.name: marginalBracketFor
MK-CF-F-103.rule: The rate of the band the taxable income falls in; income exactly on a band's top belongs to that band.

MK-CF-F-104.name: ltcgRateFor
MK-CF-F-104.rule: A marginal lookup, labelled as one: the rate on the NEXT dollar of long-term gain on top of this income. On taxable income (taxableIncomeFor): 0% up to the first threshold, 15% up to the second, 20% above. 2026 thresholds — single $49,450 and $545,500; married $98,900 and $613,700; married filing separately $49,450 and $306,850; head of household $66,200 and $579,600. Income exactly on a threshold takes the lower rate. It never prices a gain of any size: the tax on a gain stacks it on the income and slices it across the bands (ltcgTaxOnGain, IRS Schedule D Tax Worksheet), which the draw-order sheet calls since 2026-10-25.

MK-CF-F-105.name: guaranteedRows
MK-CF-F-105.rule: Nothing when the person's chosen income sources are listed without retirement income. Otherwise, over the twelve months starting with the current one, for Social Security, pension, annuity and other retirement income with an amount above zero: monthly → the amount in every month; quarterly → the amount in four months, three apart, starting at its named month (the current month when none); yearly → the amount once, in its named month (the current month when none). The amount is the amount of EACH PAYMENT.

MK-CF-F-106.name: solveSafeDraw
MK-CF-F-106.rule: 0 when the savings are zero or less. Otherwise the largest monthly draw from the savings, on top of the guaranteed income, at which the retirement simulation (1,000 futures, fixed seed 42) still lasts to the horizon in at least the floor (80 of 100 unless another is given). The first top is twice (savings ÷ years ÷ 12), $100 at least; while that top still holds the floor it is doubled (up to 20 times — if even then nothing fails, that top rounded down to $5 is the answer); then the range between the last top that held and the first that failed is halved 12 times; then rounded DOWN to the nearest $5, and that rounded draw is tested again: while it is below the floor it steps down $5 (to $0 at the least).

MK-CF-F-107.name: buildPaycheckYear
MK-CF-F-107.rule: Guaranteed rows from guaranteedRows; savings = the figure given, otherwise the accounts set aside for retirement (retirementEarmarkedValue, handed the profile's rent entries, DEC-4913). Safe draw = solveSafeDraw, with average guaranteed income in a month = the rows' total ÷ 12. Draw flag: high when safe draw × 12 ÷ savings is above 4.5%; ok otherwise; none with no savings or no draw. For each of twelve months from the current one: guaranteed total = that month's rows; bills = that month's dated bills (the table's one reader of a month's dated bills: bills with a date of their own — never a monthly category, the everyday expenses or a debt); safe to spend = guaranteed total + safe draw − bills. This year = the twelve added.

figures_checked_by_hand.4913: not a figure: the owner decision id DEC-4913 (2026-10-13), named in the rule

MK-CF-F-108.name: isMoneyOut
MK-CF-F-108.rule: For a withdrawal, a fee, or a transfer with no receiving account on record: true, unless the money the record moved into the account is known and above zero — a fee refund, a withdrawal stored as money that came in, or a journal into this account is not money out. The money moved into the account is read as everywhere else: when the record says which way the money went, its size, minus when it left; otherwise its amount with the sign it was stored with (a withdrawal or a fee moves its amount out, a transfer moves its amount out of the account it is written on). A record whose amount is not on record is read by its kind: money out. False for every other kind of record.

MK-CF-F-109.name: reviewTransactions
MK-CF-F-109.rule: Flags, in this order; a record is flagged once. (1) Possible duplicate — any new money-out above zero that has an earlier one on the same account with the same amount (within half a cent) and the same payee, 2 days apart or less. (2) For money-out from a LINKED account only — unusually large: with 5 or more money-outs on that account within 90 days of it, at least 3 × their middle value AND at least $500; with fewer than 5, at least $1,000. (3) Otherwise first-time payee — a payee not seen on that account in those 90 days and not on the known list, for $250 or more. (4) Odd pattern — 3 or more money-outs from one account on one day (the new unflagged ones plus earlier ones that day) adding to $1,000 or more.

MK-CF-F-110.name: flagComparisonText
MK-CF-F-110.rule: The sentence for a flag. Unusually large, with a typical figure: it names the typical amount in whole dollars and how many times larger this one is, rounded to a whole number; with none: it says anything over $1,000 is looked at twice. First-time payee and possible duplicate each have a fixed sentence. Several in one day: it names how many and their total in whole dollars.

MK-CF-F-111.name: applyTransaction
MK-CF-F-111.rule: What one record does to the accounts. Adjustment: nothing. Opening position: adds the shares at their price as a purchase. Opening cash: sets the account's cash to the amount, and from then on the cash counts as entered (2026-10-25). Deposit, withdrawal or fee: the cash changes by the money the record moved into the account — up by the amount for a deposit, down by the amount for a withdrawal or a fee; when the record says which way the money went, its size counts that way (a fee refund raises the cash, a deposit reversal lowers it), otherwise the amount counts with the sign it was stored with; a record whose amount is not on record changes nothing. Buy: the shares added as a purchase at their price, and the money moved inside the account (2026-10-23): what the shares cost, shares × price × the shares in one contract the record carries (an option's 100 unless its holding states otherwise, 2026-10-23; 1 for anything else), and the fee the price does not carry (feeNotInPrice) — for an account that keeps its own cash (usesSleeve) the cash goes down by the cost and the fee; a total the person typed goes down by the fee alone (the cost moved inside it); the total of an account built from its holdings is rebuilt from them, and a linked account's total is the broker's and is left as it is; an account whose cash was never entered keeps it not entered (a cash figure the trade opens on an account built from its holdings is marked as never entered, 2026-10-25). Sale with shares: sells at most the shares held (when a purchase has no share count, so the shares held are unknown, the sale stands as recorded for its money, and its shares come only out of purchases whose count is on record — the purchase of unknown size is kept, 2026-10-25), earliest purchases reduced first; the money moved the same way: what the shares sold brought in, shares sold × price × the shares in one contract the record carries, less the fee the price does not carry — the cash up by that for an account that keeps its own cash, a typed total down by the fee alone, a derived or linked total as above; a sale with no shares but an amount lowers the balance by the amount, never below 0. Transfer: the account it is written on changes by the money the record moved into it — down by the amount, or up when the record says the money came in — and the receiving account, when there is one, by the same amount the other way; nothing when the amount is not on record. Transfer of a holding: the whole holding moves to the other account. Dividend, interest or coupon: when reinvested with shares and a price, a purchase is added to a holding already there; otherwise the cash changes by the money the record moved into the account — up by the amount, down when the record says the money left (a reversal) or the amount was stored below zero; nothing when the amount is not on record.

figures_checked_by_hand.100: not a figure this function holds: an option's shares in one contract, read from the record it is handed (stamped from the holding by contractMultiplier, DEC-0274: 100 unless the broker or the person states otherwise)
figures_checked_by_hand.1: not a figure: one share is one share — the record carries no shares per contract, so the trade counts its shares as they are

MK-CF-F-112.name: makeTransaction
MK-CF-F-112.rule: The record as given, with its ticker in capitals, a new id and the time it was made.

MK-CF-F-113.name: affectedAccountIds
MK-CF-F-113.rule: The record's account, and the receiving account when there is one.

MK-CF-F-114.name: undoSnapshot
MK-CF-F-114.rule: A full copy of each account the record touches, as it stands before the record is applied.

MK-CF-F-115.name: restoreUndo
MK-CF-F-115.rule: Each account the record touched is put back to the copy saved with it; the other accounts are unchanged.

MK-CF-F-116.name: inverseOf
MK-CF-F-116.rule: The record that undoes one: a new record noting it is the reversal of the first. When the record states which way its money went (in or out), the undo states the other way — except a transfer between two accounts, which is undone by swapping its two accounts and keeps its own direction (flipping it as well would move the money a second time). A deposit → a withdrawal; a withdrawal or a fee → a deposit; a transfer between two accounts → the same transfer the other way, its two accounts swapped; a transfer out with no receiving account → a deposit; a dividend, interest or coupon paid in cash → a withdrawal; an adjustment → itself. Nothing for a buy, a sale, an opening record, a transfer of a holding or a reinvested payment.

MK-CF-F-117.name: txnLabel
MK-CF-F-117.rule: The plain name for a kind of record; the kind's own code when it has none.

MK-CF-F-118.name: cashEffect
MK-CF-F-118.rule: The change in cash from one record, its amount read by the one rule for a stored amount (2026-10-21): the way the record says the money went, else its kind's own way with the sign it was stored with. Deposit: + amount; a deposit the broker sent with a minus (a reversal, stored as gone out): − amount. Sale: + shares × price × the shares in one contract the record carries (1 when it carries none; 1 contract of an option at $3.00 = $300) less the fee the price does not carry (feeNotInPrice, 2026-10-23) — the amount, when that product is zero, with no fee taken off it. Dividend, interest, coupon: + amount; 0 when reinvested. Withdrawal or fee: − amount; + amount when the record says it came in. Buy: − (shares × price × the shares in one contract the record carries + the fee the price does not carry) — 1 contract at $2.50 = −$250. Transfer: − amount; a transfer that names only one account and says it came in (a broker's journal): + amount. A deposit, withdrawal, fee, transfer, dividend, interest or coupon with no amount on record: 0. Anything else: 0.

figures_checked_by_hand.100: not a figure this function holds: an option's shares in one contract, as the record carries it (DEC-0274)

MK-CF-F-119.name: investmentIncomeAnnual
MK-CF-F-119.rule: Dividends, interest and coupons dated within the last year (on or after the same date a year ago), not reinvested, added — each counted as the money it moved into the account: when the record says which way the money went, its size, minus when it left (a reversed payment takes away what it had added); otherwise its amount with the sign it was stored with; a record whose amount is not on record (missing, blank or not a number) adds nothing.

MK-CF-F-120.name: pctBaseMonthly
MK-CF-F-120.rule: The twelve months of take-home (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) added ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-122.name: addDays
MK-CF-F-122.rule: The date that many whole calendar days later (earlier when negative), at the same clock time — counted on the calendar, so a day the clocks change on is still one day.

MK-CF-F-124.name: nextOccurrence
MK-CF-F-124.rule: With a year given: that month and day in that year. Otherwise that month and day (the 1st when no day) this year — or next year, when that month is already past this year. A day past the end of that month in that year is the month's last day (the last day of February in a year February is short). A date earlier this month stays this month (it is passed, so a list of what is coming leaves it out), as the month table counts that month's bill in this month.

MK-CF-F-125.name: amortise
MK-CF-F-125.rule: Never clears — infinite months, interest and last payment — when the payment does not exceed the first month's interest. Otherwise month by month until the balance is zero or less: interest = balance × yearly rate ÷ 12; the payment that month is the full payment, or, in the last month, only what is left plus that month's interest; balance = balance + interest − payment. Gives the months, the interest added up, and the last payment. A loan still owing after 12,000 months is reported as never clearing. Examples: $10,000 at 6% with $501 a month → 22 months, the last payment $40.31, interest $561.31; $100,000 at 6% with $501 a month → 1,247 months; $120,100 at 0% with $100 a month → 1,201 months, $0 interest.
