figures_checked_by_hand.$100: the third example's payment a month
figures_checked_by_hand.1,201: the third example by hand: $120,100 ÷ $100 = 1,201 months at 0%

MK-CF-F-126.name: futureValue
MK-CF-F-126.rule: 0 when the months or the monthly amount are zero or less. At a yearly rate of 0: monthly amount × months. Otherwise monthly amount × ((1 + yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power months − 1) ÷ (yearly rate ÷ 12). Example: $500 a month for 12 months at 0% → $6,000.

MK-CF-F-127.name: isRental
MK-CF-F-127.rule: True for a long-term rental or a short-term rental.

MK-CF-F-128.name: grossByMonth
MK-CF-F-128.rule: When the pay varies and a month-by-month table has been filled: the table, one row a month, in month order. Otherwise one row, called typical = the typical gross pay turned into a month (perMonth; 0 when an hourly wage has no hours a week).

MK-CF-F-130.name: enteredMonthlyRaw
MK-CF-F-130.rule: Hourly: base pay × hours a week × 52 ÷ 12 — no number when no hours a week are entered (a typed 0 is 0 hours). Otherwise base pay × the periods in a year ÷ 12, from the one pay-frequency table (payPeriodsAYear: weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, yearly 1) — no number for a frequency the table does not hold.

MK-CF-F-131.name: normPayee
MK-CF-F-131.rule: The payee note trimmed and lower-cased; empty when there is none.

MK-CF-F-132.name: map
MK-CF-F-132.rule: The list of accounts with one change applied to the account named, and the rest untouched.

MK-CF-F-133.name: cashOf
MK-CF-F-133.rule: The account's cash; 0 when none is recorded.

MK-CF-F-134.name: usesSleeve
MK-CF-F-134.rule: True for an investment account (not a cash or property account) whose balance is worked out from its holdings, or that records a cash figure of its own.

MK-CF-F-135.name: availableCash
MK-CF-F-135.rule: A bank account or a property (held as cash or property, or its class is cash): its balance. Any other — an investment account: its cash. NOTHING (not entered) when that figure was never entered or is not a number (2026-10-21, DEC-3279e: an investment account's cash never entered read $0, and a buy was refused on it); and NOTHING as well when the figure was opened by the app itself, from nothing on record, to keep the total right after money was recorded in or out — the account is marked so — except on a linked account, whose cash is the broker's own figure (2026-10-25).

figures_checked_by_hand.3279: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3279e that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.$0: what it read before 2026-10-21 — not a figure the code holds

MK-CF-F-136.name: bumpCash
MK-CF-F-136.rule: For an account that keeps its own cash (usesSleeve): the cash changes by the amount, and the balance changes by the same amount when it is a total the person typed — not for an account built from its holdings (its balance is rebuilt from cash and holdings) and not for a linked account (its total is the broker's) (2026-10-23). For an investment account with holdings that does not keep its own cash: both the cash and the balance change by the amount. For any other account: the balance changes by the amount. Where the cash had no figure before, the account is marked as its cash never entered (2026-10-25), so Available cash reads the figure opened here as not entered.

MK-CF-F-137.name: findPos
MK-CF-F-137.rule: The holding in the account with the record's holding id, or else with the record's ticker (the record's ticker read in capitals).

MK-CF-F-138.name: addLot
MK-CF-F-138.rule: Adds a purchase (shares, cost per share, the record's date) to the holding the record names; when the account has no such holding, a new holding with that one purchase, its ticker in capitals and the kind the record names (an option keeps the shares per contract its record states). When the record names no kind: the class its ticker gives through the one classifier an imported holding is classed by, stored under that class's tag — unless nothing but the classifier's last-resort default says what it is, so that every screen would read the holding as Unclassified (holdingClassOf); then no class is stored and the holding is marked asked: it is counted in no class and Net worth asks what it is (2026-10-25).

MK-CF-F-139.name: removeShares
MK-CF-F-139.rule: Takes the shares out of the holding's purchases oldest purchase date first (a purchase with no date on record goes last — purchaseDateOnRecord: missing, written another way, or a day the calendar does not have, such as 31 February), whatever order they are stored in. It stops at the first purchase whose share count is not on record (2026-10-25): that purchase and every later one are kept as they were, and the shares the sale could not be matched to are taken from nothing. A purchase left with nothing is dropped; a holding left with no purchases is removed. Unchanged when the account has no such holding.

figures_checked_by_hand.31: not a figure: 31 February, named as a day the calendar does not have

MK-CF-F-140.name: periodsAYear
MK-CF-F-140.rule: Pay periods in a year: hourly 2,080, weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, yearly 1. Read from the one pay-frequency table (payPeriodsAYear); any other frequency: no number.

MK-CF-F-141.name: perMonth
MK-CF-F-141.rule: Hourly: amount × hours a week × 52 ÷ 12 — and no number at all when no hours a week are entered (a typed 0 is 0 hours). Any other frequency: amount × pay periods in a year ÷ 12. A frequency the pay-frequency table does not hold: no number.

MK-CF-F-142.name: monthsOf
MK-CF-F-142.rule: The table's rows as (month, amount) pairs, sorted by month; a blank amount counts as 0; empty when there is no table.

MK-CF-F-143.name: annualisedGross
MK-CF-F-143.rule: This calendar year's twelve months of gross (grossCalendarYear), added: when the pay varies and its month-by-month table holds rows, a typed month counts as typed, $0 included, and a month with nothing typed counts as the typical gross turned into a month (perMonth) — the average month × 12, never a fourteen-month total; otherwise the typical gross turned into a month, twelve times. An hourly wage with no hours a week has no typical month, so only its typed months count.

MK-CF-F-144.name: takeHomeAsEntered
MK-CF-F-144.rule: In this order. (1) The pay varies and a month-by-month take-home table is filled: the average of its months; not calculated. (2) A take-home was typed — 0 included, only a blank box is not typed: that amount exactly as typed — it is asked for as a MONTH, whatever the pay frequency; not calculated. (3) Otherwise it is calculated, and marked so, as a PAID month's (the months of this calendar year the wage is paid, paidMonthsOf; 12 when none). With a household rate supplied: (yearly gross × (1 − rate) − monthly 401(k) × the months paid) ÷ the months paid. With none: (yearly gross − 401(k) for the months paid − federal income tax on the yearly gross less that 401(k), by the filing status given — single when none) ÷ the months paid. That federal tax has no state tax in it. Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24).

MK-CF-F-145.name: deductionsFromPay
MK-CF-F-145.rule: Nothing when the take-home is calculated, when an hourly wage's hours a week are not entered, or when the pay frequency is not one the table holds (freqNotRecognised). Otherwise yearly gross − monthly 401(k) × the months paid − monthly take-home × the months paid (paidMonthsOf): everything else that came out of pay in the year. Paid $60,000.30 over six months, $501.13 into a 401(k), $3,799.17 typed: $34,198.50.

figures_checked_by_hand.$60,000.30: the July starter's year of wages (the outside review's case)
figures_checked_by_hand.$3,799.17: the example's typed take-home a month

MK-CF-F-146.name: payFiguresAgree
MK-CF-F-146.rule: It passes with no check when the take-home is calculated. Otherwise every month of gross pay is read, in order — leaving out a month with no gross pay, unless a take-home above zero was typed for that very month in a take-home table: left = gross − monthly 401(k) − the take-home for that month (the month's own figure when a take-home table is filled, otherwise the typed take-home, which is a monthly figure at every pay frequency). When any month's left is below −$5: it FAILS, with a sentence naming the first such month in words ("in February 2026") and how much more the take-home is than there is — a warning in an earlier month never hides it. Otherwise, when a month's gross is above zero and left ÷ gross is above 60%: it passes WITH A WARNING that gives the first such month's share as a whole percent. Exactly $5 short still passes; exactly 60% does not warn. Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24).

MK-CF-F-148.name: inMonth
MK-CF-F-148.rule: True when the expense's own day — the day each record names, read where the person is (the app's one reader of a stored day: a calendar day is that day, a clock time with no zone its own day, an instant the day it was on the person's clock) — falls in the year-month asked for.

MK-CF-F-149.name: recurringDebtPayments
MK-CF-F-149.rule: One row for each debt whose payment is the same every month (an instalment loan): its name and its payment in this month — its required monthly payment from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off (a date not given sets no bound), nothing outside them. Rows of zero are dropped. Cards, lines of credit and debts due in full are not here.

MK-CF-F-150.name: debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses
MK-CF-F-150.rule: For each debt that is NOT an instalment loan, and whose purchases are not already imported from a linked card: the payments logged this month under the category Debt payment that debtPaymentsMatched gives to that debt (by the id the payment names, else by the one debt with its payee's name, capitals and outer spaces ignored), added up. A row only when that is above zero, named after the debt with the word payment. Then, for a payment logged under a name two or more debts share, when every debt of that name is counted as an expense: one row, named as it was logged with the word payment, marked two of your debts have that name — counted once.

MK-CF-F-151.name: actualSpending
MK-CF-F-151.rule: The month's logged expenses, leaving out the category Debt payment, newest day first (each by its own day, read where the person is) — all of them, or only those entered by hand, or only those imported. Shown = the first 5. Hidden = how many more. Total = all of them added. Hidden total = total − the 5 shown.

MK-CF-F-152.name: isRadarItem
MK-CF-F-152.rule: An instalment loan: not a radar item. A debt due in full: a lump-sum item. Any other debt (a card, a line of credit): a revolving item.

MK-CF-F-153.name: radar
MK-CF-F-153.rule: For each debt that is a radar item (isRadarItem): amount = what debtPaymentsMatched gives to that debt this month when that is above zero, otherwise what falls due on it this month — its required payment from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off, and for a debt due in full its whole balance in the month it is due; dropped when the amount is zero or less. It counts as an expense unless its purchases are already imported from a linked card. A payment under a name two or more radar debts share: one item, given to neither, marked two of your debts have that name — counted once. Then every big bill of $500 or more handed in, with its due date ("due Dec 15"), each counted as an expense — the production door (thisMonthInputs) hands only the month's own dated bills (the table's one reader of a month's dated bills), so a bill is on the radar in its own month only. Debts first, bills after. Each debt item says whether its amount is a payment logged against it this month (logged); a payment under a shared name is logged; a big bill says nothing of it.

figures_checked_by_hand.15: not a figure: the day in the sample words "due Dec 15"

MK-CF-F-155.name: cash
MK-CF-F-155.rule: The number unchanged, except that negative zero becomes zero.

MK-CF-F-156.name: plannedMonthFlow
MK-CF-F-156.rule: Rows, in this order. Inflow = the monthly take-home handed in, marked after tax and 401(k) when a budget is set and unmarked when none is (the approved drawing's frames A and B). A debt has a row only in a month a payment on it falls in: from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off (a date not given sets no bound), and for a debt due in full only the month it is due, while a balance is owed. One row for each instalment debt with such a payment above zero: minus that payment. Expenses = minus this month's planned expenses when a budget is set — set when handed in as set (the plan holds any expenses, even if none falls in this month, which then reads 0), otherwise when this month plans more than zero — marked your budget; when no budget is set, 0, marked not set. Then one row for each radar debt (a card, a line of credit, a debt due in full) with such a payment above zero: minus that payment — for a debt due in full its whole balance, named "<debt> — due in full". A debt whose payment was never entered (paymentNotEntered), in a month a payment on it falls in, keeps its place as a row at 0, marked payment not entered. Inflow total = the inflow row; outflow = minus the other rows, added up; surplus = every row added up. When no budget is set, the surplus and the outflow are not given (no number) and the refusal says: "You haven't set your budget. Until you do there is no planned surplus — we won't guess one." (2026-10-25: it handed out the take-home less the debts as a planned surplus.) Otherwise, when any debt's payment was never entered, the surplus and the outflow are not given (no number) and the refusal names the debt: "<debt>'s payment is not entered, so there is no planned surplus — we won't guess one."

MK-CF-F-157.name: debtPaymentsByDebt
MK-CF-F-157.rule: For each expense logged this month in the category Debt payment, the debt it was paid on (debtPaymentsMatched): the debt whose id the payment names; when it names none, the one debt whose name matches its payee (capitals and outer spaces ignored). A payee that two or more debts share gives the payment to none of them (actualMonthFlow lists it apart, once); a payment that matches no debt is left out. Its amount is added to that debt.

MK-CF-F-160.name: daysBetweenDates
MK-CF-F-160.rule: The number of whole calendar days from the first date's own calendar day to the second's: two times on the same day are no days apart, and a time late one evening is one day before a time early the next morning.

MK-CF-F-161.name: monthlyGrossOfSource
MK-CF-F-161.rule: Twelve calendar months; rent is taken after running costs. Monthly: the amount every month. Weekly: amount × 52 ÷ 12 every month. Every two weeks: amount × 26 ÷ 12 every month. Quarterly: the amount in March, June, September and December. Yearly: the amount in its month (December when none) — or split across its months by their shares. One-off: the amount in its month (January when none). The weeks and fortnights in a year are read from the one pay-frequency table (PAY_FREQUENCIES).

MK-CF-F-162.name: daysApart
MK-CF-F-162.rule: The gap between two dates in days, never negative.

MK-CF-F-163.name: monthKey
MK-CF-F-163.rule: A date written as year-month, for example 2026-08.

MK-CF-F-164.name: monthWindow
MK-CF-F-164.rule: A run of year-months: it starts that many months back from the given date and holds that many months.

MK-CF-F-165.name: salaryMonths
MK-CF-F-165.rule: The stored month table as year-month → amount. A month whose figure is blank (cleared, or never given) is left out, so it is not entered; a month typed 0 is kept as 0. A table kept as twelve plain figures is read as January to December of this year. Rows whose key is not a year-month are dropped. Empty when there is none.

MK-CF-F-166.name: hasMonthlySalaryTable
MK-CF-F-166.rule: True when salaryMonths holds any row.

MK-CF-F-167.name: salaryCalendarYear
MK-CF-F-167.rule: January to December of the year asked for: the table's figure where it has that month, otherwise the fallback.

MK-CF-F-168.name: salaryWindow
MK-CF-F-168.rule: For each year-month asked for: the table's figure where it has it, otherwise the fallback.

MK-CF-F-169.name: withSalaryMonth
MK-CF-F-169.rule: The table with that one month set to the amount; a blank amount takes that month out, so it is not entered and counts as the typical month; a typed 0 is kept as 0; every other month unchanged.

MK-CF-F-170.name: salaryYearFromCells
MK-CF-F-170.rule: The first twelve figures, as January to December of the year given.

MK-CF-F-171.name: earnerPay
MK-CF-F-171.rule: One earner's pay figures together: gross in a month = yearly gross ÷ 12; yearly gross (annualisedGross); the monthly 401(k); the take-home, whether it is calculated and why (takeHomeAsEntered); everything else taken out, for the year and for a PAID month (the year ÷ the months paid, 12 when none) — nothing when the take-home is calculated; the verdict (payFiguresAgree); the monthly gross rows; the typical gross turned into a month (perMonth, 0 when an hourly wage has no hours a week) — what a month not typed counts as; what the employer's match is worth in a month (wageMatchMonthly on the monthly 401(k), the match's choice and its figure); the months of this calendar year the wage is paid (paidMonthsOf); and whether an hourly wage's hours a week are not entered (hoursNotEntered). Everything else taken out as a share of the year's gross: what comes off the pay besides the 401(k) (deductionsFromPay) ÷ the year's gross; nothing when that is not known or the gross is not above zero. It says whether the pay frequency is one the table does not hold (freqNotRecognised); such a wage counts as entered.

MK-CF-F-172.name: hasWage
MK-CF-F-172.rule: True when a wage record has a base salary above zero, or a month table with any row.

MK-CF-F-173.name: earnerWages
MK-CF-F-173.rule: Who earns = both: the person's own wage record, plus the spouse's when it has a wage. Who earns = the spouse, and the spouse's record has a wage: the spouse's only. Otherwise the person's own only.

MK-CF-F-174.name: hasTwoEarners
MK-CF-F-174.rule: True when earnerWages gives more than one.

MK-CF-F-175.name: sumOverEarners
MK-CF-F-175.rule: The chosen figure worked for each earner and added; a missing figure counts 0. Its domain: its callers hand it at most two earners (earnerWages gives no more), each a row that is never missing, and a box left blank as 0 — the screen says to leave it blank when there is none.

MK-CF-F-176.name: sumMonthsOverEarners
MK-CF-F-176.rule: The chosen twelve-month row worked for each earner and added month by month.

MK-CF-F-177.name: wageGrossByMonth
MK-CF-F-177.rule: With a month table: this calendar year's twelve months from the table, any month not in it taking the typical monthly figure. With none: the typical monthly figure (enteredMonthlyRaw) in every month. An hourly wage with no hours a week has no typical monthly figure, so those months read $0.

MK-CF-F-178.name: wageMatchMonthly
MK-CF-F-178.rule: A match typed as a percent — or with neither choice made, which every screen shows as a percent: monthly 401(k) × that percent ÷ 100. Typed as dollars: that amount.

MK-CF-F-179.name: entryFromWage
MK-CF-F-179.rule: Turns a stored wage record into the pay entry: frequency (monthly when none); varies = the record says month-by-month, or its month table holds any row; typical gross = the base salary; the month table, only when it varies; the monthly 401(k); the typed take-home; hours a week; the employer match's choice and its figure.

MK-CF-F-180.name: enteredLandsAnnual
MK-CF-F-180.rule: Nothing unless EVERY earner typed a take-home (a typed 0 counts; a blank box does not). Otherwise each earner's typed take-home — a monthly figure, whatever the pay frequency — × the months that earner is paid this calendar year (wagePaidMonths), added. $3,799.17 over six paid months is $22,795.02.

figures_checked_by_hand.$3,799.17: the example's typed take-home a month

MK-CF-F-181.name: rateInForce
MK-CF-F-181.rule: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home (a typed 0 counts): rate = (yearly salary − the household's 401(k)s for the year, each earner's only in the months they are paid (householdK401ByMonth) − the yearly take-home (enteredLandsAnnual, the months paid), never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction. Its label names the rate to two decimals ("your rate, 24.00%", "your figures, …", "calculated, …"). Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24).

MK-CF-F-182.name: asPercent
MK-CF-F-182.rule: A rate × 100, always to two decimals (a trailing zero kept), followed by a percent sign. Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24).

MK-CF-F-183.name: paidOutByAccount
MK-CF-F-183.rule: Dividends, interest and coupons dated in the window — the twelve months ending today (on or after the same date last year, on or before today), or a window handed in, never after today — naming an account, added by account, reinvested ones included: each counted as the money it moved into the account: when the record says which way the money went, its size, minus when it left (a reversed payment takes away what it had added); otherwise its amount with the sign it was stored with; a reinvested record with no amount = shares × price. A record whose amount is not on record (missing, blank or not a number, and not reinvested with shares and price) adds nothing and is counted, by account, as not on record. A record that names no account is not counted.

MK-CF-F-184.name: incomeFromAccounts
MK-CF-F-184.rule: For each account whose income is taxed when paid (a pre-tax or Roth account is left out), the first that applies. (1) It paid more than zero over the trailing twelve months (paidOutByAccount, reinvested included): that amount, said as paid out over the trailing twelve months. (2) A bond or CD, by the one rule for its year of interest (yearlyInterestNow): no rate entered → $0, said so (owner A46), marked as assumed; a rate but no year's interest — a bond with a maturity date and no face value — → $0, said to be the face value not entered, marked as assumed; past its maturity date → $0, said to be matured on that date; a face value entered → the rate × the face value; otherwise (a CD bought from the bank typed by its balance, or a bond fund) → the rate × the balance. (3) Cash with a rate above zero: rate × balance. (4) Any other account with a balance above zero is named as not counted; foreign currency is skipped. Payouts in the window with no amount on record are named by account ('Not counted: 1 payment from Brokerage — amount not on record.'). Yearly income = the rows added. Then each bond or CD held inside an account (heldBondInterest) is a line of its own, named with its account: counted at face × rate; matured, $0 with 'matured — it pays no more interest'; with no rate or no face, $0 and assumed, saying it is not counted until it is entered (bondWhy).

MK-CF-F-185.name: needsTakeHomeConversion
MK-CF-F-185.rule: True when the pay was stored the old way — as take-home — and is above zero.

MK-CF-F-186.name: convertTakeHomeMode
MK-CF-F-186.rule: Unchanged unless it needs converting (needsTakeHomeConversion). Otherwise: yearly take-home = the stored figure × the periods in a year (periodsOf: from the one pay-frequency table, and for an hourly wage the hours a week × 52; unchanged when no hours are entered or the frequency is not in the table); yearly gross = when the person typed their own rate (a rate of 0% up to, not including, 100%): (the yearly take-home + 12 × their monthly 401(k)) ÷ (1 − that rate), so their rate and their take-home both hold; otherwise the income whose federal tax leaves exactly that take-home (grossFromNet) + 12 × their monthly 401(k), so gross − 401(k) − tax on (gross − 401(k)) = the take-home; the stored base pay becomes yearly gross ÷ periods; the typed take-home becomes the yearly take-home ÷ 12 — the month every screen now asks for; the mode becomes gross; and the profile is marked as having its gross worked back, which Your base pay says until a gross is typed. $4,211.17 a month with $511.43 into a 401(k): $61,084.93 a year.

figures_checked_by_hand.$4,211.17: the example's typed take-home a month (the outside review's MK-CF-F-186 case)
figures_checked_by_hand.$61,084.93: the example worked by hand: the take-home a year 50,534.04 is left by a taxable wage of 54,947.77 (single, 2026: 54,947.77 − 16,100 = 38,847.77 taxable; tax 1,240 + 12% × 26,447.77 = 4,413.73; 54,947.77 − 4,413.73 = 50,534.04), plus 12 × 511.43 = 6,137.16 of 401(k): 61,084.93; pinned in part16 and part_year_one_rule_2026_10_26

MK-CF-F-187.name: seniorDeductionFor
MK-CF-F-187.rule: 0 outside tax years 2025 to 2028; when filing separately; when nobody is 65 or over; or when the income is not known. Otherwise each person 65 or over (2 at most) gets $6,000 less 6% of the income above $75,000 (single, head of household) or $150,000 (married), never below 0 — the 6% comes off each person's $6,000, not off the two together; the answer is that amount × the number of those people.

MK-CF-F-188.name: householdPreTaxContributionsAnnual
MK-CF-F-188.rule: The household's 401(k)s for the year: each earner's monthly 401(k) in each month that earner is paid (householdK401ByMonth), added — never × 12 for someone paid part of the year. $1,000 a month, paid July to December: $6,000.

figures_checked_by_hand.$1,000: the example's 401(k) a month, not a figure the code holds

MK-CF-F-189.name: essentialsFromLoggedSpending
MK-CF-F-189.rule: Adds the logged expenses by calendar month, each by the day each record names, read where the person is (the app's one reader of a stored day: a calendar day is that day, a clock time with no zone its own day, an instant the day it was on the person's clock). Looks at the 12 months BEFORE the current month. When at least one of those months holds any expense: average = their total ÷ the number of months that hold any — empty months are not counted as zero — labelled N month average. When none does: if the current month holds any, that month's total so far, labelled as one month; otherwise nothing.

MK-CF-F-190.name: essentialsMonthly
MK-CF-F-190.rule: The logged average (essentialsFromLoggedSpending) when there is one; otherwise the typed figure when it is above zero, labelled you entered; otherwise nothing.

MK-CF-F-191.name: ym
MK-CF-F-191.rule: A date written as year-month, for example 2026-08.

MK-CF-F-192.name: inflowLabel
MK-CF-F-192.rule: The prefix, then the source words in brackets joined by a plus sign — each word once, in the order given. With no sources: income (take-home).

MK-CF-F-193.name: inflowSourceWord
MK-CF-F-193.rule: The source lower-cased and trimmed. Starting with salary, base salary or paycheck → income (take-home). Starting with rental, or exactly rent → rent. Starting with social security → Social Security. Anything else → itself, with a trailing bracketed part removed.

MK-CF-F-194.name: monthOutflow
MK-CF-F-194.rule: With a stored record for the month: its expenses + its debt paid. With none: what has been logged so far.

MK-CF-F-195.name: monthsLeftInYear
MK-CF-F-195.rule: 12 − the number of months already finished this year: 12 in January, 1 in December. The current month counts as left.

MK-CF-F-196.name: perMonthToFill
MK-CF-F-196.rule: Room left ÷ the months left in the year (monthsLeftInYear), rounded to the nearest $100.

MK-CF-F-197.name: ageAttainedInYear
MK-CF-F-197.rule: This calendar year − the birth year. Nothing when the birth year is missing or before 1900.

MK-CF-F-198.name: payrollTaxWithheld
MK-CF-F-198.rule: On a year's wages (below zero counts as 0): 6.2% of the wages up to $184,500, plus 1.45% of all the wages, plus 0.9% of the wages above $200,000.

MK-CF-F-206.name: householdK401ByMonth
MK-CF-F-206.rule: For each earner: their monthly 401(k) in every month they have gross pay, and 0 in months they do not. Added over the earners, month by month.

MK-CF-F-212.name: receivedInMonth
MK-CF-F-212.rule: The income records whose own day — the day each record names, read where the person is (the app's one reader of a stored day: a calendar day is that day, a clock time with no zone its own day, an instant the day it was on the person's clock) — falls in the year-month asked for, newest day first.

MK-CF-F-216.name: typed
MK-CF-F-216.rule: True when a figure was typed: it is present and is not blank once spaces are taken off. A typed 0 counts as typed.

figures_checked_by_hand.0: an example of a typed figure (a typed 0 counts as typed), not a figure the code holds

MK-CF-F-217.name: hasOldRentFigure
MK-CF-F-217.rule: True when the profile still holds any of the old single rent fields (rent coming in, costs going out, or the kind of let); false for no profile.

MK-CF-F-218.name: moveOldRentFigure
MK-CF-F-218.rule: Moves the old single rent figure into the rent list once, then removes the old fields. Unchanged when there is no old figure, or when the rent list is there but cannot be read. When the rent list already has entries, the list stands and the old fields are just removed. When neither old figure was typed, the old fields are just removed. Otherwise the list becomes one entry with no property — short let or long let as stored (long when not stated), the rent and the costs as typed, blank when not — which is not rent until its property is picked (DEC-4059d).

figures_checked_by_hand.4059: a decision number (DEC-4059d), not a figure

MK-CF-F-219.name: rentEntryMonthly
MK-CF-F-219.rule: What one rent entry comes to a month, as typed: its rent and its running costs, each read only when it is a plain number (digits with at most one decimal point, a leading dollar sign, thousands commas and spaces allowed). A rent not entered (blank, or text that is not a number such as "about 2k") is nothing, and so is the net: no net, and the entry counts nowhere (2026-10-25, tenet 3, DEC-3768c — it read $0 rent and gave −$600 a month). A running cost not entered is $0. Net = rent − running costs, which can be below zero; a typed 0 rent is $0. No entry: no rent, $0 costs, no net.

figures_checked_by_hand.3768: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3768c (2026-10-10) that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.2: not a figure: the typed text "about 2k" quoted as an example of an entry that is not a number
figures_checked_by_hand.3: not a figure: tenet 3 of DEC-3523, named
figures_checked_by_hand.$600: what the function read before 2026-10-25 for the example's $600 of running costs — not a figure the code holds

MK-CF-F-220.name: pastMonthFlow
MK-CF-F-220.rule: A past month as the Cash flow tab shows it. The income recorded = the amounts of the income records whose own day (the app's one reader of a stored day, read where the person is) falls in that month, added up (an amount that is not a number counts 0); the expenses logged = the amounts of the expenses logged in that month (inMonth), added up. What came in = the take-home the month's frozen record states, when there is a frozen record and it states one, else the income recorded. What went out = monthOutflow: with a frozen record, its expenses + its debt paid (each 0 when missing), else the expenses logged. Surplus = what came in − what went out.

MK-CF-F-221.name: spendByMonthByBucket
MK-CF-F-221.rule: The month's planned expenses in the budget's three groups (bills and fixed, once in a while, everyday), for each of the 12 calendar months, January first. The categories are in force once at least one has an amount above 0 (categoriesInForce; an empty list, or one whose categories are all 0, is no categories). With categories, each category with an amount above 0 counts; one entered as a percent counts at amount ÷ 100 × the monthly take-home it is a share of (pctBaseMonthly). A once-in-a-while category's yearly amount (its amount, or for a percent that share × 12) falls in the months it names, split equally among them, or spread equally over all 12 when it names none; any other category counts its monthly amount in every month, under bills and fixed when it is a fixed bill and under everyday otherwise. While no category is a monthly one (only once-in-a-while categories), every month also gets the typed bills and fixed total and the typed everyday total, each in its own group. Without categories, every month gets the budget's three monthly totals (spendBuckets). Then every month's everyday expenses gain whatever the monthly spending entered is above what the plan puts in every month: the monthly categories, the typed totals counted above, and a once-in-a-while category that names no month at its twelfth. A once-in-a-while category that names its months is never counted against the monthly spending entered, so it adds to its own months only.

MK-CF-F-222.name: tradeCash
MK-CF-F-222.rule: What a buy or a sale does to an account's cash and its total, given what the shares cost (below 0) or brought in at the price, and the fee the price does not carry. An account's total counts as typed unless it is built from its holdings or comes from a connection. An account that keeps its cash apart from its holdings (usesSleeve): its cash = its cash (0 when missing) + what the shares cost or brought in − the fee, and a typed total loses only the fee. Any other account: a typed total loses the fee when there is one; otherwise the account is unchanged. Where an account that keeps its cash apart had no cash figure before, the account is marked as its cash never entered (2026-10-25), so Available cash reads the figure opened here as not entered.

MK-CF-F-223.name: tradeMultiplierOf
MK-CF-F-223.rule: The shares per contract a buy or a sale trades: 1 for any other kind of record. Otherwise the holding it trades, found in its account as a trade finds it (findPos), read through contractMultiplier. When the account does not hold it yet (2026-10-25), the type and the shares per contract the record itself names, read through the same contractMultiplier: an option's stated shares per contract, or 100 when it states none; 1 for anything else and for a record that names no type. The trade sheet asks both for a ticker the account does not hold.

figures_checked_by_hand.100: not a figure this function holds: an option's shares in one contract when none is stated, read through contractMultiplier (his ruling: 100 unless the broker or the person states otherwise)

MK-CF-F-224.name: openingRecordsOf
MK-CF-F-224.rule: The purchase records of a holding already owned: one opening-holding record for each purchase handed in (by default the holding's own purchases), each with the purchase's date, the account, the holding's id, ticker and kind, the purchase's shares, its cost per share as the price when that is on record (no price otherwise), and the purchase's identifier when it has one, so the record follows that purchase, each made the one way every record is made (makeTransaction).

MK-CF-F-225.name: useCashflowModel
MK-CF-F-225.rule: The Cash flow model, from the store as it stands. The budget is the budget as counted (theBudgetCounted: a mortgage in Debts stands the budget's rent or mortgage line down), with the interest and dividends the accounts pay for the year counted as income (profileWithAccountIncome), when the person's answers are entered; the lens, working or retired, is read from it and from the one the person picked. The return the paycheck runs on is the Retirement cockpit's (paycheckReturn): the return set on the Plan, else the blended benchmark of the accounts set aside for retirement, else 6%, with the accounts' volatility or that rate's band — stated as words for the screen. With no birth year there is no paycheck year (no simulation is run) and the refusal says: "Your birth year is not entered, so there is no paycheck to work out — we won't guess one." Otherwise the paycheck year (buildPaycheckYear) is built from that budget, the accounts and the debts: the person's age, to the age the plan runs to (else the age + 5, and at least 92); that return and volatility; inflation as set (0.025 when not set); a fixed seed of 42 and 1000 paths. The dated grid is datedGridOf for the same budget, the debts and an adopted Roth conversion's tax and year.

MK-CF-F-226.name: datedGridOf
MK-CF-F-226.rule: The dated grid every Cash flow surface reads: the dated grid builder's, for the budget and the debts handed in, from the starting balance when one is handed in, with one bill more when an adopted Roth conversion's tax is above 0 — that tax, as a one-off bill in April of the year after the conversion's year (the year the Roth screen saves with the adoption; for an adoption saved without one, the year after today's), labelled as from the Plan. With a starting balance handed in (the Bill calendar's cash on hand), each month's running balance starts from it; without one, from $0.

MK-CF-F-227.name: thisMonthInputs
MK-CF-F-227.rule: This month's inputs, assembled once for the month's orchestrator (theMonth). The month = the one handed in, else today's on the person's own calendar. Take-home = the money in of the dated grid's cell for that month — its year and calendar month — (0 when the grid holds no such cell), with the sources inside it; every debt; planned expenses = that cell's bill items that are bills, added up (each 0 when missing); whether a budget is set = one was entered (budgetEntered: a typed total, $0 included, a total by group, or a category with an amount; a budget whose every line stood down for a debt counts as entered), said only when the person's answers are handed in; the planned expenses for that month the way the budget was entered (spendByMonthByCategory): each category given an amount, in the order entered — one that comes once a year only in its months — then what is left of the monthly total as Other; a budget typed only by group reads by group in its words (Bills & fixed, Once in a while, Everyday expenses); a row of 0 left out; the rows of each group add up to spendByMonthByBucket's; every expense logged, as the budget counts it (expensesAsCounted: one logged under a line that stood down for a debt is that debt's payment); the month's dated bills for the big-ticket radar (the table's one reader of a month's dated bills, on that cell), each with its due day ("Dec 15", or "in December" with none); and what the Plan promises to goals.

MK-CF-F-229.name: balanceGrownTo
MK-CF-F-229.rule: What a pot grows to: the starting balance × (1 + the yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power of the months, plus what the monthly contribution grows to at that rate over those months, each added at the end of its month (futureValue; at 0% the contributions themselves). Example: $10,000 and $500 a month for 12 months at 0% → $16,000.

MK-CF-F-230.name: taxedAfterPreTax
MK-CF-F-230.rule: What the year is taxed on once the 401(k)s are out: everything taxable over the year less the household's 401(k) contributions — each earner's own, for the months they are paid — added up; never below 0.

MK-CF-F-231.name: addedAfterRecord
MK-CF-F-231.rule: What a past month's record leaves out: the expenses logged in that month (inMonth) that were entered after the record was last saved; none when the record has no time it was saved. Their ids, and their amounts added up. Also: no saved time = a record is handed in and says no time it was saved; more than the record = then, the month's expenses logged (debt payments left out) less the record's expenses, never below 0 (0 otherwise) — which entries came later cannot be told, so none is named and the list says the record does not say when it was saved.

MK-CF-F-232.name: balanceByDay
MK-CF-F-232.rule: What is there by a day, read from the month table. Starting balance = the first month's End − its In + its Out. A day before the table's first month: the starting balance. A day after its last month: the last month's End. Otherwise: the End of the month before the day's month (the starting balance when the day is in the first month) + every item of the day's month dated on or before the day (an income with a day added; a bill that is not regular money taken away, on its day, the 1st when it has none) + the lower of 0 and the month's regular money (its In − its Out − the dated incomes + the dated bills). Regular money = the everyday expenses and the monthly debt payments on the bill side, and every income with no day.

MK-CF-F-233.name: earnerWageShares
MK-CF-F-233.rule: Each earner's wage by calendar month, with the share of it that earner's own typed take-home says comes out. A take-home and a 401(k) are each a PAID month's (a month whose wage is above $0), so that share = (the year's wages − their 401(k) a month × the months they are paid − their typed take-home a month × the months they are paid) ÷ the year's wages, kept between 0 and 1. A take-home typed as 0 is their answer; nothing (so the household's rate in force applies) only when the take-home box is blank or they have no wages. Paid $60,000.30 over six months, $501.13 into a 401(k), $3,799.17 typed: 57.00%, so each paid month lands $3,799.17.

figures_checked_by_hand.$60,000.30: the July starter's year of wages (the outside review's case), not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.$3,799.17: the example's typed take-home a month

MK-CF-F-234.name: wagesLandingByMonth
MK-CF-F-234.rule: The wages that land, month by month, January first: for each month, every earner's wage that month × (1 − the share their own take-home says comes out, else that month's household rate in force), added up (earnerWageShares), less the household's 401(k)s that month.

MK-CF-F-235.name: paysInMonth
MK-CF-F-235.rule: Whether a payment on a debt falls in one calendar month, written year-month: no for a month not written that way. A debt due in full: yes only in the month its payoff date falls in, while a balance above 0 is owed. Any other debt: yes from the month of its first payment (from any month when none is recorded) to the month of its payoff (to any month when none is recorded), both included.

MK-CF-F-236.name: paymentInMonth
MK-CF-F-236.rule: What a debt asks for in one calendar month: 0 in a month no payment of it falls in (paysInMonth); in a month one does, the whole balance for a debt due in full, and its required payment for any other.

MK-CF-F-243.name: grossCalendarYear
MK-CF-F-243.rule: One wage's gross for each month of this calendar year, January first: when the pay varies and its table holds rows, this year's months from the table (salaryCalendarYear), a month not typed taking the typical gross turned into a month (perMonth); otherwise that typical month twelve times. An hourly wage with no hours a week has no typical month (0). Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

MK-CF-F-244.name: paidMonthsOf
MK-CF-F-244.rule: The months of grossCalendarYear above $0 — the months of this calendar year the wage is paid. Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

MK-CF-F-245.name: hoursNotEntered
MK-CF-F-245.rule: True when the wage is paid by the hour, an hourly amount above 0 is typed, and no hours a week are entered (a blank box; a typed 0 is an answer). Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A) under DEC-0296.

figures_checked_by_hand.0296: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0296 that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-246.name: expensesAsCounted
MK-CF-F-246.rule: The expenses logged, as the budget counts them: an expense logged under a budget line that stood down for a debt (the lines theBudgetCounted lists as paid on debts — the Rent / Mortgage line beside the home's mortgage, or a line named as a debt), matched by the line's name with capitals and outer spaces ignored, is read as a Debt payment on that debt, with its id when the debt has one. Nothing changes when no line stood down. Worked: $2,300 logged as Rent / Mortgage beside a $2,400 mortgage on no property → the mortgage's payment; the $1,100 plan has $698 spent, $402 left.

figures_checked_by_hand.$2,300: the worked household: the Rent / Mortgage line logged (FIX-MONTH, 2026-10-25)
figures_checked_by_hand.$2,400: the worked household: the mortgage payment in Debts
figures_checked_by_hand.$1,100: the worked household: the plan with the Rent / Mortgage line stood down
figures_checked_by_hand.$698: the worked household: the expenses left once the $2,300 is the mortgage's payment

MK-CF-F-247.name: unplacedMortgageSentence
MK-CF-F-247.rule: Words only, no arithmetic: given the mortgage's name, the one sentence for a mortgage in Debts that is placed on no home beside a Rent / Mortgage budget line — "Your Rent / Mortgage budget line is not counted here: your mortgage, <its name>, is in Debts and is counted from there. Place it on your home in Net worth, so we know they are the same."

MK-CF-F-248.name: medicareFromOf
MK-CF-F-248.rule: When Medicare began, as the person answered it: "YYYY-MM" (its first month, 1–12) → that year and month; "before-YYYY" → before that year; anything else → not answered.

MK-CF-F-249.name: rentalsHeld
MK-CF-F-249.rule: The rentals the household has and what they clear a month. The count is the rentals that name their property (rentalList); with none, nothing (no row). Otherwise the month's figure is the year's rental net (rentalNetAnnual: each rental's rent less its running costs, a year) ÷ 12, signed, so a rental that loses money gives a figure below 0.

MK-CF-F-250.name: guaranteedReceivedNow
MK-CF-F-250.rule: The guaranteed income received now, a month. When the person's income sources are listed and do not include retirement income: 0. Otherwise the four guaranteed sources from outside their own savings (guaranteedOutsideStreams: Social Security, a pension, an annuity, another), each a month, added up, less the Social Security answered Not yet (socialSecurityNotYetMonthly). A withdrawal from a 401(k) or a required withdrawal is not among them.

MK-CF-F-251.name: debtPaymentsMatched
MK-CF-F-251.rule: Each expense logged in the month in the category Debt payment, given to exactly one place: the debt whose id the payment names; when it names none, the one debt whose name matches its payee (capitals and outer spaces ignored); a payee two or more debts share — to none of them, added up per name with the debts that share it; no debt matching — unmatched. Worked: debts A "Loan" and B " loan ", $250 logged to "Loan" with no id → none credited, shared $250 under "Loan".

figures_checked_by_hand.$250: the example's payment, not a figure the code holds

MK-CF-F-252.name: payoffRefusal
MK-CF-F-252.rule: The one sentence for a payoff plan that cannot be worked out: each debt whose payment, rate or both were never entered, named — first each debt with both missing ("<debt>'s payment and rate"), then the debts with only the payment missing ("<debt>'s payment", or "<A> and <B> payments"), then the debts with only the rate missing ("<debt>'s rate", or "<A> and <B> rates"), joined by "and" — then "is not entered" for one debt with one thing missing and "are not entered" otherwise, and ", so there is no payoff date — we won't guess one."

MK-CF-F-253.name: startingCashOnRecord
MK-CF-F-253.rule: The Bill calendar's starting cash. When any account holds a cash balance on record — an uninvested cash figure entered on it, or a cash account whose balance is entered as a number, a balance of 0 included — the cash Net worth counts over all the accounts (cashTotal). When none does: nothing (no figure), so nothing is projected.

MK-CF-F-254.name: categoriesInForce
MK-CF-F-254.rule: The budget's categories, when they count: the category list if at least one category has an amount above 0; otherwise none (an empty list, or one whose categories are all 0, is no categories, and the totals typed by group stand). spendBuckets, spendByMonthByBucket and monthlyEssentials read it.

MK-CF-F-255.name: spendByMonthByCategory
MK-CF-F-255.rule: The month's planned expenses as the budget was entered, for each of the twelve calendar months, January first. With no category that has both a name and an amount above 0, each month lists the three groups (fixed, once a year, everyday) at their amounts from spendByMonthByBucket, a group at 0 left out. Otherwise each such category is a row: a monthly category (fixed or everyday) its amount in every month — a category typed as a percent is that percent ÷ 100 of the monthly figure the budget's percents are worked on (pctBaseMonthly); a once-a-year category its yearly amount (a percent: ÷ 100 × that monthly figure × 12) split evenly over the months it falls in, or a twelfth in every month when no month is picked. Then, group by group, what the categories leave of that month's group total (spendByMonthByBucket) is one more row, called Other when any monthly category was given and otherwise the group's own name. A row of 0 is left out, so each month's rows add up, group by group, to spendByMonthByBucket.

MK-CF-F-256.name: budgetEditorBuckets
MK-CF-F-256.rule: The budget editor's three buckets (fixed, once a year, everyday) for the month of the date given, with the rows under each. Each bucket's plan and what was spent in it are budgetVsActual's for that month (its plan is that month's own). When the budget was entered by category (any category with a name and an amount above 0), each row spendByMonthByCategory lists for the month is a row with that plan and what was spent in that category (0 when nothing), placed in the bucket its spending is counted in; every other category with spending is a row with a plan of 0. A budget typed only by group lists what was spent by category, each with a plan of 0. The rows of a bucket are sorted by what was spent, largest first, and each row's printed spend is its share of the rows' spend in whole dollars, so the printed rows add up to their printed total.

MK-CF-F-257.name: budgetEntered
MK-CF-F-257.rule: Whether a budget was entered at all: yes when a monthly total is typed (a $0 included), a total is typed by group (bills and fixed, once in a while, everyday), or a category has an amount above 0 (categoriesInForce); no profile, or none of these, is no budget.

MK-CF-F-258.name: equityVests
MK-CF-F-258.rule: Every vesting row with a value above zero (equityRowValue), with what its typed date names — four digits are the year; a dash and a month from 1 to 12 after them are the month: its year and month; its year alone, said "vest month not entered"; or nothing, said "vest date not entered".

MK-CF-F-259.name: rateNotEntered
MK-CF-F-259.rule: Whether a debt's interest rate was never entered: no rate, an empty one, or one that is not a number. A typed 0 is an entered 0%.

figures_checked_by_hand.0: not a figure: a typed 0 named as an answer, not as a number the function uses
figures_checked_by_hand.0%: not a figure: a typed 0% named as an answer

MK-CF-F-260.name: householdEmployerMatchAnnual
MK-CF-F-260.rule: The household's employer match for the year: each earner's match a month (wageMatchMonthly) × the months that earner's wage is paid this calendar year (payrollMonths — 12 when no wage is on record), added. $1,000/month into a 401(k) paid July to December with a 50% match: $3,000. Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

figures_checked_by_hand.$1,000: the worked example: the 401(k) typed a month
figures_checked_by_hand.50%: the worked example: the match typed

MK-CF-F-261.name: ownK401Annual
MK-CF-F-261.rule: One earner's own 401(k) for the year: their monthly 401(k) × payrollMonths — what counts against that person's elective limit. $1,000/month paid July to December: $6,000. Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

figures_checked_by_hand.$1,000: the worked example: the 401(k) typed a month

MK-CF-F-262.name: payrollMonths
MK-CF-F-262.rule: The months a payroll amount (a 401(k), an employer's match) comes out of one wage this year: the months the wage is paid (wagePaidMonths); 12 when no wage is on record (a base pay above zero or a month table). Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

MK-CF-F-263.name: incomeIsTaxedWhenPaid
MK-CF-F-263.rule: Whether an account's interest and dividends are taxed in the year they are paid: yes for every account except one whose tax treatment (taxTreatmentOf) is tax-deferred — an IRA, a 401(k), an HSA — or tax-free — a Roth IRA, a 529. An account with no tax type stated counts as taxed.

MK-CF-F-264.name: interestAndDividendsForYear
MK-CF-F-264.rule: The interest and dividends figure for one calendar year, from the first of four that answers. (1) Records: the payouts recorded in that year, from 1 January to 31 December and never past today, reinvested ones counted and a reversal cancelling (paidOutByAccount), added over the accounts whose income is taxed when it is paid (incomeIsTaxedWhenPaid), one line an account, said "from your accounts' records for <year>". (2) Entered: the yearly figure typed on Interest & dividends, a typed 0 included, said "you entered". (3) Calculated: each account's rate on its balance and each bond's coupon for a year (incomeFromAccounts, with no records), the lines above 0 that are not assumed added up, marked approximate, said "calculated from your accounts — " with each line's working. (4) Not entered: no figure. A payout whose amount is not on record is counted and named on every branch, never added as 0. Nothing is rounded.

MK-CF-F-265.name: vestsOf
MK-CF-F-265.rule: The one reader of the vests, loaded when called: every vest with a value, its year and month or what is missing — equityVests in src/domain/cashflow.

MK-CF-F-266.name: vestsAreCash
MK-CF-F-266.rule: True only when the person answered yes to "Do you sell the shares when they vest?"; otherwise a vest is shares — taxed in its year, in no month's money.

MK-CF-F-267.name: vestsNotEntered
MK-CF-F-267.rule: How many vests have no date (vest date not entered) and how many a year and no month (vest month not entered), from equityVests.

MK-CF-F-268.name: unemploymentMonthly
MK-CF-F-268.rule: The part of a month's benefits that is unemployment pay: with unemployment the only kind chosen, the whole monthly amount; beside another kind, the typed unemploymentMonthly (never more than the total, never below 0), or the whole amount until it is typed; 0 when unemployment is not chosen.

MK-CF-F-269.name: landsOnceInYear
MK-CF-F-269.rule: The amounts of one kind (signing bonus, or one-time other payment) that count in one calendar year (landsOnce counts), added up; $0 for one that does not count.

MK-CF-F-270.name: landsOnce
MK-CF-F-270.rule: Money that lands once, with its year and month or what is missing, and whether it counts in its year. A signing bonus above 0, read from its date: no date — "date not entered", not counted; a year with no month — "month not entered", counted in that year; a year and a month — counted, in that month; it is always taxed. A one-time other payment above 0 (an other income whose rhythm is one time), read from the year and the month asked for it: counted only when both are given; otherwise "year not entered", or "month not entered" when only the year is given; taxed unless the person said it is not.

MK-CF-F-271.name: socialSecurityNotYetMonthly
MK-CF-F-271.rule: The Social Security amount a month (ri_ss ÷ its rhythm) when it is answered Not yet (ri_ss_receiving no); otherwise 0.

MK-CF-F-272.name: socialSecurityReceivedMonthly
MK-CF-F-272.rule: The Social Security received now, a month: 0 when the chosen income sources leave out retirement income; otherwise ri_ss ÷ its rhythm less the part answered Not yet.

MK-CF-F-273.name: socialSecurityTaxedAnnual
MK-CF-F-273.rule: IRS Publication 915 Worksheet 1: provisional = other income + half the benefits; at or under the first base (25,000 single or head of household, 32,000 jointly, 0 separately) none is taxed; over it, half of the smaller of the excess and the gap to the second base (34,000 / 44,000 / 0), capped at half the benefits, + 85% of anything over the second base; never more than 85% of the benefits.

figures_checked_by_hand.915: not a figure: IRS Publication 915, the source named

MK-CF-F-274.name: taxedSourcesAnnual
MK-CF-F-274.rule: One row per source the year is taxed on, signed, a row of 0 left out (Social Security's row kept whenever any is received): each earner's wages (wageGrossByMonth), tips, self-employment, rent net, interest and dividends (interestAndDividendsForYear on the profile), the bonus, a signing bonus or one-time payment of this year (landsOnce), this year's stock vesting (rsuAnnual), other taxed income, unemployment pay, retirement income received now less Social Security, and Social Security's taxed part (socialSecurityTaxedAnnual on the other rows less the year's 401(k)s, by filing status).

MK-CF-F-275.name: profileWithAccountIncome
MK-CF-F-275.rule: The profile with its yearly interest-and-dividends answer replaced by interestAndDividendsForYear's figure for this year, with that figure's basis and whether it is approximate beside it, when the figure comes from the records or is calculated from the accounts; the profile unchanged when the figure is the one typed or nothing is known (and nothing when there is no profile).

MK-CF-F-276.name: retirementIncomeTaxedMonthly
MK-CF-F-276.rule: Retirement income received now, a month (currentRetirementIncomeMonthly), and its taxed part: the received amount less the Social Security received plus Social Security's taxed part for the year ÷ 12.

MK-CF-F-277.name: wagePaidMonths
MK-CF-F-277.rule: How many months of this calendar year one wage is paid in: the months of wageGrossByMonth above $0. Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A) for the part-year rule: a take-home and a 401(k) are each a paid month's.

MK-CF-F-278.name: ltcgTaxOnGain
MK-CF-F-278.rule: The federal tax on a long-term capital gain of any size, stacked on top of the year's ordinary income (the IRS Schedule D tax worksheet). A gain of 0 or less costs 0. Taxable income = taxableIncomeFor(the ordinary income, never below 0, plus the gain; the filing status; how many are 65 or over). The gain taxed = the smaller of the gain and that taxable income; if that is 0 or less the tax is 0. The ordinary part = taxable income less the gain taxed. With the two tops for the filing status (LTCG: single $49,450 and $545,500; married filing jointly $98,900 and $613,700; married filing separately $49,450 and $306,850; head of household $66,200 and $579,600): the part at 0% = the smaller of taxable income and the first top, less the ordinary part, never below 0; the part at 15% = the smaller of (the gain taxed less the 0% part) and (the second top less the larger of the ordinary part and the first top, never below 0); the part at 20% = the rest of the gain taxed. The answer = 15% of the 15% part + 20% of the 20% part, at full precision.

MK-CF-F-279.name: paycheckReturn
MK-CF-F-279.rule: The return and volatility the paycheck simulation runs on — the Retirement cockpit's own, the inputs Will my money last runs on. The blended benchmark of the accounts set aside for retirement (rentals included), 6% when nothing is; with the Plan's basis set to the scenario, the return set there (else that benchmark); with the twelve-month basis, the accounts' own return over the last twelve months (else that benchmark). Volatility: the accounts' own blended volatility, else the rate × 1.7 kept between 5% and 20%. It also says where the rate came from, in words: the rate to two decimals with "/year — " (written by its declaration, MK-CF-M-082), then your scenario return, your 12-month return, the blended benchmark, or the typical return, with nothing set aside for retirement. Example: nothing set aside, nothing set → 6.00%/year, volatility 10.2%, "the typical return, with nothing set aside for retirement".

MK-CF-F-280.name: useIncomeProfile
MK-CF-F-280.rule: The profile every income and tax figure reads: the stored answers (or the answers being edited) with the year's interest and dividends from the accounts handed in — profileWithAccountIncome on the store's accounts and records. Read only; never saved. Calculates nothing itself. Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

MK-CF-F-281.name: incomeProfileNow
MK-CF-F-281.rule: The same as useIncomeProfile, outside a component: profileWithAccountIncome on the store's accounts and records as they are when it is called. Calculates nothing itself. Written 2026-10-26 (FIX-INCOME-A).

MK-CF-F-282.name: growthUsed
MK-CF-F-282.rule: The growth a pre-tax balance is projected at, and the words that say it, never below 0%. A return of 0 or more (paycheckReturn's) is used as it is, with paycheckReturn's own words. A return below 0 is used as 0, and the words are "0.00%/year — " and then "your last 12 months were −X" when the return is the accounts' own over the last twelve months, "your scenario return is −X" when it is the one set on the Plan, or "the return is −X" otherwise — the return lost written to two decimals with "/year" — then "; we don't project a loss forward".

MK-CF-F-284.name: federalBracketForComparison
MK-CF-F-284.rule: The federal tax bracket the mortgage comparison runs on: the one the Income summary shows as "Federal tax bracket" (incomeSummary), when an income is entered; otherwise none, and the comparison runs before tax.

MK-CF-O-001.name: basePay
MK-CF-O-001.rule: Runs earnerPay for each earner with the household's filing status (single when none), the number of people 65 or over, and the household's rate in force (rateInForce). Yearly gross = the earners' yearly gross added up. Take-home = their monthly take-homes added up — each a PAID month's (a month the earner's wage is above $0). Tax band = the federal band on ALL the earners' wages together less each earner's own 401(k) for the months they are paid (a 401(k) is not taxed), plus everything else the profile is taxed on (taxableAnnual less the wages: rent kept, a bonus, interest and dividends) — the Income summary's bracket — by filing status; the band on the first earner's wage less their own 401(k) for the months paid is also worked out, and when there are two or more earners, the two bands differ, and every earner typed a take-home, a note says so. When there are two or more entered earners and every one typed a take-home, a sentence also says the rate in force is their own figures. When nobody typed a take-home the card states its own sum in words: gross in a month − tax − 401(k)s = take-home. Tax in a month = each earner's yearly gross × the rate in force ÷ the months that earner is paid (12 when none), added; the card's gross in a month is each earner's yearly gross ÷ the months paid, added. An earner is entered when their yearly gross is above zero, they typed a take-home, or they are paid by the hour with no hours a week entered; the names of those hourly earners are given, and the household card shows no total while any is listed; nothing entered = no earner entered. Mode, and every sentence that says whose figure is whose, are worked over the entered earners (all the earners when none is): entered when every one typed a take-home; calculated when none did; mixed otherwise — then one line per entered earner, their take-home with ≈ only when it is the app's estimate. A take-home is the app's estimate when it was calculated AND the rate in force is the calculated one (one worked from a typed rate is theirs); the household take-home is marked as an estimate when any entered earner's is. When the rate in force is the calculated one, short-by = Social Security and Medicare on each earner's yearly gross (payrollTaxWithheld) ÷ the months that earner is paid (12 when none), added up; nothing otherwise. Every figure agrees only when every earner's check passes (payFiguresAgree). Monthly 401(k) = added up over the earners. Other taken in a month = each entered earner's everything-else added up; nothing when any entered earner's take-home is calculated. The sentence under the take-home, when every earner typed one: what they entered, nothing calculated — or, when the gross was worked back from a take-home entered the old way, that the take-home is what they entered and the gross was worked back from it. What the band is read on = everything taxable entered (taxableAnnual on the profile); what is still to add = rent unless rent kept is above zero (rentalNetAnnual), a bonus unless one is entered, a spouse's wage unless two earners are entered or the person said there is no spouse — in that order. With a state income tax rate entered (stateRateOf), the tax carries the words "the N.NN% state rate you entered", the rate written to two decimals; none otherwise. Whether the band is read on more than the wages (anything else taxed is above zero) is also given. It names the earners whose pay frequency the table does not hold (freqNotRecognised), and such an earner counts as entered. Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24). While any earner's wage cannot be read, an earner whose take-home is calculated is marked as waiting, so no household figure is built half-read.

MK-CF-O-002.name: expenses
MK-CF-O-002.rule: Recurring debt rows (recurringDebtPayments) and their total. Planned rows by category, as handed in, and their total. Actual expenses for the month — all, entered by hand, and imported (actualSpending). The debt payments that count as expenses (debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses). Actual total = the actual expenses total + those debt payments. And the radar (radar).

MK-CF-O-003.name: thisMonth
MK-CF-O-003.rule: The planned block (plannedMonthFlow) and the actual block (actualMonthFlow), side by side.

MK-CF-O-004.name: incomeSummary
MK-CF-O-004.rule: TAKE-HOME rows — everything that arrives in a usual month; after tax means × (1 − the rate in force): each earner's take-home above zero (basePay); tips after tax when every month has pay; self-employment after tax; rent after running costs, signed (a loss is a row) — whole when the rate is the person's own, after tax when calculated; interest and dividends paid to the bank, or the calculated tax on reinvested ones; retirement income received now less the tax on its taxed part (Social Security per IRS Publication 915); other income; the untaxed benefits and unemployment pay after tax; support; scholarships. The usual month is the rows added. WHAT IT IS TAXED ON: one row for each of taxedSourcesAnnual's sources, signed, adding to = Gross /year (taxableAnnual); − the year's 401(k)s = what it is taxed on (taxedAfterPreTax). With the accounts handed in, interest and dividends are interestAndDividendsForYear's figure (≈ when calculated). Ready when a salary, a gross or any take-home row exists. Says the year's vest kept as shares and each thing counted nowhere yet (2026-10-25). Hands out YOUR SOURCES too (incomeSources of the profile as typed), the rows the Income tab prints. An earner whose pay frequency the table does not hold is not counted, and the sentence 'Pay frequency not recognised — open Base pay to choose one.' says so; the pay line reads '· pay frequency not recognised'. A wage entered that cannot be read — its frequency not in the table, or hourly with no hours — is named in one refusal sentence (from wageRefusalOf's two sentences), and the summary counts as ready so the refusal shows. It names the rows that wait on an unread wage (each earner's pay and gross), and rent typed with no property named — counted nowhere — is said, with its amount a month after costs.

figures_checked_by_hand.915: not a figure: IRS Publication 915, the source named

MK-CF-O-005.name: theContributionRoom
MK-CF-O-005.rule: Age = the calendar year of the day it is read on − birth year; nothing with no birth year, and then every limit is the base one and the answer says so (it is marked base limits only). 401(k): limit by age (annual401kLimit); used = monthly 401(k) × 12, never cut to the limit; room = limit − used, never below 0; excess = used − limit, never below 0 (k401Headroom). IRA: limit by age (annualIraLimit); used = the one IRA amount a month, Traditional and Roth together, × 12 — until that is typed, the Roth amount sign-up stored; room and excess the same way. HSA: the self-only or the family limit by age (annualHsaLimit), as the cover chosen — self-only when none is chosen, and the cover chosen is handed back; enrolled in Medicare with its first month in this year → that limit × the months before it ÷ 12; enrolled from before this year, or with no month given → 0; a start in a later year → the whole year; used = monthly HSA × 12; room and excess the same way. Also: the months of HSA that count, and the whole-year HSA limit before Medicare, for the cover chosen. Catch-up flags: 401(k) and IRA at 50 or over; HSA at 55 or over. Months left = 12 − the months already finished this year (January 12, December 1). Per month to fill the 401(k) = room ÷ months left, to the nearest $100. Examples: born 1966, $3,333.33 a month → used $39,999.96, excess $4,249.96; no birth year, $1,000 a month → limit $24,500 (the base one), room $12,500; born 1960, Medicare from July 2026 → HSA $5,400 × 6 ÷ 12 = $2,700.

MK-CF-O-006.name: theCreditLine
MK-CF-O-006.rule: With no limit, or a limit of zero or less: no share used and no status. Otherwise share used = balance ÷ limit, at full precision (rounded only where it is shown); status good at 30% or under, caution above 30% up to 50%, high above 50%.

MK-CF-O-007.name: theTaxOrganizer
MK-CF-O-007.rule: The year's interest and dividends (interestAndDividendsForYear), for the tax year named (this year when none is given): the records of that calendar year — 1 January to 31 December, never after today — from accounts whose income is taxed when paid (not a pre-tax or Roth account), reinvested payouts counted, kept to the cent; none on record → the yearly figure the person entered (a typed $0 included); nothing entered → calculated from the accounts' own rates (each bond's coupon, each cash account's rate on its balance), marked ≈ with its working; none → not entered (no line). The profile handed to the organiser carries that same figure as its interest and dividends (profileWithAccountIncome, read as of today for this year and as of 31 December for an earlier year), so the organiser's rate counts it. That figure with its basis, the count of payouts with no amount on record, the profile, the accounts, the debts and the year are handed to the tax organiser, whose answer is returned unchanged. With no income line at all the organiser gives Gross income $0 and no walk, no taxable income and no rate (the refusal 'Nothing entered yet.').

MK-CF-O-008.name: whatsComing
MK-CF-O-008.rule: The month table: the one handed in (the table the screen draws), or else the dated grid builder's for the budget, the debts and the starting balance handed in (from $0 when none), from today. The upcoming bills (upcomingBills) read from that table, with today and the horizon given (365 days when none), soonest first; and the first of them as the next one — nothing when there are none. With no starting balance handed in (none, or not a number): each bill keeps its name, amount and dates, but what is there by its need-by day and how much short are nothing, and the answer says "No balance to start from — nothing is projected." when there is a bill. A starting balance of $0 handed in is projected from $0.

MK-CF-O-010.name: theMonth
MK-CF-O-010.rule: The planned and actual blocks (thisMonth); the Expenses tab (expenses); committed = the monthly amounts of the goals added up; free = planned surplus − committed — no number when there is no planned surplus (no budget, or a payment never entered).

MK-CF-O-016.name: incomeSources
MK-CF-O-016.rule: One row for each entered source, in its own period, in the Income tab's drawn words and order (the tab prints these rows through incomeSummary): every earner with a base salary or a month table (steady, with its pay period, or varies); self-employment (yearly when entered 'annual', otherwise monthly); the bonus with its month; other income (a one-time payment says when it lands, or 'month not entered' / 'year not entered'); each rental the household has, whatever it nets (rentalsHeld); Equity comp — the stock that vests this year (rsuAnnual), 'RSU grants' or 'option grants', '· vest date not entered' when no grant has a date; guaranteed income received now (guaranteedReceivedNow); benefits, a month ('every month' or the months of the year); child support or alimony, a month; interest and dividends, a year, reinvested or paid to the bank (2026-10-25). Each wage source says how often it is paid by the one pay-frequency table, and when it cannot be read says why (pay frequency not recognised, or hours a week not entered); an hourly wage is marked as hourly.

MK-CF-O-017.name: futurePaycheck
MK-CF-O-017.rule: Nothing when the age is unknown; when the person is at or past the retirement age (the one retirement age: the age set on the Plan, else the age typed in sign-up, else today's age for someone retired, else the app's own assumed age — and it says when the age is the app's own); when the savings are zero or less; or when the projection gives nothing. Otherwise: the retirement projection is run to the retirement age — on the Plan's inputs, the accounts' records handed in for the year's interest and dividends — and gives the projected savings at that age; the monthly draw those savings can support comes from buildPaycheckYear (solveSafeDraw); monthly paycheck = guaranteed income (Social Security, pension, annuity, other — guaranteedOutsideStreams) + that draw, at full precision — nothing is rounded here; the screen rounds once, to whole dollars. Example: $2,731.17 guaranteed + a $1,730 draw = $4,461.17 (shown $4,461). Also hands back the yearly return and inflation the projection ran on.

MK-CF-O-018.name: theDebts
MK-CF-O-018.rule: Counts only debts with a balance above zero. Total = their balances added. Minimum in a month = each debt's minimum payment added, a debt due in full counting 0. Payments in a month = each debt's required payment added (requiredPayment: the payment set, never less than its minimum); a payment never entered adds 0. Interest in a month = balance × yearly rate ÷ 12, added over the debts; no number when any debt's rate was never entered (rateNotEntered), and then the interest refusal names it: "<debt>'s rate is not entered, so there is no interest figure — we won't guess one." Each debt's interest in a month, by its id, the same way — nothing for a debt whose rate was never entered. Plan in a month = the payments + the extra (his DEC-0641, what actually leaves; it was the minimums + the extra). Progress: paid down = the debt at the start of the year − the total now; share = paid down ÷ the start-of-year debt; given only when the start-of-year debt and the paid-down amount are both above zero. The payoff plan is payoffPlan, with the extra and the method chosen (highest rate first when none is); when payoffPlan names a debt whose payment or rate was never entered, there is no plan (and the plan in a month is no number), and the refusal (payoffRefusal) names each: "<debt>'s payment is not entered, so there is no payoff date — we won't guess one." When the accounts are handed in, which property each mortgage is on and which mortgages are on none (mortgagesByProperty, Net worth's own reading), with the sentence for a mortgage on none; otherwise nothing.

figures_checked_by_hand.0641: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0641 that this rule follows

MK-CF-O-019.name: theIncomeManager
MK-CF-O-019.rule: Takes the ten sources in the picker's order — a job, self-employment, rent, interest and dividends, retirement income, benefits, support, scholarships, student loans, something else — gives each one figure, and splits them into entered and not entered: a figure above zero, or for rent any rental the household has (a loss shown signed), and for a job any wage including an hourly one with no hours ("· hours a week not entered"). A job: the household's monthly take-home (basePay), marked calculated when any part is. Retirement income says "· Social Security not received yet" when answered Not yet; something else "· year not entered" for a one-time payment with no year. Bonus and stock: the bonus + this year's vest, read with the job, or on its own when there is no job (2026-10-25). An earner whose pay frequency the table does not hold is shown with '· pay frequency not recognised' in place of a figure. Such a wage's line prints no figure: it is refused, and named without 'take-home'.

MK-CF-O-020.name: theBudgetCounted
MK-CF-O-020.rule: Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "Once user enters mortgage or any debt - the app deduct it directly to calculate surplus, emergency fund, and any other place instead of leaving it for user to add it to planned expenses." The home = the property read as HOME (propertyUses, handed the profile's rent entries — none recorded is read as none, not as unknown). Its mortgage = the mortgage matched to that property (mortgagesByProperty). When the home has a mortgage in Debts AND the budget's Rent / Mortgage line holds an amount: that line is counted as nothing, and the sentence says the line is not counted and names the mortgage. When no home has a mortgage but a mortgage in Debts is on no property, beside a Rent / Mortgage line with an amount, that mortgage is taken as the home's (the lead's ruling, 2026-10-25, on DEC-1923 / DEC-2440): the line is counted as nothing and the sentence (unplacedMortgageSentence) asks the person to place it on their home. Any other line that is a debt in Debts is counted as nothing too: the budget's own Debt payment line while Debts holds any debt, and a line named as a debt is (its name, or its name with the word payment; capitals and outer spaces ignored), each with its sentence. The one typed monthly total (when there is one) is lowered by every amount stood down, never below zero. What is logged under a line that stood down is that debt's payment (listed as paid on debts, which expensesAsCounted reads), and the budget is marked as entered. Otherwise — a renter, a home with no mortgage, a mortgage on another property, or no amount on the line — the budget is counted exactly as typed. It also names the home's mortgage when there is one. What the person typed is never changed; this is the budget as it is counted.
