MK-NW-F-001.name: isAlternative
MK-NW-F-001.rule: True when the account's class (assetClassOf) is Alternatives.

MK-NW-F-002.name: alternativesSummary
MK-NW-F-002.rule: Over every account that holds alternatives, read from its class split (altPartsOf): count = how many such accounts; total = their alternatives parts added up, every part included — the same dollars as the Alternatives line; the parts no priced holding or option explains (asset type not classified) are added up on their own as the money not classified. Blended rate = each classified part × the yearly rate for its kind (the person's own rate for that kind first, else the benchmark), added up, ÷ the classified parts' total — no figure when that total is 0; growth in a year = the classified parts' total × blended rate, and no figure when it is 0 ($0 would read as a forecast). The rate and the growth leave the not-classified money out (DEC-4036h, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-003.name: valueFreshness
MK-NW-F-003.rule: No answer for an account whose balance is built from its holdings, or one with no value date. Otherwise months old = the whole months that have fully passed since the value date: (years apart × 12 + calendar months apart), less 1 when today's day of the month is before the day the value was set — unless today is the last day of its month, which completes the month for a value set on a day that month does not have (a value set on the last day of January is one month old on the last day of February). A value dated by its month alone counts from the 1st, and its date is given as the 1st of that month. Never below zero. Stale when 6 or more.

MK-NW-F-004.name: portfolioActualReturn
MK-NW-F-004.rule: What the money set aside for retirement returned over the last twelve months — not the return of everything invested. Over accounts that are not property, that have a return for the last twelve months reported by the person (a reported 0 counts; one not reported is left out, never read as 0; a reported loss of everything or more is left out), and that have some amount set aside for retirement: each account's start = the amount set aside today ÷ (1 + its return). The answer = the amounts set aside today added up ÷ the starts added up − 1 — what the money set aside grew by, each account weighed by what was set aside when the twelve months began. No answer when either total is zero or less.

MK-NW-F-005.name: accountAllowsTicker
MK-NW-F-005.rule: False for property, for cash accounts, and for checking and savings. Otherwise true when the account already lists holdings, a 529 included (DEC-2484g). Otherwise false for a 529, and false for an account classed as Bonds & CDs or Alternatives (it is itself one bond, CD or alternative holding typed by hand), and true for everything else.

MK-NW-F-007.name: assetKind
MK-NW-F-007.rule: Looks a kind up by its id in the app's list of account kinds and returns its entry (name, section, tax bucket, typical yearly return), or nothing when the id is not in the list. The id is matched exactly — capitals and spaces count — because only the app writes these ids; no id, or one typed another way, finds nothing.

MK-NW-F-008.name: incomeBearingClassOf
MK-NW-F-008.rule: From the account's name, capitals ignored, whole words only (put is not Putnam; cd is not ABCD), first match wins. Money market (also mmkt, mmf, or the ticker of a money-market fund) → Stocks / Funds — read before the sweep words, so a money-market settlement fund is the fund (the owner's rule of 2026-08-04). Then the words sweep or settlement → cash. The ticker of a Treasury-bill fund → Bonds & CDs. An option — an option code, a dated option, or the words put or call → Alternatives. Crypto — a coin's ticker, or the words bitcoin, ethereum or crypto → Alternatives. A commodity fund's ticker, or the words gold, silver, platinum, palladium or commodity unless the name is a company's → Alternatives. The words currency or forex, or the tickers FXE or FXY → Alternatives. The words CD, certificate of deposit, T-bill or Treasury bill → Bonds & CDs. The words bond, note, treasury, treas, UST, muni, debenture or coupon → Bonds & CDs, EXCEPT in a company's name (owner rule DEC-2747d): the name carries a company word (Corp, Corporation, Inc, Ltd, plc, Company, Mining, Resources), or the bond word is followed straight away by a business word (Wine, Wines, Estates, Group, Holdings, Brands, Partners, Properties, Industries, Hotels, Foods, Energy, Technologies, Systems, Pharmaceuticals, Enterprises) — so Treasury Wine Estates, with or without Ltd, is nothing. Whatever the name: a percent followed by the word due or a year, or a percent right beside a bond word (4.5% Bond, Notes 3.85%) → Bonds & CDs, so Apple Corp 4.5% Bond is a bond. Otherwise nothing: the name gives no evidence.

MK-NW-F-009.name: maturityClass
MK-NW-F-009.rule: Bonds & CDs when a maturity date is given that is a date by the one reading of a maturity date (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts): spaces round the text are ignored; then it must be a year, a two-digit month and a two-digit day joined by dashes, or a year and two-digit month alone, read as that month's first day; the month must be 1 to 12 and the day must exist in that month. Anything else — a one-digit month or day, words such as 'tomorrow', a time or other text after the day, a day that does not exist such as February 30 — is no date; cash when none is. An empty or blank date counts as none (owner rule DEC-4059b/c, 2026-10-10: dates are picked, never typed). It does not look at whether the date has passed.

MK-NW-F-010.name: wrapperAccount
MK-NW-F-010.rule: 401(k) → kind 401(k), pre-tax. Traditional IRA → kind Traditional IRA, pre-tax. Roth IRA → kind Roth IRA, Roth. Roth 401(k) → kind 401(k), Roth. HSA → kind HSA, pre-tax. Taxable → kind brokerage, taxable. Nothing chosen, or a word not on this list → no kind and no tax type: never assumed taxable (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10).

figures_checked_by_hand.4036: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-4036f (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-011.name: assetClassOf
MK-NW-F-011.rule: The first of these that applies. (1) The class stated on the account. (2) Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date (owner rule, 2026-08-04: any maturity-dated instrument is a bond) — whatever its name says. (3) The class its name is evidence for — except for a home, real estate, a vehicle or anything in the property bucket, whose name is a place and is not read. (4) The class of its kind: checking, savings, high-yield savings, cash management and foreign currency are cash; money market and stocks are Stocks / Funds; CD and fixed income are Bonds & CDs; private equity, hedge funds, commodities, crypto, annuities, options and other are Alternatives; home and real estate are Real estate; vehicle is Personal property. (5) Stocks / Funds if it lists holdings. (6) Cash if it is a cash account. (7) If it is property: Real estate when no kind is recorded or its use (lived in, rented, second home, land) is recorded; Personal property for any other kind. (8) Otherwise Unclassified.

MK-NW-F-012.name: taxTreatmentOf
MK-NW-F-012.rule: A 529 is tax-free whatever is stored (what it earns comes out untaxed when used for education; DEC-4036d, 2026-10-10). An HSA is tax-deferred — pre-tax going in — whatever bucket it is filed in (DEC-4036e, 2026-10-10). Otherwise the tax treatment stated on the account. Otherwise by its tax bucket — the one on the account when it is one of cash, pre-tax, Roth, taxable or property, else the bucket its kind carries when that bucket is not taxable — a kind whose catalogue bucket is taxable (crypto, a bond, a CD, a brokerage) says nothing about tax (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10): no bucket at all → tax type not stated, never assumed taxable (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10); pre-tax → tax-deferred; Roth → tax-free; anything else → taxable.

figures_checked_by_hand.4036: not a figure: the number of the owner decisions DEC-4036d/e/f (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-014.name: isRealAsset
MK-NW-F-014.rule: True when the account's class (assetClassOf) is Real estate or Personal property.

MK-NW-F-016.name: cashTotal
MK-NW-F-016.rule: For an account that has a class split (accountClassBreakdown): the cash part of it — a linked account's uninvested cash, or the uninvested cash an account built by hand records for itself. For any other account: its whole balance when its class is cash, otherwise nothing. Added up over every account.

MK-NW-F-021.name: investmentsTotal
MK-NW-F-021.rule: The Investments line on Net worth: the Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives and Unclassified lines of the class split (assetAllocation), added up. Cash sitting uninvested inside an investment account is on the Cash line (cashTotal), not here; a CD inside a cash account is here. Always: cashTotal + investmentsTotal = investableAssets.

MK-NW-F-022.name: investableAssets
MK-NW-F-022.rule: The balances of every account that is not a real asset (isRealAsset), added up by sumWhere — an account with no balance is left out, not counted as zero.

MK-NW-F-023.name: wrapperWord
MK-NW-F-023.rule: The word for a kind: checking → Checking; savings → Savings; high-yield savings; money market; CD; cash management; foreign currency → Foreign currency; brokerage, stocks, fixed income, commodities and options → Brokerage; annuities → Annuity; 401(k); Traditional IRA; Roth IRA; HSA; 529; Home; Vehicle. Crypto, private equity, hedge funds and other name what is held, not an account: nothing, unless the person confirmed the account is a brokerage. Nothing for an unknown kind or none.

MK-NW-F-024.name: accountLastFour
MK-NW-F-024.rule: From the account's mask, or failing that its account number: drop everything but digits; if four or more digits remain, the last four; otherwise nothing.

MK-NW-F-025.name: accountDisplayName
MK-NW-F-025.rule: The kind word is wrapperWord for the account (401(k), Traditional IRA, Roth IRA, HSA, 529, Brokerage, Checking and so on; none for a kind that names contents, such as crypto, unless confirmed a brokerage). An account is tax-advantaged only when taxTreatmentOf says tax-deferred or tax-free — a tax type not stated is not (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10). For a tax-advantaged account: where the kind says only Brokerage — or there is no kind and the last four digits are known — the word is Roth when the account is tax-free and 401(k) / IRA when it is tax-deferred; a 401(k) in the Roth bucket or tax-free is Roth 401(k). A tax-advantaged account always shows what it is. With an institution: a tax-advantaged account that has a word reads Institution + word + -last four (without the digits when unknown); otherwise with digits it reads Institution -last four; otherwise Institution + kind word. With none of those: the account's own name (an account named Imported holding with exactly one holding takes that holding's ticker or name), with the institution in front only if the name does not already contain it, and the mask at the end only if it is not already there.

figures_checked_by_hand.4036: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-4036f (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-026.name: accountDisplayNames
MK-NW-F-026.rule: Each account gets its display name (accountDisplayName). Where two or more accounts end up with the same name, each gets · 1, · 2 and so on added, in the order of their account ids read as text (an id is made by the app from the moment the account was created, so that is the order they were made). A numbered name that is already another account's name is skipped, so no two accounts are ever shown by the same name.

MK-NW-F-027.name: accountClassBreakdown
MK-NW-F-027.rule: LINKED ACCOUNT. Cash = the uninvested cash the broker reports (0 when none). Each holding with a price = shares × last price × the one multiplier (contractMultiplier: the shares a contract stands for — 100 for an option unless another figure is stated — one hundredth for a bond quoted per $100 of face value, else one), filed under its class (holdingClassOf). Each option = its value as synced, under Alternatives (an option is valued when it is synced, at contracts × price per share × 100 — owner, 2026-08-26). If the parts come to less than the balance and one or more holdings with shares have NO price: the whole difference is filed under the unpriced holdings' class when they share one, and under Unclassified when they span classes — never under cash. If the parts come to less than the balance, every holding is priced and the broker listed at least one holding or option: the whole difference is cash, whatever its size (owner decision DEC-0095, 2026-08-11; until 2026-10-21 only a difference within the margin below was cash). Otherwise, if the parts do not add up to the balance: a difference no bigger than the larger of $1 or 1% of the balance is added to cash when positive (owner rule, 2026-08-11), or taken off the largest class when negative; a bigger one is put under the account's own class (assetClassOf). ACCOUNT BUILT BY HAND (not a cash or property account): when it records its own cash (or its balance is built from its records) and its balance is below zero, the whole balance is cash — overdrawn is negative cash: balance −$100 with a cash field of $50 is Cash −$100 (DEC-4036i, 2026-10-10). Otherwise its cash = the uninvested cash it records, above zero, never more than the balance, when its balance is built from its records or it records cash. When its balance is built from its holdings, each holding is weighed at today's value — shares × the broker's price × the same one multiplier; else the value its balance was last built from; else what was paid over its purchases whose price paid is on record (a cost per share above zero, paidOnRecord — which already applies that multiplier, and is not scaled again); a holding with none of these, or with what was paid not on record, weighs nothing. Example: a Treasury quoted per $100, 10,000 face bought at 99, and 100 fund shares at $100, balance $19,900: Bonds & CDs $9,900 (10,000 × 99 ÷ 100), Stocks / Funds $10,000 — and the rest of the balance is shared out among the holdings' classes by those weights, so a T-bill is Bonds & CDs; if every holding is of the account's own class, the rest stays whole under that class. No answer when it records no cash and its holdings are all of its own class. ANY OTHER ACCOUNT — a typed balance, a bank account — gets no answer. The parts always add up to the balance.

MK-NW-F-028.name: classPortionLabel
MK-NW-F-028.rule: The words for one class inside one account, counting the holdings of that class (holdingClassOf — the same test the dollars beside the words were split by). Cash: cash in this account. Bonds: counts the holdings whose name has the whole word CD (or certificate of deposit), those whose name has the whole word Treasury (or Treas, UST, T-bill, T-note, T-bond, government — the broker's wording too), capitals ignored, and the rest as bonds; a count of one is singular, any other count takes its plural from the one list of words (plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10 — Treasuries for more than one), a count of zero is left out, two parts are joined with &, three as A, B & C — for example 3 CDs & 1 Treasury in this account, or 1 CD, 1 Treasury & 2 bonds in this account — or bonds & CDs in this account when none are listed. Stocks: N holdings in this account (1 holding), or stocks & funds in this account when none are listed. Alternatives: N options & N holdings in this account, each part left out when its count is zero (an option is one option position, however many contracts), or alternatives in this account. Any other class: unpriced portion of this account.

MK-NW-F-029.name: assetAllocation
MK-NW-F-029.rule: The value in each asset class across every account. An account with a class split (accountClassBreakdown) — a linked account, or an account built by hand that records its own uninvested cash — is split by it; any other account counts whole under its one class (assetClassOf). The seven classes add to everything owned, and the Cash class is cashTotal.

MK-NW-F-030.name: earmarkDefault
MK-NW-F-030.rule: The share of an account counted towards retirement by default (owner, 2026-08-11, DEC-0100: all assets minus the home lived in and the car driven): 0% for a 529, for the car driven (primaryCarIdOf), and for the home lived in. Told the household's home (its identifier, from primaryHomeIdOf), only that property is 0%; told the household has no home (null), no property is; told nothing, a property stated as the home lived in, or with no use stated, is 0%. 100% for everything else — a rental, a second home, a second car, valuables included.

MK-NW-F-031.name: primaryCarIdOf
MK-NW-F-031.rule: Among the accounts whose kind is vehicle, and no other: the vehicles whose value is entered are the candidates — a vehicle with no value is not ranked as $0 (DEC-4036j, 2026-10-10); when none has a value, every vehicle is. Of the candidates, the one with the largest balance; a tie goes to the lower id read as text (the one made first). Nothing when there is no vehicle. Valuables and other personal property are never the car.

MK-NW-F-032.name: earmarkedAmount
MK-NW-F-032.rule: Balance × the share earmarked for retirement. The share is the one stated on the account, held between 0% and 100%, or the default (earmarkDefault, told which car is driven and which property is lived in, or that there is none) when none is stated.

MK-NW-F-033.name: retirementEarmarkedValue
MK-NW-F-033.rule: Every account's earmarked amount (earmarkedAmount) added up, with the car driven found by primaryCarIdOf and the home lived in by primaryHomeIdOf, handed the Income screen's rent entries when the caller has them (DEC-4913, 2026-10-13). Example: A $400,000 with no use stated, B $300,000 marked the home with rent entered for B → $700,000 (B a rental, A a second home, no home). Not handed the rent entries, the stored home mark decides: $400,000.

MK-NW-F-034.name: benchmarkReturn
MK-NW-F-034.rule: The person's own yearly rate for that kind where they set one — a rate of exactly 0 counts as set. Otherwise the app's typical yearly return for the kind: checking 0.5%, savings 2.4%, high-yield savings 4.2%, money market 4.5%, CD 4.2%, cash management 3.5%, foreign currency 0%, brokerage 8%, stocks and funds 10.4%, fixed income 4.2%, crypto 8%, private equity 13%, hedge funds 6%, gold and commodities 8.2%, options 5%, annuities 4.5%, 529 7%, other 5%, 401(k), IRA, Roth IRA and HSA 7.9%, home 4.5%, vehicle −5%. 6% for a kind that is unknown or missing. A kind is matched exactly as the app writes it; capitals count.

MK-NW-F-035.name: blendedVolatility
MK-NW-F-035.rule: Over exactly the accounts the nest egg counts, the home read the same way (handed the rent entries when the caller has them, DEC-4913): each account's volatility — the person's own figure for its kind, else the app's figure for the kind, else 12% — averaged, weighted by its earmarked amount. No answer when nothing is earmarked (the Plan then uses the band its growth rate implies, chosen at its call site). It is a weighted average of the parts, which is the portfolio's own volatility only when the parts move together; a table of how the classes move together is not yet built.

MK-NW-F-036.name: benchmarkInfo
MK-NW-F-036.rule: The rate from benchmarkReturn, with where it came from. Edited = the person set a rate for that kind (0 included): then the source reads Your custom estimate, the period is blank and estimate is true (a person's own rate is an assumption). Otherwise the source and period on record for that kind, and estimate = whether that record is marked an assumption rather than a measured index; a kind with no record reads Generic blended estimate, period blank, estimate true. Blank is the empty text "" — never a dash; a screen that prints the period shows nothing, or its own mark, when it is blank.

MK-NW-F-037.name: blendedReturn
MK-NW-F-037.rule: Over exactly the accounts the nest egg counts (every account, each weighted by its earmarked amount — the home lived in, the car driven and a 529 weigh nothing by default, a rental weighs its full value; the home is read with the rent entries when the caller hands them in, DEC-4913): the benchmark yearly rate of each account's kind (benchmarkReturn), averaged, weighted by its earmarked amount. No answer when the earmarked total is zero — the Plan then chooses its own 6% at its call site, and says so there.

MK-NW-F-039.name: buildAssetsState
MK-NW-F-039.rule: A balance that is missing (blank, or not a number) is left out. Total = the balances that are there, added up. Each account's share = its balance ÷ total × 100, or 0 when the total is zero or less, or its balance is missing (an overdrawn account has a negative share; with a total above zero the shares still add to 100). Average target return = each account's target return weighted by its balance; no answer when the total is zero or less — an average weighted by a negative total means nothing. Example: one overdrawn account at −$50 → total −$50, its share 0%, no average return.

MK-NW-F-040.name: assetsFromOnboarding
MK-NW-F-040.rule: Makes up to four accounts from the setup answers, skipping an answer left blank or below zero (a typed 0 is kept): traditional retirement savings → a pre-tax 401(k); Roth retirement savings → a Roth IRA; investment holdings → taxable stocks and funds; each of those three gets a target return of 7%. Savings or portfolio → an Unclassified account with no kind, no tax type and a target return of 0, marked to be asked: Is this cash savings or investments? (DEC-4036g, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-041.name: monthlyContributionsFromOnboarding
MK-NW-F-041.rule: No answer when none of the contribution questions was answered (401(k), Roth, investing, employer match). Otherwise, a month's retirement contributions = the 401(k) amount, held at the year's elective limit for the person's age ÷ 12 (2026: $24,500 under 50, $32,500 at 50 to 59 and 64 and over, $35,750 at 60 to 63), + the Roth amount as entered (the question does not say Roth IRA or Roth 401(k), whose limits differ, so it is not held at either), + the investing amount, + the employer's match for a month (the stated share of the 401(k) amount AFTER it is held at the limit — an employer matches only what can go in — or the stated dollars). Money saved toward a property (an older setup question) is not a retirement contribution and is left out. The age is the one attained this year, from the birth year.

MK-NW-F-045.name: sourceWording
MK-NW-F-045.rule: Linked account: Linked — or Linked · N days old when its last successful update is 4 or more days old, and Linked · not updated yet when no update is on record (no age is invented). Imported account: Imported, by the same test. Anything else: By hand · you update it. The timestamp read is the account's last successful sync (MK-XS-I-066), never the time prices were fetched.

MK-NW-F-046.name: historyCoverage
MK-NW-F-046.rule: Entered by hand: a sentence saying it has no activity records. The history start is the person's own date when they entered one (DEC-4059c, 2026-10-10 — it outranks the date the sync read), otherwise the date the sync recorded. Linked with no history start on record: a sentence saying none has been shared yet. A history start that is not a real calendar date, or is after today: the refusal 'History start date cannot be read.' with no months figure and no start date — the screen offers 'Edit date' (owner rule DEC-4059c, 2026-10-10). History starting on or before the period's first day: nothing to say. Otherwise: months covered = the whole months from the history start to today plus the part month (days ÷ the days in that month), rounded DOWN to one decimal; the sentence is built from the whole months only and names the start date: N years when the whole months are an exact multiple of twelve and there is no part month, N years and a bit when there is, N years M months when twelve or more, N months when one or more, otherwise a few days. Year and month take their plural from the one list of words (plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10): 1 year, 1 month. It never rounds up.

MK-NW-F-047.name: uberGroupOf
MK-NW-F-047.rule: Cash → Cash. Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives and Unclassified → Investments. Real estate and Personal property → Personal property.

MK-NW-F-048.name: uberGroupRows
MK-NW-F-048.rule: Sorts the class rows into the three groups, in the order Cash, Investments, Personal property: Cash ← cash; Investments ← Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified; Personal property (the third group, which the screen labels so) ← Real estate, Personal property. A group's total = its classes' totals added up, in the order the rows came; the groups add to What you own. A group with no classes is left out.

MK-NW-F-049.name: itemizedTotal
MK-NW-F-049.rule: The values of the listed holdings that have one, added up in exact decimals; a holding with no value is left out (itemizeMissingCount counts it), never counted as zero; a negative value counts.

MK-NW-F-050.name: itemizeRemainder
MK-NW-F-050.rule: The entered balance less itemizedTotal, in exact decimals (an entered total that equals its holdings leaves exactly 0, never a stray fraction of a cent). Positive: some is still unexplained. Negative: the holdings add up to more than was entered.

MK-NW-F-051.name: itemizedResultTotal
MK-NW-F-051.rule: The account's total after itemising: the holdings added up, plus what is still unallocated when that is above zero (it stays as cash) — so it is the entered total until the holdings listed come to more than the entered total, when it is their sum. The screen shows the new total before the person taps Done.

MK-NW-F-052.name: buildItemizedAccounts
MK-NW-F-052.rule: Refused when any listed holding has no value (the refusal counts them with plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10) — nothing is built, so the account stays as it was. Otherwise one account for each listed holding: named by its label, else its ticker, else Holding; with the original's institution and tax bucket, and what the original carried — its retirement share, its source, and its wrapper kind when the original is a 401(k), IRA, Roth IRA, HSA or 529 (otherwise the kind for the class); balance = its value; class as given; its yearly rate = the benchmark for its class's kind (benchmarkReturn), never 0. A bond also carries its maturity date, its rate only when one was entered, and its face value only when the person entered one — never today's value in its place. What is still unallocated, when above zero, becomes one more account named institution + cash, with the same share, source and wrapper, at the cash-management benchmark rate.

MK-NW-F-053.name: correctClassOf
MK-NW-F-053.rule: The class an account SHOULD have, or nothing when there is no correction to make. A class the person chose is the class it should carry. Otherwise, in the order assetClassOf reads: Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date; else the class its name is evidence for — never for a home, real estate, a vehicle or anything in the property bucket, whose name is a place; else Stocks / Funds for a money market account; else Bonds & CDs for a CD.

MK-NW-F-054.name: reclassifyAccounts
MK-NW-F-054.rule: For each account the person has NOT confirmed (an account they confirmed is left exactly as it is): if the person did not choose its class and correctClassOf gives a class different from the one it carries, it takes that class (a cash tax bucket becomes no tax type stated unless the new class is cash — never taxable, DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10). For each holding inside it: a holding the person classed, or one waiting on their answer, is left as it is; otherwise, when holdingClassOf gives it a class (not Unclassified) that its stored tag does not mean, it is stored under that class — bond for Bonds & CDs, other for Alternatives (Gold), cash for Cash, stock_etf for Stocks / Funds — so the class the broker sent, kept on the holding, is stored before its name is read (owner ruling, 2026-10-20: "always the class broker sends"). A holding holdingClassOf leaves Unclassified is left as it is. Returns the accounts and how many changes were made.

figures_checked_by_hand.4036: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-4036f (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-055.name: isBond
MK-NW-F-055.rule: True when the account's class (assetClassOf) is Bonds & CDs.

MK-NW-F-056.name: bondInfo
MK-NW-F-056.rule: Reads a bond's facts off its account: face value (not entered when missing or zero or less), yearly rate (not entered when missing; a typed zero is kept), maturity date — by the one reading of a maturity date (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts), written back as year-month-day with two-digit month and day (a year and month alone becomes that month's first day), and empty when the text is no date — value — the balance when it is a market value; 0 when the balance is what was paid or the face value, or when there is no balance, so no yield is calculated on anything but a market value (owner decision DEC-0281, 2026-08-26) — and, only when the value shown is not a market value, the value shown (the balance, or nothing when there is none) and where it came from (what was paid, the face value, or none); what was paid, only when entered (a typed 0 is kept); how many times a year it pays, only when entered as 1 or 2; accrued interest (not entered when missing), whether it is a CD — its kind is a CD, or its own name says CD, certificate of deposit or share certificate, as whole words; its institution is never read for this (DEC-4036c, 2026-10-10) — and where a CD was bought: through a broker only when the person said so, otherwise from the bank (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10).

figures_checked_by_hand.4036: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-4036c (2026-10-10) that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.124: not a figure: the identifier MK-NW-F-124 of maturityParts, the one reading this function asks
figures_checked_by_hand.0281: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0281 (2026-08-26) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-057.name: annualCoupon
MK-NW-F-057.rule: Face value × yearly interest rate. Nothing when either was not entered.

MK-NW-F-058.name: yearsToMaturity
MK-NW-F-058.rule: Exact years to maturity, by anniversaries: the whole years counted back from the maturity date while still on or after today, plus the days from today to the first of those anniversaries ÷ the days in that year. One year to the day is exactly 1. Zero when the date is today or past. By the calendar date, never the time of day. Nothing when there is no date or the day does not exist (a day past the end of its month is not rolled into the next month). An anniversary on a day its year does not have — a leap day outside a leap year — falls on the last day of that month, never rolled into the next.

MK-NW-F-059.name: currentYield
MK-NW-F-059.rule: yearlyInterest ÷ the value as entered (the statement's market value, which leaves accrued interest out — his ruling of 2026-10-09). Nothing when yearlyInterest gives nothing — no rate entered, or a bond with a maturity date and no face value — or when the value is zero or less.

MK-NW-F-060.name: approxYTM
MK-NW-F-060.rule: Nothing when there is no maturity date or the bond has matured. A CD bought from the bank (pricedLikeBond says no): its stated rate, even when no face value was entered, and nothing when no rate was entered (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10). A bond, or a CD bought through a broker: nothing when no face value or no rate was entered, or when its value is zero or less; else the yield y at which priceAtYield equals the full price — the value as entered plus accrued interest (as entered, else estimatedAccrued; his ruling of 2026-10-09) — found by halving the interval two hundred times.

figures_checked_by_hand.3837: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3837 (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-061.name: bondSummary
MK-NW-F-061.rule: Count = how many bonds. Total value = each bond's value shown, added up — the market value, else what was paid, else the face value (owner decision DEC-0281); a bond with none of the three adds nothing. Total face value = each face value added up, a face not entered counting as zero (the bonds without one are named apart by theBonds). Interest in a year = yearlyInterestNow of each, added up: a bond past its maturity date counts $0, and a bond whose year's interest is not known (no rate, or a bond with a maturity date and no face value) counts as zero. Average yield is over the bonds that have a market value above zero AND a year's interest (yearlyInterest gives one) AND are not past their maturity date — a bond whose value shown is what was paid or its face value has no market value and is not in it: their yearlyInterest added up ÷ their market values added up, as entered, without accrued interest; nothing when no bond qualifies. Next maturity = the earliest maturity date AFTER today, by the calendar — a bond maturing today has matured and is not next. Each date is read by the one reading of a maturity date (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts) and written year-month-day; a text that is no date is never next.

figures_checked_by_hand.124: not a figure: the identifier MK-NW-F-124 of maturityParts, the one reading this function asks
figures_checked_by_hand.0281: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-0281 (2026-08-26) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-062.name: couponIncomeAnnual
MK-NW-F-062.rule: Over the accounts that are bonds or CDs: yearlyInterestNow of each, added up — $0 for one past its maturity date, and one whose year's interest is not known (no rate, or a bond with a maturity date and no face value) counting as zero.

MK-NW-F-063.name: interestIncomeAnnual
MK-NW-F-063.rule: For a bond or CD: nothing when it is past its maturity date (isPastMaturity, by the calendar; no date or an impossible one is not past); otherwise yearlyInterest (face × rate; with no face, nothing for a bond with a maturity date and balance × rate for a CD bought from the bank or a bond fund; with no rate, nothing). For a cash account that states a rate: balance × rate. Nothing for anything else. Added up over every account. It adds the year of interest of the bonds and CDs held inside each account (heldBondInterest), a year not known counted as nothing.

MK-NW-F-064.name: bondRateSensitivity
MK-NW-F-064.rule: Nothing for a CD bought from the bank (pricedLikeBond says no; a CD bought through a broker is priced like a bond, DEC-3837, 2026-10-10), when the yield to maturity is unknown, when the bond cannot be priced (matured or no date), or when the face value or rate was not entered or is zero or less. For rates one percentage point UP and one DOWN: the change = priceAtYield at the yield to maturity plus or minus one point (never below 0.01%) less priceAtYield at the yield to maturity itself. The new price = today's value + that change. It gives a range from 1% under to 1% over the new price, and the change, each rounded in proportion to the bond: to the nearest $1,000 for a bond worth $100,000 or more, the nearest $100 from $10,000, the nearest $10 from $1,000, and so on down.

figures_checked_by_hand.$100,000: 10 to the power 5: the step is 10 to the power (whole digits of the value − 3)
figures_checked_by_hand.$1,000: the step from $100,000, and 10 to the power 3
figures_checked_by_hand.3837: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-3837 (2026-10-10) that this rule follows

MK-NW-F-065.name: buildNetWorth
MK-NW-F-065.rule: Net worth = total assets − total debt, returned with both totals.

MK-NW-F-066.name: sumWhere
MK-NW-F-066.rule: Over the accounts that pass the given test: the total = the balances that exist, added up (a negative balance counts), and beside it how many have no balance. A missing balance is never counted as zero. Nothing passing the test is a total of 0 with nothing missing.

MK-NW-F-067.name: plural
MK-NW-F-067.rule: The count followed by the noun: the noun for exactly 1, otherwise its plural from the one list of words the app counts in words, PLURAL_WORDS (his ruling, 2026-10-10) — Treasury → Treasuries, property → properties, the verb has → have, every other word on it adds s; zero takes the plural. The count is written as the caller gives it (a formatted figure or a number word) when one is given, otherwise the number. A word not on the list is refused (an error) in tests and development, never given a guessed s; a release build writes the word unchanged.

MK-NW-F-068.name: prettyDay
MK-NW-F-068.rule: Reads a date written year-month-day as a calendar date — never through a clock or a time zone — and writes the short month name (Jan … Dec, Sep not Sept), the day without a leading zero, a comma and the year. An empty or impossible date gives nothing.

MK-NW-F-069.name: priceAtYield
MK-NW-F-069.rule: Nothing when the bond has matured or has no maturity date, when no face value above zero was entered, or when 1 + yield ÷ payments a year is zero or less. Otherwise t = yearsToMaturity, exact, and the payments a year are 2 when the bond was entered as paying twice a year, else 1 (not entered reads as once a year). Each payment is the yearly coupon (face × rate; zero when no rate was entered) ÷ the payments a year, falling at t, t − 1 ÷ payments a year, … down to the last above zero; price = each payment ÷ (1 + yield ÷ payments a year) to the power of (payments a year × its time), added up, plus face ÷ (1 + yield ÷ payments a year) to the power of (payments a year × t). Once a year this is each coupon ÷ (1 + yield) to the power of its time plus face ÷ (1 + yield) to the power t.

MK-NW-F-070.name: accruedInterestCaveat
MK-NW-F-070.rule: When accrued interest was not entered and estimatedAccrued gives an estimate (a bond or a CD bought through a broker that pays interest, not a CD bought from the bank, not matured, not on a coupon day): his words — Added estimated $<the estimate, whole dollars> in accrued interest to bond value at <the rate>% coupon for <days> days (1 day for one; the plural from plural, the one list of words — his ruling of 2026-10-10) to calculate YTM. If this is not accurate, enter actual accrued interest. Otherwise nothing. Percents are written by the one percent writer, half up on the decimal value (R24).

MK-NW-F-071.name: isCertificateOfDeposit
MK-NW-F-071.rule: True when bondInfo says the account is a CD: its kind is a CD, or its own name contains the whole word CD, or the words certificate of deposit, in any capitals. The institution's name is never read: a brokerage account at CD Capital is not a CD (DEC-4036c, 2026-10-10).

MK-NW-F-072.name: rowOf
MK-NW-F-072.rule: One row for one bond: face value and yearly interest rate (each not entered when it was not), interest paid in a year (yearlyInterestNow: face × rate; with no face, nothing for a bond with a maturity date and the value shown × rate for a CD bought from the bank or a bond fund; with no rate, not entered; $0 once past its maturity date, so the rows add up to the summary), maturity date, years left (yearsToMaturity — exact, never below zero), current yield (the year's interest ÷ the value; nothing once past its maturity date, as it pays no more interest), yield to maturity (approxYTM — solved exactly; nothing when matured), value — by the one value rule (owner decision DEC-0281, 2026-08-26): the market value, else what was paid, else the face value, and nothing when none was entered — with where it came from and, when it is not a market value, the sentence saying so (bondValueNote), what was paid (nothing when not entered), the price per $100 of face (pricePer100OfFace), whether it is a CD, whether it is priced like a bond (pricedLikeBond: a bond, or a CD bought through a broker), the accrued-interest note (accruedInterestCaveat, worked for today), and, where that interest is an estimate and how often the bond pays is not entered, the sentence saying the estimate takes it as once a year (accruedFrequencyAssumed). The heading is the institution when it is not blank after trimming, otherwise the account's name.

MK-NW-F-073.name: itemising
MK-NW-F-073.rule: Returns four things. Keep-total-at = the balance the account was entered at. Itemised = the values of the listed holdings that have one, added up. Remainder = the entered balance less that sum. Remainder-final = false when any listed holding has no value (the remainder is then not final, never called unexplained).

MK-NW-F-084.name: categoryEarnings
MK-NW-F-084.rule: Uses the dividend, interest and coupon records dated on or after the period's first day; a coupon is interest (owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19). Each record counts the money it moved into its account (2026-10-21): a record that states its direction counts its amount as plus when the money came in and minus when it went out; otherwise the amount with the sign it was stored with, so a −$50 dividend, a reversal, lowers what was earned; an amount not on record counts 0. A record that names a ticker goes to the category of the holding with that ticker (capitals ignored) — the class holdingClassOf gives it, the class the broker sent first (owner ruling, 2026-10-20: "always the class broker sends"): Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Cash in this account or Alternatives; a holding holdingClassOf cannot place in one of those four is Unclassified (2026-10-21, owner decision DEC-2160: "Refuse the line and ask"); a category's return weighs the holdings of that same category; a ticker with no holding on record → Stocks / Funds for a dividend, Bonds & CDs for interest. A record that names NO ticker → Stocks / Funds for a dividend; for interest, Bonds & CDs when the record's account is a bond or CD account handed in, else Cash in this account. A category's return is classReturnOf over the holdings of that category that have a return over the whole period (never a yearly rate), each handed in with its path across the window and what it paid for shares bought inside it (2026-10-22): where every one counted carries a path, the return is split at every day money went into the category (owner decision DEC-1669); otherwise each holding's worth = its value now + the interest it was paid in the period (a bond's or CD's, carried on the row; 0 for anything else — DEC-6212); its value at the start = that worth ÷ (1 + its return) when it is worth more than $0 and its return is above −100% (where it bought shares inside the period, the start the row carries, its worth then = that start × (1 + its return)), else the start the row carries when that start is above zero (what it was worth when the period began — a holding worth $0 today counts with what it lost; 2026-10-21, owner decision DEC-5068, tenet 4), and it is left out when it carries none; return = the worths added up ÷ the values at the start added up − 1. Nothing when no holding qualifies. Bonds & CDs shows a stated YEARLY rate instead — each bond account's rate weighted by its balance — when every bond account with a balance states a rate and no bond is held as a holding — a bond holding row worth exactly $0 holds nothing and does not count, unless it carries a start above zero — worth something when the period began, it still counts (2026-10-21); one whose worth is not known still does. Example: a bond account of $10,000 at 4%, one bond holding row worth $0, $100 of interest → Bonds & CDs $100 at 4.00%/year. An entered 0% states a rate of 0% (DEC-2748b, 2026-10-12); a rate never entered states none. On day one the categories are returned with no return: Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs and Cash in this account always, Alternatives only when a holding is classed Alternatives, and Unclassified only when a holding is Unclassified; any other day (2026-10-25, the lead's ruling MM-PF D3 under Performance v17, DEC-0647, and the owner's empty-state rule of 2026-08-04 — it replaces the third part of DEC-0064) every category held in the period, and any other that earned something other than zero: held means a holding of that category worth something now or when the period began, for Bonds & CDs also a bond account with a balance, for Cash in this account also an investment account handed in with cash; a category held that received nothing shows $0 earned. With nothing held and nothing earned, the three day-one categories with no return. Example: $1,000 of VTI up 10% and $2,000 of cash in the account, no records → Stocks / Funds $0 at +10.00%, Cash in this account $0 with no return. OVER A PERIOD LONGER THAN A YEAR (2026-10-23, owner decisions DEC-0237 and DEC-7217): where the period's own years are handed in — the years of thePerformance's answer, handed in only where that answer's return is a yearly rate — each category's return is classReturnOf over those years, the yearly rate its total gives, as the summary's is; a bond's stated yearly rate is unchanged. Example: Stocks / Funds $78,400 → $106,000 over the 731 days of a 2Y window: 35.20% in all, 16.25% a year.

MK-NW-F-090.name: windowStartKey
MK-NW-F-090.rule: Since: the day after the earliest recorded day, but never later than today; today when nothing is recorded. This year: 1 January of today's year. 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y and 2Y: today moved back 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 months — the same day of that month, or its last day when that month is shorter (one month before 31 March is 28 February). Every window except Since is read from startDateFor, on the calendar day today names. Any other label: nothing — no start, so no figure.

MK-NW-F-091.name: pricedGainOf
MK-NW-F-091.rule: Each holding's gain over the period, added up. For a holding bought inside the period: its whole gain (value − cost), with what its sales in the period brought in and everything it paid in the period counted (2026-10-22). For any other holding with a period return: value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + return)) when its value is above zero, which is today's value less its value when the period opened — but a holding held when the period opened that bought or sold shares inside it (the row carries what was paid for shares bought and what its sales brought in, 2026-10-22) gains its value + the interest it was paid less what it was worth when the period opened (the start the row carries, from the shares held then, those sold since counted back in) less what was paid for shares bought plus what its sales brought in, and its gain cannot be known (nothing) when a purchase has no price paid on record or a sale has no price and no amount; nothing when it holds nothing. For a holding with no period return that states a yearly rate (only a certificate of deposit is given one): value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + rate) to the power years), years handed in (none handed in counts as 0, so it gains nothing). Any other holding that holds something (its value, or the broker's last price × its shares, or the value it was entered at, above zero) has a gain that cannot be known: the answer is then NOTHING — not zero — for the whole total. A holding that holds nothing gains nothing. (Owner decision DEC-3656, 2026-10-09.) Its caller asks it one holding at a time, so a holding whose gain cannot be known adds nothing to the beginning and is named, while the others still count (owner decision DEC-5068, 2026-10-13). A holding sold in full inside the period has a row of its own (buildPerformance, 2026-10-22): it gains what its sales brought in less what it was worth when the period opened.

MK-NW-F-092.name: investmentAccountIdsOf
MK-NW-F-092.rule: The ids of the accounts whose class is Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives or Unclassified. Cash and property accounts are left out.

MK-NW-F-094.name: ledgerGroups
MK-NW-F-094.rule: Groups the accounts for the Net worth list, by asset-class label or by institution. By class: an account with a class split (accountClassBreakdown) is a row under EVERY class it has a part in, at that part; any other account is one row, whole, under its one class. Each group's total = its rows added up (his ruling, 2026-10-07: the rows under a heading add up to the heading). By institution (an account with no institution goes under No institution set; names are matched trimmed, capitals ignored, and the group shows the first spelling seen): each account is one row at its balance, a group's total = those balances added up, and the group lists the classes inside it with their totals, from the same split, largest first. An account with no balance entered is a row of nothing (not known), never $0 (DEC-3279e), and adds nothing to its group's total, which stays the sum of what is known: a Bank group of one account with no balance and one of $100 totals $100. Group totals by class equal the class rows; both views add to everything owned.

MK-NW-F-103.name: investmentRecordDates
MK-NW-F-103.rule: The dates of the recorded days that hold a value for at least one of the named accounts, written year-month-day, oldest first. Each day is read first without the rows of accounts whose balance was left blank — a row with no holding in that account, no value typed by hand, no total the broker stated and no cash other than $0 (a typed $0 is a value and stays; owner decision DEC-3279e, "A missing balance is never $0", 2026-10-21) — so a day on which a named account's balance was never entered does not count for it. A day whose date is not written year-month-day is not counted. Empty when no accounts are named.

MK-NW-F-104.name: closedWith
MK-NW-F-104.rule: The daily record with today added: one row per account that the latest earlier recorded day holds (of the accounts named), carrying between them the ending value handed in. The record is returned unchanged when there is no earlier day or it holds none of those accounts. It adds no arithmetic: it lets a return be measured to today when the caller gave an ending value and no accounts.

MK-NW-F-105.name: whyNoReturn
MK-NW-F-105.rule: The sentence shown where a time-weighted return cannot be measured; empty when it was measured. Money moved on a day with no recorded value: names the day and says a return cannot be measured across it. A movement with no date: says so. A deposit or withdrawal with no amount on record: names the day and says a return cannot be measured across it. Shares moved in or out: names the day and says the records do not say what they were worth. Nothing to grow from on a day (the previous evening's value + money added − money taken out is zero or less while that day holds a value): names the day and says which — a value recorded with nothing there the evening before and no money added, or more money taken out than was there the evening before plus the money added that day. Since DEC-4439 (2026-10-11) a value below the money added is a loss, measured, and has no sentence. Nothing invested over the period: says there is no return to state. Today's value not on record: says so. A record the app could not name (an activity word it does not know): says the broker recorded that amount (or an activity, when it carries no amount) on that day under its own word (or, when the broker sent no word, that it came with no word for what it was), that a return cannot be measured across that day, and that it is not counted as money put in or taken out. Interest, a dividend or a coupon with no amount on record (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3): names the kind (Interest, A dividend, A coupon) and the day, says it has no amount in the records so a return cannot be measured across that day, and says the walk's Interest line (the Dividends line, for a dividend) does not count it. A value below $0 on a day (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 1): names the day, says the value recorded is below $0 so a return cannot be measured across that day, and that the dollar figures are still right. A beginning that cannot be read has no sentence here — the period is shown as not covered instead.

MK-NW-F-106.name: mortgagesByProperty
MK-NW-F-106.rule: Properties = the accounts whose class is real estate. Mortgages = the debts whose type is mortgage. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "It is feasible to have property without mortgage but no mortgage without property. So check should be 3 properties in NW - 3 or less mortgage." A mortgage is on the property it names, when that property exists and has no mortgage placed on it yet. A mortgage that names no property is placed only where its own name says so: on the one property without a mortgage whose name it is, or begins with, followed by a space — names read without capitals, hyphens or extra spaces, so 'rental-house mortgage' is the Rental house's. It is never placed by position: the one mortgage left over is not put on the one property left over (the lead's ruling of 2026-10-27). Every other mortgage is listed as on no property — including a second mortgage that names a property already taken. It gives: the count of properties and of mortgages; for each property its mortgage (or none) and that mortgage's required monthly payment; the mortgages on no property; whether there are none of those; and the sentence to show when there are.

MK-NW-F-107.name: propertyUses
MK-NW-F-107.rule: For each property: what it is used for, as propertyUseMap reads it, handed the rent entries from the Income screen (none handed in when the person has none on record). Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "unless rental income is added on the income screen, assume property is second or vacation home." RENTAL = a rent entry names it — or, only when no rent entries are handed in at all, it is stored as a rental. HOME = the one marked as the home lived in; with none marked and no use stated on any, the one entered first. SECOND = every other property. A rent entry that names no property is not rent: it makes no property a rental (DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10). A use stated on any property stops the entered-first choice of the home (DEC-4913, 2026-10-13).

MK-NW-F-108.name: taxWordsOf
MK-NW-F-108.rule: The words for how an account is taxed, shown on its page. A 529 always reads tax-free for education; an HSA always reads pre-tax — tax-free for medical costs, whatever treatment is stated. Otherwise by its treatment (taxTreatmentOf): tax type not stated reads tax type not stated (DEC-4036f, 2026-10-10); tax-deferred reads pre-tax — taxed when it comes out; tax-free reads tax-free (Roth) for an account in the Roth bucket and tax-free for any other; taxable reads taxable.

MK-NW-F-109.name: holdingClassOf
MK-NW-F-109.rule: The class of one holding inside an account, by the one order of evidence for a holding's class (owner ruling, 2026-10-20: "always the class broker sends", which settles DEC-2159 against brief B7's name-first order). What was stored: the broker's or importer's tag (bond → Bonds & CDs, other → Alternatives, cash → cash, any other tag → Stocks / Funds), else the class of the kind picked when it was added (not real estate or personal property), else nothing. (1) If the person said what it is, their answer — the stored class, or Unclassified when nothing is stored. (2) The class the broker sent, kept on the holding as it was sent: its cash-equivalent flag is Cash; otherwise its own type — a broker code that names a class (common stock, preferred stock, ADR, ETF, open-end, closed-end or mutual fund → Stocks / Funds; bond or CD → Bonds & CDs; crypto, precious metals, warrant, right → Alternatives), or the words of an import file's type column, read in this order: cash, money market or sweep → Cash; option, crypto, precious metal, commodity, warrant, right or future → Alternatives; equity, stock, share, ETF, fund, ADR or closed end → Stocks / Funds; fixed income, bond, CD, certificate of deposit, Treasury, T-bill or muni → Bonds & CDs. A type that names none of these (unit, structured product, when issued, blank) says nothing. (3) If it is marked as asked, Unclassified (owner rule, 2026-09-30: "Refuse the line and ask"). (4) The class its ticker and name are evidence for: a money-market fund is Stocks / Funds, a sweep or settlement balance is cash, a CD or a T-bill is Bonds & CDs (owner rule, 2026-08-04: cash means cash only). (5) A maturity date that reads as a date: Bonds & CDs. (6) What was stored. (7) Otherwise Unclassified — never a guessed Stocks / Funds or cash.

MK-NW-F-119.name: estimatedAccrued
MK-NW-F-119.rule: The interest earned since the last coupon, estimated from the coupon schedule, with the days. The payment dates step back from the maturity date by 12 ÷ the payments a year months — every 12 months when it pays once a year, every 6 when twice; once a year when how often it pays was not entered (the lead's decision of 2026-10-20 under DEC-3390). A payment day the month does not have is that month's last day. Amount = face × rate ÷ payments a year × the days since the last payment date ÷ the days between that payment and the next. Nothing for a CD bought from the bank (a CD bought through a broker is estimated like a bond, DEC-3837, 2026-10-10), a bond with no face or no rate above zero, no maturity date or a day that does not exist, a matured bond, or on a payment day (nothing has accrued).

MK-NW-F-124.name: maturityParts
MK-NW-F-124.rule: A maturity date read as a real calendar day: its year, month and day. This is the one reading of a maturity date (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts): spaces round the text are ignored; then it must be a year, a two-digit month and a two-digit day joined by dashes, or a year and two-digit month alone, read as that month's first day; the month must be 1 to 12 and the day must exist in that month. Anything else — a one-digit month or day, words such as 'tomorrow', a time or other text after the day, a day that does not exist such as February 30 — is no date, and the answer is nothing. Every function that reads a maturity date asks this one (outside review OpenAI re-run part 4, 2026-10-13), so a text is a date to all of them or to none.

MK-NW-F-125.name: isPastMaturity
MK-NW-F-125.rule: Yes when the bond's maturity date is a real calendar day earlier than today's date on the device; no when it is today or later. No date, or a day that does not exist, is unknown, so the answer is no — never matured.

MK-NW-F-126.name: yearlyInterestNow
MK-NW-F-126.rule: A year's interest from one bond or CD as it pays today: $0 once it is past its maturity date; otherwise its yearly interest (yearlyInterest: face × rate; with no face, nothing for a bond with a maturity date, and the value × rate for a CD bought from the bank or a bond fund), and nothing when no rate was entered.

MK-NW-F-127.name: gainOfRow
MK-NW-F-127.rule: What one holding gained over the window, or nothing when that cannot be known. Bought inside the window, where the row carries what was paid for every purchase in the window (2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-3656): its value now + the interest it was paid in the window + what its sales in the window brought in − what it paid − what the shares it held when the window began were worth (only a holding sold out and bought again inside the window held any); nothing (unknown) when its value now is unknown, a purchase has no price paid on record, a sale has no price and no amount on record, or what it held at the start is unknown — 10 bought at $100, 5 sold at $120, 5 left at $130: $650 + $600 − $1,000 = $250. A row that carries none of that: nothing (unknown) when its own gain is not known — no close and no mark of its own; otherwise its own gain (value less cost) plus the interest it was paid in the window (a bond's or CD's, carried on the row; 0 for anything else — owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19). With a return for the period: the return over the WHOLE window (the window total the row carries; else, when the window is longer than one year, the yearly rate compounded over the window's years — (1 + rate) to the power years − 1; else the return as given); then, for a holding held when the window began that bought or sold shares inside it (the row carries what was paid for shares bought and what its sales brought in — buildPerformance, 2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-3656): (value now + the interest it was paid in the window) − what it was worth when the window began (the start the row carries, from the shares held then, those sold since counted back in) − what was paid for the shares bought inside it + what its sales brought in, and nothing (unknown) when a purchase has no price paid on record, a sale has no price and no amount on record, or the row carries no start — 10 shares held at $100, 10 more bought at $110, now 20 at $121: $2,420 − $1,000 − $1,100 = $320; 20 held at $100, 10 sold at $110, 10 left at $121: $1,210 − $2,000 + $1,100 = $310; otherwise, with a value now above zero, (value now + the interest it was paid in the window) × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + that)) — the price change plus the interest, since a bond's total holds its interest. WORTH $0 TODAY (2026-10-21; owner decision DEC-5068, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0): (value now + interest) − the value it was worth when the window began, the start the row carries — a holding that fell from $1,000 to $0 lost $1,000; $0 when that start is $0 or less (it held nothing); with no start carried, $0 when its return is above −100%, and nothing (unknown) when it is −100% or worse. A CD with a stated rate of zero or more (an entered 0% is a rate: it gains $0; a rate never entered is no rate — DEC-2748b, 2026-10-12): value now × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + the rate) to the power of the window's years), and $0 when it holds nothing. A cash position (its class by holdingClassOf is cash — a money-market fund the broker flags cash-equivalent is cash, owner ruling 2026-10-20) with neither: $0 — cash gains nothing and is never unknown (owner decision DEC-5291, 2026-10-13). Otherwise: $0 when it holds nothing (heldValueOf is 0 and it holds no shares), and nothing (unknown) when it holds something or its worth is unknown — a holding with no price history and no rate; shares the broker marks at $0 are something held (2026-10-21), so they are unknown, never $0 gained. A holding sold in full inside the window with no period figure (no prices to say what it was worth when the window began): nothing (unknown), never $0 (2026-10-22, tenet 3).

MK-NW-F-130.name: notIncludedSentence
MK-NW-F-130.rule: The sentence when a holding with no price history is left out of Wealth generated and Return (owner decision DEC-5068, 2026-10-13; worded by DEC-6076, 2026-10-19). It is handed the holdings left out, each with a name and its value today (or no value when that is unknown), and the value today of the holdings the return counts. Spaces round each name are removed and a blank name is dropped; each name is listed once, however many times it is handed in, and the values of all the holdings left out are added. The names: one name (or none, read as "a holding"); several joined by commas with "and" before the last. When every left-out value is known their total follows the names in brackets, in whole dollars: "Treasury 2031 ($10,000)"; when one is unknown there are no brackets. The left-out part: "<names> has no price history, so its gains are not included." for one name, "have ... their" for several, from the one list of words and plurals (MK-NW-F-067 plural). When the value the return counts is above zero, the sentence opens with "Return is on the $<that value> with a price history. " in whole dollars; when it is zero only the left-out part is said, opening with a capital when it begins "a holding". Example: VTI $40,000 counted, Treasury 2031 $10,000 left out: "Return is on the $40,000 with a price history. Treasury 2031 ($10,000) has no price history, so its gains are not included." EACH LEFT OUT FOR ITS TRUE REASON (2026-10-22; tenets 1 and 3, canon row 24): each holding handed in carries why it is left out — no price history (the default), a purchase in the window with no price paid on record, or a sale in the window with no amount in your records. The holdings are grouped by reason, and one left-out part is said for each, in that order, each with its own names and its own bracketed total: "<names> has a purchase with no price paid on record, so its gains are not included." (several: "have purchases … their"), "<names> has a sale with no amount in your records, so its gains are not included." (several: "have sales … their"). With nothing handed in, the part about "a holding" with no price history is said, as before. Example: Y $2,420 with a price history, a purchase of it in the window with no price paid on record: "Return is on the $2,420 with a price history. Y ($2,420) has a purchase with no price paid on record, so its gains are not included." A holding whose last close before the window began is more than START_CLOSE_DAYS days old is named with that close's day — it has no price near the window's start, so its gains are not included — after the other reasons.

MK-NW-F-138.name: knownHoldingsReturn
MK-NW-F-138.rule: The return of the holdings whose growth over the period is known (owner decision DEC-5068, 2026-10-13), worked by classReturnOf — the method each category's return uses, one function since 2026-10-22 — so where every holding counted carries its path across the window the return is split at every day money went into them (owner decision DEC-1669). For each holding: its return over the WHOLE period (the period total it carries; else, when the period is longer than one year, its yearly rate compounded over the period's years — (1 + rate) to the power years − 1; else the return as given); a holding with no return that states a yearly rate of zero or more (only a certificate of deposit is given one) grows by (1 + rate) to the power years − 1. A holding with neither is LEFT OUT — never counted at 0%. Each holding's worth = its value + the interest it was paid in the period (a bond's or CD's, carried on the row; 0 for anything else — owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19). A holding with a value above zero and a return above −100%: its start = that worth ÷ (1 + its return) — or, where it bought shares inside the period, the start the row carries (from the shares held then), its worth then = that start × (1 + its return). A holding worth $0 today, or with a return of −100% or worse, counts at the start the row carries (what it was worth when the period began — 2026-10-21, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0) when that start is above zero, and is LEFT OUT when it carries none. Answer = the worths added up ÷ the starts added up − 1 (everything lost is −100%, a return); nothing when no start is counted. Example: VTI $40,000 at +10% and Treasury 2031 $10,000 with no price history → 40,000 ÷ 36,363.64 − 1 = +10.00%. Example: AAA $1,000 → $0 (start $1,000) and BBB $1,000 → $1,200 at +20% → 1,200 ÷ 2,000 − 1 = −40.00%.

MK-NW-F-141.name: holdingBondFacts
MK-NW-F-141.rule: A bond or CD held as a holding, its facts for the line under its name (owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19): it is read as a bond account would be (the bond row of the bonds door) with its holding id (else ticker) as the account, its name (else ticker) as the label, its type, face value, coupon rate, maturity date and how many times a year it pays, and the value handed in as its balance — a market value. MK-NW-F-142.name: classReturnOf
MK-NW-F-142.rule: What one category grew by over the window (outside review MK-NW-F-084; owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19). Of the items handed in, keep those with a total that is known and above −100% and a value today above zero. Each kept item's worth = value today + its interest in the window (0 when missing); its start = worth ÷ (1 + total). An item with a known total that is not kept — worth $0 today, or a total of −100% or worse — counts too when it carries a start above zero (what it was worth when the window began; 2026-10-21, owner decision DEC-5068, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0): worth = value today + its interest, start = that start. SPLIT AT EVERY DAY MONEY WENT IN (2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-1669): when every item kept carries its path across the window (buildPerformance) and each path's pieces give back that item's own total (an item changed after its row was built does not), the answer is returnSplitAtPurchases over those paths instead — the window split at each day money went into any of them; on each such day the piece ends at what they were all worth at the previous evening's close and the next begins once that day's money is in; the last ends at their values today plus their interest; the pieces multiplied, − 1. Otherwise: an item that carries what it paid for shares bought, or what its sales brought in, inside the window (2026-10-22) and a start above zero counts at that start, its worth = that start × (1 + total). Answer = the worths added up ÷ the starts added up − 1; nothing when the starts add to zero or less, or the worths to less than zero. Example: $5,000 with $100 interest and $4,000 with $85, both totals from a flat price plus that interest → 9,185 ÷ 9,000 − 1 = 2.06%. Example: one holding alone, $1,000 → $0 → 0 ÷ 1,000 − 1 = −100.00%. Example, split: A $1,000 and B $10,000 when the window began; the evening before A buys 90 more at $105 they are worth $1,050 + $10,000; with the $9,450 in, $20,500; today $11,000 + $5,000 → 11,050 ÷ 11,000 × 16,000 ÷ 20,500 − 1 = −21.60%. An item bought and sold inside the window, nothing held at either end, is in the split while it was held, with no start of its own in the starts; an item worth $0 today because it was sold, with what its sales brought in on the row, counts at its start × (1 + total) (2026-10-22). OVER A WINDOW LONGER THAN A YEAR (2026-10-23, owner decisions DEC-0237 and DEC-7217): when the window's own years are handed in and are more than 1, the answer above is made the yearly rate it gives, (1 + answer)^(1 ÷ years) − 1, the one rule every return over such a window follows; with no years handed in, or years of 1 or less, the answer is the window's own total. Example: VTI alone, $208 → $280 over the 731 days of a 2Y window: 280 ÷ 208 − 1 = 34.62% in all; years = 731 ÷ 365; 1.3462^(365 ÷ 731) − 1 = 16.00% a year.

MK-NW-F-143.name: gainRowBetween
MK-NW-F-143.rule: What one holding did over the days before the daily record begins (owner decision DEC-6412, 2026-10-19): from the evening before a window (from) to the record's first day (to). Each purchase is dated by its own purchase date when it is on record (a real calendar day written year-month-day; 31 February is not), else by the purchase date the window used for a holding bought inside it, else it was held from before the window. Purchases dated after the first day are left out; when the holding has purchases and none is held by the first day, the answer is nothing (it had no part in those days), and so is a holding with no purchases on file that the window counts as bought after the first day. Its close on the first day = the latest close on or before that day; its close at the start = the latest close on or before the evening before the window, else, where its prices begin inside those days, its first close. When the close on the first day is not known, or the close at the start is not known for shares held from before, the holding comes back with no return (and no interest, no purchase date): its gain over those days is unknown. Value on the first day = the shares held that day × that day's close × the contract multiplier. Start = the shares held from before × the close at the start × the multiplier + what was paid for the shares bought inside those days (shares × cost per share × the multiplier; a purchase with no price paid on record — none, or a stored $0: a price paid is on record only when it is a number above zero — makes the return unknown). A holding with no purchases on file: value on the first day = today's value × that day's close ÷ the latest close; start = today's value × the close at the start ÷ the latest close (unknown when the latest close or today's value is not above zero). Start not above zero: unknown. Interest = the interest a bond or CD was paid from the window's first day on, less what it was paid from the day after the record's first day on (bondInterestInWindow; nothing for anything else). Return = (1 + value on the first day ÷ start − 1) × (1 + interest ÷ value on the first day) − 1 (returnWithInterest; worth $0 on the first day, interest ÷ start − 1), given as both the period return and the period total, with the value on the first day as its value and the start as the value it carries for when those days began (2026-10-21: a holding worth $0 on the record's first day is counted with what it lost); a holding that comes back with no return carries no start. It carries no money paid inside the window and no path across it (2026-10-22): those are the whole window's, and here a purchase inside those days is already in the start at what was paid. A purchase inside those days with no price paid on record comes back unknown and says so (no money paid inside, 2026-10-22), so the left-out sentence gives that reason, not a missing price history. A CD WITH A STATED RATE AND NO PRICES (statedCdRate; 2026-10-27, FX-PF), held through those days with no purchase inside them, its value today above zero, and today handed in: it grows by its rate across them — its value on a day = its value today ÷ (1 + the rate) to the power of (the days from that day to today ÷ 365); the return = the value on the record's first day ÷ the value the evening before the window, less 1, given as the period return and total, with that start carried. The close at the start is no start when it is more than START_CLOSE_DAYS days before the evening before the window (staleStartClose): such a holding comes back with no return. For a day inside the window (money moved), the close at the start is that day's own however old — the 7-day limit is the window's start's only (R19b).

MK-NW-F-150.name: heldInOf
MK-NW-F-150.rule: Which Held in choice an account's saved answer is, so a form opened on it shows that choice again; nothing when there is no account or the answer cannot be told apart. The choice kept on the account, when it is one of the six (Taxable, 401(k), Traditional IRA, Roth IRA, Roth 401(k), HSA). MK-NW-F-151.name: linkedSplit
MK-NW-F-151.rule: A linked account split into its classes, with the cash in it that is not a holding and the value of its holdings with no price. It starts with Cash = the uninvested cash stored on the account (0 when none), every other class 0, and the cash that is not a holding at the same figure. Each holding is put in its class by holdingClassOf. A holding with a last price adds its shares (the shares of its purchases added up, a missing count as 0) × that price × the one multiplier (contractMultiplier: the shares a contract stands for — 100 for an option unless another figure is stated — one hundredth for a bond quoted per $100 of face value, else one) to its class; a holding with no price adds nothing, and when its shares are not 0 its class is noted as unpriced. Every option adds its value (0 when none) to Alternatives. The difference = the account's balance (0 when none) − the classes added up. When the difference is not 0: (1) above zero with at least one unpriced holding: the difference is those holdings' value — added to their class, or to Unclassified when they span classes — and handed back as the unpriced part with that class; (2) otherwise above zero with at least one holding or option listed: all of it is Cash, whatever its size (owner decision DEC-0095), and is added to the cash that is not a holding; (3) otherwise within the larger of $1 or 1% of the balance (sizes without their signs): above zero it is Cash and is added to the cash that is not a holding, below zero it goes to the largest class; (4) otherwise it goes to the account's own class (assetClassOf), Unclassified when that is not known. The unpriced part is nothing except in case (1).

Nothing when every holding is priced, the total leaves nothing over, or the account was built by hand.
