MK-NW-F-162.name: yearsWords
MK-NW-F-162.rule: How long a window longer than a year is, in words: two years when its years are from 1.9 up to (not including) 2.1; otherwise its years written to one decimal place, then years.

MK-NW-F-163.name: yardstickName
MK-NW-F-163.rule: The yardstick's name in words: its ticker, trimmed and in capitals, looked up in the one table of yardstick names; a yardstick not in the table is named by its ticker; no ticker, no name.

MK-NW-F-164.name: gapWords
MK-NW-F-164.rule: The gap between a holding's return and its yardstick's, in words: nothing when the gap is missing or not a number; otherwise ahead when it is 0 or more, behind when below, then by, the gap's size as a percent to two decimals, then points, and /year after it when the window is longer than a year.

MK-NW-F-165.name: purchaseQuantityWords
MK-NW-F-165.rule: One purchase's quantity on its line: no share count on record when the count is missing or not a number; for a holding counted in shares, the count written by the caller's writer then sh; for any other unit, the count with that unit in full as the Quantity row writes it, or the count then sh when there is none.

MK-NW-F-168.name: holdingRowsIn
MK-NW-F-168.rule: Each holding's window figure in one account, one way on every page that shows it. The records read are that account's own; each holding's first purchase day is the earliest date of its purchase records by ticker (a record with no full year-month-day date is skipped). Then buildPerformance for those holdings, the window and today, with that first purchase day for each, the window's first day when one is handed over, and the account's records and the account itself handed in.

MK-NW-F-169.name: isWholeAccountPart
MK-NW-F-169.rule: Whether one part of an account is the whole account, so its return is the account's: no when the part's value is unknown; yes when the part's value and the account's balance (0 when missing), each rounded to whole dollars, are equal and nothing else in the account was worth more than 0 when the window began.

MK-NW-F-170.name: incomeSumParts
MK-NW-F-170.rule: The parts of the income sum under the account page's table. None when the account's income is missing or not above 0. Otherwise each row in order gives its dividends + interest (each 0 when missing), added exactly in decimals, kept when above 0; then what the account's income is beyond those parts, added when it is above 0 (the income no holding carries), so the parts add up to the account's income.

MK-NW-F-171.name: listedShares
MK-NW-F-171.rule: The shares a holding holds: the share counts of its purchases added up; nothing (unknown) when any purchase has no share count on record.

MK-NW-F-172.name: classValueOf
MK-NW-F-172.rule: One class's value on the account page: its rows' values added up (a missing value counts 0); nothing (unknown) when any row's share count is not stated.

MK-NW-F-173.name: restOfAccountBeside
MK-NW-F-173.rule: The rest of an account beside one class: the account's balance − that class's value, each 0 when missing.

MK-NW-F-174.name: overTheYearsSentence
MK-NW-F-174.rule: The one sentence for a window longer than a year: nothing when the window's own total or the yearly rate is missing; otherwise the window's own total, written by the caller's writer, then the words over the, the window's years in words (yearsWords), the words which is, and the yearly rate written by the same writer with its /year.

MK-NW-F-175.name: whyLeftOut
MK-NW-F-175.rule: Why a holding's gain over the window is not known, for the left-out line: what was paid for its purchases in the window is unknown, so a purchase there has no price paid on record (paid); else what its sales in the window brought in is unknown, so a sale has no amount in the records (sale); otherwise it has no price history (history).

MK-NW-F-176.name: categoriesEarnedTotal
MK-NW-F-176.rule: All categories, the table's last line: what each category earned, added up; an amount that is not a number counts 0.

MK-NW-F-177.name: walkDirectionWords
MK-NW-F-177.rule: Which way the value went over a window: up to when the ending is above the beginning, down to when it is below, level at when they are equal.

MK-NW-F-178.name: itemisedShare
MK-NW-F-178.rule: How much of an account's total the listed holdings fill, from 0 to 1: what is listed ÷ the total, kept between 0 and 1; 0 when the total is 0 or less.

MK-NW-F-179.name: balanceWithBondTakenOut
MK-NW-F-179.rule: An account's balance once a bond added as part of it is taken out: the balance (0 when missing) − what the bond is worth, never below 0.

MK-NW-F-180.name: barSegments
MK-NW-F-180.rule: The composition bar's segments. Each row counts at its total, or 0 when that is below zero; the whole is those added up, and with a whole of 0 or less there are no segments. Each segment's exact share = its count ÷ the whole × 100; its percent = that share rounded to a whole number; whatever the percents added up fall short of 100, or exceed it by, goes to the segment with the largest exact share, so the percents always total 100. Its width = its exact share, never less than the sliver floor of 1.5. Each bar's whole percent is written by the app's one points writer, half up on the decimal value.

MK-NW-F-181.name: barDrawnWidths
MK-NW-F-181.rule: The bar as drawn: each segment's drawn width = its width × 100 ÷ the widths added up, so after the sliver floor the drawn widths fill the bar exactly.

MK-NW-F-182.name: accountsInClass
MK-NW-F-182.rule: How many accounts sit in one class: an account counts when its split by class holds that class, or, when it has no split, when its own class is that class. An account holding several classes counts in each it holds.

MK-NW-F-183.name: accountsInClasses
MK-NW-F-183.rule: How many accounts sit in several classes: accountsInClass for each class, added up, so an account holding two of the classes counts in both.

MK-NW-F-184.name: isPartOfAccount
MK-NW-F-184.rule: Whether the amount shown for an account is only part of it: yes when the amount differs from the account's balance (0 when the balance is missing) by more than half a cent.

MK-NW-F-185.name: valueChanged
MK-NW-F-185.rule: Whether an edit changed a value: yes whenever the new value is not exactly the old one; an empty value and a number differ.

MK-NW-O-001.name: theBonds
MK-NW-O-001.rule: Takes every account that is a bond or CD. Rows are sorted by maturity date, soonest first, with any that has no date last — the date read by the one reading of a maturity date (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts), so a text that is no date sorts with the ones that have none. Count, total value, total face value, interest in a year, average yield and next maturity come from bondSummary. The bonds the average yield leaves out are named by why: no value, no rate, a rate and no face value on a bond, or past its maturity date (matured — it pays no more interest). When one bond is opened it also gives: matured = its maturity date is today or earlier, by the calendar (a bond with no date has not matured — it is unknown); a matured bond gives no yield to maturity and no rate-move figure; and what a move in interest rates would do to its value (bondRateSensitivity) — except for a CD not priced like a bond (bought from the bank, or where it was bought not entered, which the bond's facts read as the bank), where no figure is given and a sentence says why. For a CD where it was bought is not entered (2026-10-21, owner decisions DEC-3523 and DEC-3837), the sentence says where this CD was bought is not entered, that a CD bought from the bank is not traded so its value does not move with rates, and that a CD bought through a broker is traded and its value does move with rates — and the bond is marked as not answered. For a CD marked as bought from the bank, the sentence says a CD is not traded and is worth its balance until it matures. A CD bought through a broker gets the figure like a bond and no sentence (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10). It also names the bonds the average yield leaves out — those with no market value above zero, and, apart, those with a market value above zero but no rate entered, and those with a market value above zero and a rate whose year's interest is not known because no face value was entered on a bond with a maturity date (2026-10-24, owner decision DEC-3523 tenet 3) — and the bonds with no face value entered, so a screen can say which. It also names the bonds with no value of any kind entered — no market value, nothing paid and no face value — which the total value leaves out (owner decisions DEC-0281 and DEC-3657). The bonds the average yield leaves out are also given by why: value not entered at all; a market value of $0 or less; the value shown is what was paid; the value shown is the face value — each bond the average leaves out is in exactly one of the four. Where a bond or CD has no face value entered, the sentence says the money put in comes back when it matures, not the face value.

MK-NW-O-002.name: theAccount
MK-NW-O-002.rule: Uses the records whose account is this account, and any transfer that arrives in it from another account. Market value = the account's balance. Income = dividends + interest + coupons in those records, to the cent — a coupon is interest (owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19) — and NO FIGURE when the account has no records at all. Inside = the value in each asset class that is not zero, from the account's class split (accountClassBreakdown) — a linked account always has one; nothing when the account has no split (a balance typed as one figure). Activity = every record with its date, type, ticker and amount: the amount is the record's effect on cash (cashEffect), except a transfer INTO this account, which shows the amount that left the other account — both read by the one rule for a stored amount (2026-10-21: the direction the record states, else its kind's own way, the amount keeping the sign it was stored with), so a deposit the broker sent with a minus shows as minus, and an amount not on record has no effect; each record also says whether its amount is not on record (a deposit, withdrawal, transfer, dividend, interest, coupon or fee whose amount is missing, blank or not a number), so the page shows a dash for it, never $0; a record counts as the person's own unless it came through the link. Income of one holding = dividends, interest and coupons whose record names that holding's ticker, capitals and surrounding spaces ignored; a record naming no ticker belongs to no holding. Income of the cash in the account = the interest records (type INTEREST only) that name no ticker, to the cent, with no dividends — the cash row's own income on the account page (the account-page drawing v01, approved 2026-10-19, owner decision DEC-6457); a dividend naming no ticker stays with the account only. Each activity record also carries, when it was sent under a word the app does not know, the broker's word and the amount it sent, unsigned, so the page shows that amount and word instead of its effect of 0 (Q15, the lead's decision of 2026-10-20); nothing for every other record. Cash in this account (the cash row) = for a linked account, the uninvested cash the broker reports (0 when none is reported) plus the part of the broker's total that the listed holdings, the options and that cash do not reach, when that part is above zero, every holding is priced and the broker listed at least one holding or option (owner decision DEC-0095: the difference is cash) — the same figure Net worth's Cash line counts; nothing for an account built by hand. The holdings with no price = for a linked account where at least one holding with shares has no price and the broker's total leaves a part above zero that the priced holdings, the options and the cash do not reach: that part as their value, filed under their class (Unclassified when they span classes), and how many holdings have no price and a share count that is not zero — a share count that is not on record, because a purchase has none, counts as not zero (2026-10-22: the count is unknown, not 0); nothing when every holding is priced, the total leaves nothing over, or the account was built by hand — never $0. An opening-cash record moves the account's cash by its own amount, as entered (never below zero), and is neither money in nor a gain.

MK-NW-O-003.name: theNetWorth
MK-NW-O-003.rule: Assets = every account's balance added up. Debts = every debt's remaining balance added up. Net worth = assets − debts. Cash = cashTotal. Investments = investmentsTotal: the investment classes of the class split added up (Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified, from assetAllocation) — so a linked account's uninvested cash is in Cash only, and Cash + Investments + property comes to everything owned. Investable = investableAssets. By class = assetAllocation. Each debt is listed with its balance and its required monthly payment: the larger of its minimum and the payment the person says they make (a minimum not entered beside a payment that was is that payment; a balance due in one lump has none); a debt with neither a minimum nor a payment entered (paymentNotEntered) counts 0 on its line and is named, by its id and its name (A debt when it has none), in the list of debts whose payment is not entered — never counted as $0 unsaid (owner decision DEC-3523, tenet 3). Monthly debt payments = those lines added up; monthly debt minimum = the minimums alone added up. Investments by account = each account with its id, its name (the institution, spaces at the ends ignored, else its label) and how much of it counts in Investments (accountInvestments) — only those above zero, the largest first. Return on cash + investments = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return.") over every account that is not property: the period from the day compared from to today is split at every day money moved in or out; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off; returned as a share. A month given without a day is read as its first day. Cash earns only interest: any other change in a cash account's balance is money moving, counted on the day the record first shows it. For the other accounts, money moving = deposits, withdrawals and cash transferred between accounts. Today's value is read from the accounts as they stand. No figure when no day is given, when no recorded day on or before the day compared from holds the accounts, when money moved on a day with no recorded value, when a deposit, withdrawal or transfer on a measured account has no amount on record, when interest, a dividend or a coupon on a measured account has no amount on record (since 2026-10-21: unknown is not zero), when a record the app could not name sits on a measured account inside the period, or when shares were moved in or out. It also hands out the match of mortgages to properties (mortgagesByProperty). It also names the holdings nothing could class and the person has not yet answered about (account, holding), and the sentence that asks. A holding with no price today is taken out of every day of the return's window, the start day included, so the change line leaves it out as the fix sheet promises (Net worth v08 state F).

MK-NW-O-004.name: theEmergencyFund
MK-NW-O-004.rule: Cash = all cash (cashTotal), or the amount handed in when one is given. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "Once user enters mortgage or any debt - the app deduct it directly to calculate surplus, emergency fund, and any other place instead of leaving it for user to add it to planned expenses." Debt minimums = the MINIMUM monthly payment of every debt added up, never below zero — the home's mortgage included; a balance due in one lump has none. A payment a person chooses to make above the minimum is not counted: it can be stopped. When a debt has no minimum stored, the monthly payment the person entered stands in for it. A debt with neither a minimum nor a payment entered (paymentNotEntered) counts 0 and is named, by its id and its name (A debt when it has none), in the list of debts whose payment is not entered — never counted as $0 unsaid (owner decision DEC-3523, tenet 3). The budget is read as it is counted (theBudgetCounted): where the home's mortgage is in Debts, the Rent / Mortgage budget line is counted as nothing, and the screen is given a sentence saying so. Essentials for a month = essential expenses + debt minimums — only when there are essential expenses: with nothing logged and no plan typed there is no month, and the debt payments alone are never one (the lead's ruling of 2026-10-27). Essential expenses = the average of what was logged, over the calendar months of the last twelve that have a logged entry (this month alone when only it has one); the typed plan only when nothing is logged. Left out of that average, so nothing is counted twice: a payment logged against a debt that is entered (an expense in the category Debt payment, named for that debt), and, where the home's mortgage is in Debts, anything logged under Rent / Mortgage. Rent that keeps arriving = the Rent row of the Income summary (rent from a property less what it costs to run, less calculated tax when the tax rate is calculated), never below zero; owner, 2026-10-04: "add it to the cash as losing job does not mean loosing rental income too." It arrives every month, so it is added to the cash every month. From cash each month = essentials − that rent, never below zero. Months covered = cash ÷ from cash each month; no figure when essentials are zero, and no figure when the rent pays for the whole month (the cash is then not drawn on, and it says so). Planned = planned monthly expenses + debt minimums, when planned monthly expenses are above zero (no planned figure otherwise); months covered at the planned level = cash ÷ (planned − that rent); no figure when that is zero or less. Target for N months = from cash each month × N; gap = target − cash, never below zero. Months left after a shock = (cash − the shock, never below zero) ÷ from cash each month. When a typed month of essentials is handed in, it stands in for essentials + debt minimums. A target, and the months left after a shock, are given only when there is an essentials figure. Rent not known, owner rule 2026-10-10 (instead of showing nothing, the card says the months are counted with the rent not included, and asks for the rent): the answer also says whether a property's rent is not known. It is not known only when the household holds a property that is not the home (home, rental and second home read by the owner's property-use rule of 2026-10-04) AND one of these holds: a rent entry's rent figure is blank or not a plain number, or the entry names no property (it is not counted as rent, owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10); the rent entries are stored in a shape that is not a list; or with no rent entries stored at all, a property is kept as a rental. A property with no rent entry when rent entries are stored is a second home, not a missing rent. A household with no property other than the home is never flagged. The months covered are still given, counted without the unknown rent. The old single typed rent figure (from before rent became a list) is not read: the app moves it once into the rent list as an entry with no property, which the entry rule above then treats as not known. Where the month comes from is said with it, as a tag and as the end of a sentence: a month typed here (you entered; 'the month you entered here'); the one monthly total typed in the plan, with no debt payment added (you entered; 'the monthly total you entered'); the plan otherwise (calculated; 'calculated from your budget', and 'and your debt payments' when debt minimums are added); logged expenses by their own words ('… of your logged expenses', with ', plus your debt payments'). The months covered, at the essentials and at the planned level, are given only when a cash figure is entered — a cash figure handed in, cash other than zero, or a cash account with a balance entered — and it says whether one is.

MK-NW-O-005.name: theAlternativesOutlook
MK-NW-O-005.rule: Count, total value and blended rate come from alternativesSummary: over every account that holds alternatives, its alternatives part (altPartsOf) — the same dollars the Net worth tab's Alternatives line counts. Blended rate: over the classified parts only; no figure when nothing classified is held. Growth in a year = alternativesSummary's growth (the classified parts × blended rate), given only when there is at least one such account and the total is above zero; otherwise no figure. Money not classified = the parts no priced holding or option explains; when it is not 0 the summary says: Expected return and growth leave out <amount> asset type not classified. Rows = each account that holds alternatives, at its alternatives part, with the yearly rate of its classified parts weighed by value (no rate when none of it is classified) and its not-classified money; for an account that is not itself an alternative (a brokerage holding a bitcoin fund or options), the row also says which part of it this is (classPortionLabel for Alternatives). The rows add up to the total (DEC-4036h, 2026-10-10). Its share of the investable assets handed in: the total value of the alternatives ÷ the investable assets, nothing when those are not handed in or are not above zero.

MK-NW-O-006.name: theHolding
MK-NW-O-006.rule: Shares = shares of every purchase still held, added up (nothing when a purchase has no share count); a sale has already taken its shares from the purchases, oldest purchase date first (a purchase with no date last). Total paid = shares × cost per share over the purchases whose price paid is on record, a cost above zero (paidOnRecord; × 100 for an option contract unless the holding states its own multiplier); nothing when a share count is not on record, or shares are held and none has a price paid on record. The price is the daily price when there is one, else the holding's own price on record (priceOnRecord: its last price, the broker's mark or the price typed — a CD or an option read from a file has no daily price but carries its mark). With a price: value = shares × price (× 100 for an option contract unless the holding states its own multiplier); gain = the value of the units counted − total paid, over the same purchases (unrealizedGain); return on cost = gain ÷ total paid (no figure when nothing was paid, or either is unknown). With NO price: value shown = total paid, and gain, return and the tax estimate are not given. Average paid per share = Σ shares × cost per share ÷ Σ shares over the purchases whose price paid is on record, per share as the price is quoted (nothing with no shares held, a share count not on record, or no purchase with a price paid on record); the shares it leaves out = the shares of the purchases with no price paid on record (0 when none; nothing when a share count is not on record). A purchase's cost not on record stays not on record, never 0. Closed = shares known and zero or less. Day change = last close − the close before, for ONE share (it is shown under the price of one share, not multiplied by shares held), and that ÷ the close before; none with fewer than two closes. Gain if sold today is split by purchase (capGains): long-term = purchases held MORE than one year; a purchase held exactly one year or less is short-term; a purchase with no purchase date on record is in neither part and its gain is given on its own; an option on a broad-based index is 60% long-term and 40% short-term whatever the holding period. Not capital gains = the account it sits in is taxed as pre-tax or tax-free (taxTreatmentOf: a 401(k), a Traditional IRA, a Roth IRA, a Roth 401(k), an HSA, a 529; with no account handed in its tax type is not stated) — the split is then not shown and the gain is given whole; an account whose tax type is not stated keeps the split. Dividends = dividend records IN THIS ACCOUNT that name this ticker (the ticker read with spaces trimmed and capitals ignored): the last 365 days, and all time, each counted as the money it moved into the account (when the record says which way the money went, its size, minus when it left; otherwise its amount with the sign it was stored with; an amount not on record adds nothing); a dividend in another account belongs to that account's holding of the ticker. It also says how many such dividend records there are (2026-10-21): with none, nothing is on record about this holding's dividends, and the page draws no Dividends line rather than $0. Realised gain = from the sale records of this ticker in this account, × this holding's contract multiplier. Where the closes are handed in with their days, the day's change is given only from the last two dated closes, and only when they are one to four days apart (a weekend or a holiday between); fewer than two dated closes, or a wider gap, gives no day's change.

MK-NW-O-007.name: theLookBack
MK-NW-O-007.rule: Passes the amount, the two price histories, the number of months and today to lookBack and returns its answer unchanged.

MK-NW-O-008.name: thePerformance
MK-NW-O-008.rule: A record dated after today is read as dated today (the balance already holds its money, so it is put in today and has earned nothing yet). Each recorded day, and today's, is read without the rows of accounts whose balance was never entered: a row is kept when its account has a holding, a typed value (a typed $0 counts), a total stated by the broker, or cash other than $0 (DEC-3279e). Records of the period = those dated on or after its first day; contributions, withdrawals, dividends and interest are their totals. Contributions also count cash or shares transferred in from an account that is not one of those measured, and, when the beginning is read, each account that first appears in the record after the day before the period (up to today) — at the money added to it that day when more than half a cent was (it was worth $0 the evening before, DEC-4439), otherwise at its first recorded value (its own records up to that day are then not counted again); withdrawals also count cash or shares transferred out. A transfer between two measured accounts is neither. THE BEGINNING IS READ from the daily record at the day BEFORE the period opens, and only when investment accounts are named and the record's first day is on or before that day; the value read is the last recorded day on or before it. If it cannot be read, the period does not open today, the record holds days for these accounts (beginning after the period opens), and NO holding here has a history over the period (a period return, a stated rate of 0% or more such as a certificate of deposit's, or bought inside the period; or, with only a dollar gain handed in, a known gain other than 0): NO walk (no beginning, no wealth generated), and a sentence: The record begins <its first day>, so it cannot say what this account was / these accounts were worth on <the day before the period>. Owner decision DEC-5291, 2026-10-13 (it replaces DEC-3035i): if it cannot be read and any holding has such a history — whether or not the record holds days for these accounts — the beginning is WORKED BACK: beginning = ending − priced gain − contributions + withdrawals (priced gain counts as 0 when the period opens today). Where the beginning CAN be read but some of the accounts named are not in the record on the day before the period and hold something with a history (and every holding handed in belongs to an account handed in), the answer is the parts added up: the accounts the record holds that day, measured together by this same rule, plus each other one worked back on its own by this same rule; every walk line is the parts' lines added; the return = Σ values now ÷ Σ (value now ÷ (1 + return)) − 1 over the measured part (its ending and its measured return; its beginning read from the record is its start where it lost everything, 2026-10-21) and each worked-back holding with a history (knownHoldingsReturn), no percent when the measured part refuses (its sentence is given); the sentence for holdings left out names those of the worked-back accounts; the yearly rate as below. The priced gain is each holding's gain over the period by the one rule for it (pricedGainOf: a holding's return is read as the period's own total, never a yearly rate), years = the period's days ÷ 365; a measured account with no holdings and a balance above 0 counts as its own holding, worth its balance — a certificate of deposit stating its rate gains by that rate (an entered 0% is a rate and gains $0; a rate never entered is no rate — DEC-2748b, 2026-10-12), any other has no price history. With no period at all (day one) no rate is applied and a holding with no price history adds nothing. Owner decision DEC-5068, 2026-10-13 (it replaces part 2 of DEC-3656): where the beginning is worked back (a period that does not open today, no record of these accounts at all) and a holding's gain cannot be known (it holds something, has no price history and no stated rate), that holding adds NO gain — its value is taken as unchanged — the walk is still drawn, and a sentence names it (worded by owner decision DEC-6076, 2026-10-19): Return is on the $<counted> with a price history. <name> ($<left out>) has no price history, so its gains are not included. Several names are joined with commas and "and" before the last, their values added: <A> and <B> ($<left out>) have no price history, so their gains are not included. $<counted> = today's value of every holding the return counts (each holding knownHoldingsReturn keeps, asked one at a time; in the parts-added case, the measured part's ending where its return is measured, plus each worked-back holding kept); when it is 0 the first sentence is left out. $<left out> = today's value of the holdings named: the broker's mark × shares or the value typed by hand (heldValueOf), else what was paid for it (costBasis); when any of them is unknown the brackets are left out. Whole dollars. A holding is named by its ticker (the security's name where the ticker is a 9-character identifier); an account by its display name; a dollar gain handed in as unknown is named "a holding". In that worked-back case, when the holdings themselves are handed in, the return given is the return of the holdings whose growth is known (knownHoldingsReturn): each holding with a value above zero and a return over the period above −100% (its whole-period total; a certificate of deposit with no return by (1 + its rate) to the power years − 1) has a start = value ÷ (1 + that return), and a holding worth $0 today counts at the start its row carries (what it was worth when the period began; 2026-10-21, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0); return = values added up ÷ starts added up − 1; a holding with neither is left out, never counted at 0%; with none, no percent. When only a dollar gain is handed in, no percent is given. It also says whether the beginning was worked back this way, so a screen shows that period like any other rather than greying it. The ending is given on its own as well, whether or not there is a walk. Walk: wealth generated = ending − beginning − contributions + withdrawals; change in investment value = wealth generated − dividends − interest. Records counted are those of the investment accounts named, a transfer whose other side is one of them, and a record that names no account (with no accounts named, every record); a record on any other account is not money put into these investments. Return = a TIME-WEIGHTED return (owner decision, 2026-10-04: "All return should be True Weighted Return and not Dietz return."): the period, starting at the last recorded day on or before the day before it opens, is split at every day money moved in or out of those accounts; each piece = the value just before the next movement ÷ the value just after the last one; the pieces are multiplied and 1 is taken off. The record holds one value a day, taken after that day's money moved; money that moves on a day counts for that whole day (owner decision DEC-4439, 2026-10-11), so a day's link = that day's value ÷ (the previous recorded day's value + money added that day − money taken out that day). Money moving = deposits (in), withdrawals (out), cash transferred between accounts (out of the first, into the second), and shares moved in or out at what they were worth (the amount, or shares × price) when the record says which way they went. Ending = what the measured accounts are worth today, each counted whole (its balance, uninvested cash inside it included), read from the accounts handed in — a figure handed in beside them is not used, so no two screens can give two endings; with no accounts handed in, the ending handed in is used, and closes the record unless the record already holds today. Today's value for the return is read from the same accounts. An account that first appears in the record inside the period counts as money in, at the money added to it that day, else its first recorded value (as above). A recorded day that is missing an account with holdings is not used; a typed balance stands until it is next recorded. It REFUSES — no percent, a sentence saying why, never another method — when: the beginning cannot be read; money moved on a day with no recorded value; a movement has no date; a deposit, withdrawal or transfer has no amount on record; interest, a dividend or a coupon on a measured account has no amount on record (since 2026-10-21: unknown is not zero — the sentence names its kind and day); a record the app could not name sits on a measured account inside the period; shares were moved in or out and the record does not say which way or what they were worth; the previous recorded day's value + the money moved that day is zero or less while that day holds a value (nothing to grow from); or nothing was invested. Where the beginning IS read but the return cannot start from that day (the record's day before the period is missing an account with holdings, so it is not used), the period counts as not reached: the walk is drawn from the beginning read, but there is no percent and no sentence, and the screen greys it. For a period longer than one year — its first day earlier than one year back from today by the calendar (windowStartKey), so a period opening one year back to the day is a year and is never made yearly — and days ÷ 365 above 1, unless it is the whole-record Since period, the figure shown is the yearly rate (1 + return) to the power 1 ÷ years, − 1. Owner decision DEC-6412, 2026-10-19 (it amends DEC-5291): where the beginning cannot be read, the record holds days for these accounts that begin after the day before the period and before today, the holdings and their price histories are handed in, the period is JOINED at the record's first day instead of worked back whole. The record's part = this same rule asked for the period that opens the day after the record's first day (the Since answer), each holding handed over as it did from that first day to today (gainRowBetween; a holding not held over those days is left out); when the record's part draws no walk, nothing is joined and the DEC-5291 answer above stands. The days before = each holding of an account that had a part in them — the record holds it on its first day, or (several accounts, every holding placed) the record's part works it back on its own because it is not on the record that day and holds something with a history — worked from the day before the period to the record's first day (gainRowBetween, handed today, so a CD with a stated rate and no prices grows by its rate across those days; a holding not yet held then is left out); each instrument account the record holds that day counts at its value read then (one worked back on its own: its value now ÷ (1 + its rate) to the power of the record's part's years); years = those days ÷ 365. Their return = knownHoldingsReturn over those rows; when there is none and some row's gain is unknown, nothing is joined and the DEC-5291 answer above stands; when there is none and every gain is known (only cash, or nothing held), it is 0. Return = (1 + that return) × (1 + the record's part's return) − 1 (no percent when the record's part refuses: its sentence is given); the yearly rate as below. Walk: beginning = the record's part's beginning − the gains of those days (gainOfRow, an unknown one adding 0) − the money put in during them + the money taken out during them (records from the period's first day to the record's first day, leaving out those of an account with no part in them); contributions, withdrawals, dividends and interest = those days' plus the record's part's; ending = the record's part's ending. The left-out sentence names the holdings of those days whose gain is unknown, through beforeTheRecordSentence, $<counted> = today's value of each holding those days count (knownHoldingsReturn asked one at a time) and each left-out value today's (as above). It also gives the record's first day, and says the beginning was worked back (the period is not greyed). THE WHOLE-RECORD SINCE PERIOD COUNTS THE DAY A NEW ACCOUNT OPENED (owner decision DEC-4439; 2026-10-21): when the beginning can be read, the day before Since opens is the first day the record holds any of these accounts, and money was added that day — more than half a cent, by the same movement rules — to one or more of the accounts the record holds that day, the period is measured from the evening before that day: on that evening each such account is worth $0 and every other account the record holds that day is worth its own value that day, and that day's records of those other accounts are not counted again (they are inside that value). The answer is this same rule asked for the period that opens on that first day, with the period's first day given as handed in and that first day as the day the beginning is read. It is done once: never when the record already holds such an evening. Each holding left out is named for its own reason (2026-10-22, notIncludedSentence): no price history, a purchase in the window with no price paid on record, or a sale in the window with no amount in your records. A holding sold in full inside the window carries its own account (2026-10-22): it is counted in that account's parts, and an account whose holdings were all sold in the window is read from those sales, not as an instrument of its own. ONE TYPED ACCOUNT THAT SOLD INSIDE THE PERIOD (2026-10-31, FX-PF): for the period worked back, one account whose holdings were typed by hand (not added up from its holdings, not linked) with a sale inside it, every holding named and a walk drawn, the return is the walk's ending ÷ its beginning, less 1, when no money moved in or out; when money moved, there is no return, and the sentence names the first day money moved that the record does not hold. TYPED-TOTAL ACCOUNTS (R18, 2026-11-01): for one typed account worked back, every record inside the window enters the walk — beginning = ending − the holdings' move − interest paid to its own cash + fees − put in + taken out — for every record kind; its return is the walk's own (ending ÷ beginning − 1 with no money moved; with money moved, the pieces are split at each day money moved, the value just before each worked back from today the same way, and multiplied; nothing where a piece cannot be worked). With several accounts, each typed-total account is read on its own by this same function and counted as one row (its value now, its start, its return) beside the other accounts' holdings; one of them refusing refuses the summary too. The sentence then names the whole the return is on and its two parts: the dollars with a price history and the rest of the typed accounts' totals, worked back from their records. A holding whose start close is too old (staleStartClose) is named with that close's day. ROUND 5 (2026-11-01): a holding with prices on record, however old, counts as having a history, so the window is worked back and the holding named in R19's sentence rather than the window greyed. One typed account with no holdings listed, its gain not known (a bond or fund typed as a value): the beginning is worked back without its interest, which stands on its own line, so its change in investment value is $0, not a loss. With money moved inside the window, the value just before each day money moved is today's total less today's holdings, plus the shares held that day — today's plus those sold since less those bought since, at the close before that day — less the money put in since, the interest to its cash and the sale proceeds net of fees since, plus the fees and buy costs since; no figure when a trade's shares or price is not on record, when shares moved in kind, or when a dividend was reinvested. A buy or a sale inside the window saved without its price or amount (a holding left out for no price paid or no sale on record) leaves the walk's own change unknown: no return for a typed-total account, and the sentence names the record. Where the return is measured from the daily record (covered) and not refused, it also hands back the pieces that return is made of, from the time-weighted return (timeWeightedReturn); otherwise no pieces.

MK-PF-F-001.name: totalShares
MK-PF-F-001.rule: The shares of every purchase added up. Nothing (unknown) when any purchase has no share count — a missing figure is never counted as zero; a share count of 0 is a count.

MK-PF-F-002.name: costBasis
MK-PF-F-002.rule: Shares × cost per share, added up over every purchase, × the contract multiplier (contractMultiplier: an option's own shares per contract when it states a real number above zero, else 100 for an option; one hundredth for a bond the broker quotes per $100 of face value; otherwise 1). A purchase with no shares adds nothing. Nothing (unknown) when a purchase has no share count, or has shares and no cost per share on record; a cost per share of 0 is a figure.

MK-PF-F-004.name: marketValue
MK-PF-F-004.rule: Shares × price × the contract multiplier, unrounded. 0 when no shares are held. Nothing (unknown) when there is no price, or the share count is unknown — shares with no price are worth something unknown, not 0.

MK-PF-F-005.name: unrealizedGain
MK-PF-F-005.rule: Over the purchases whose price paid is on record (paidOnRecord — a cost above zero): the units counted × the price (× the contract multiplier) − what was paid for them. Nothing (unknown) when there is no price, a purchase has no share count, or units are held and none has a price paid on record. Nothing held: 0 when the market value can be worked out, else nothing. With every price paid on record this is market value − cost, as before.

MK-PF-F-006.name: capGains
MK-PF-F-006.rule: With no price: the long-term, short-term and total gains and the counts of shares are nothing (unknown). Purchases with no shares held are passed over. For each other purchase whose price paid is on record (a cost per share above 0 that is a real number — a stored $0 is not on record): gain = shares × (price − cost per share) × the contract multiplier (100 for an option unless the holding states its own, otherwise 1). A purchase with no price paid on record is left out of the gain, and its shares are counted as held but not counted. Each purchase goes in one of three parts by its purchase date: long-term when today is after the first anniversary of the purchase date — held MORE than one year (a purchase on the leap day has its anniversary on the last day of February the next year, so a sale on the first of March is long-term) — short-term otherwise; and in NEITHER when its purchase date is not on record (none, blank, written another way, or a day the calendar does not have, such as 31 February) — that part is returned on its own as the undated gain, with its shares counted and held. When no dated purchase is held and an undated one is (or has no share count), the long-term and short-term gains are nothing (unknown); with no purchase held at all the gains and share counts are 0. A part with shares held and none with a price paid on record has no gain (unknown); a purchase with no share count makes its part, the total and the share counts unknown. Total = the gain over every purchase with a price paid on record, in all three parts added up — a part whose own gain is unknown only because none of its shares has a price paid on record adds nothing to it; the total is nothing when a purchase has no share count, or shares are held and not one of them has a price paid on record. For an option on a broad-based index (SPX, SPXW, XSP, NDX, NDXP, RUT, MRUT, VIX, DJX, OEX or XEO, read from the ticker's letters before the expiry): long-term = 60% of the total and short-term = the total less that, whatever the purchase dates (IRS Publication 550, the 60/40 rule of section 1256), and no undated part. Returns the long-term gain, the short-term gain, the total, the shares counted and held, and the undated part when there is one.

MK-PF-F-007.name: totalROI
MK-PF-F-007.rule: Unrealised gain ÷ what was paid, both over the purchases whose price paid is on record (paidOnRecord). Nothing when there is no price, what was paid is unknown or zero or less, or the gain is unknown.

MK-PF-F-008.name: startDateFor
MK-PF-F-008.rule: 1M, 3M and 6M: today moved back that many months; 1Y and 2Y: back 12 or 24 months — the same day of that month, or its last day when that month is shorter (one month before 31 March is 28 February; a year before 29 February is 28 February). This year: 1 January of today's year. Any other label: nothing — a window name the app does not have gives no start.

MK-PF-F-009.name: latestClose
MK-PF-F-009.rule: The close on the latest date on record, in whatever order the prices are listed; nothing when there are no prices.

MK-PF-F-010.name: periodReturn
MK-PF-F-010.rule: End = the latest close. The beginning day = the calendar day BEFORE the period's start date, as the person's own calendar day (both boundary days are inside the period). Start = the last close on or before the beginning day — or, when every price on record is later than that day, the FIRST close on record. Return = end ÷ start − 1. For 2Y it is given as a yearly rate by the one rule every screen uses (2026-10-21, MK-PF-M-016): (end ÷ start) to the power 1 ÷ years, − 1, where years = the days from the evening the figure starts at (the beginning day, or the first price's day when the prices begin later) to today ÷ 365 — 21% over 731 days is +9.99% a year — and only when that span is longer than a year on the calendar (it starts before the 1Y window's own beginning day); a span of a year or less keeps its own total. Nothing when there are no prices or the start close is zero or less. The same move is also given as the period's own total, never a yearly rate, for anything that adds holdings up. Nothing for a window name the app does not have.

MK-PF-F-011.name: periodReturnSince
MK-PF-F-011.rule: The same as periodReturn but measured from a given day, read as written: latest close ÷ the last close on or before that day (or the first close on record when all are later), − 1. Never turned into a yearly rate. Nothing when the day is not one the calendar has, and nothing when it is after today, the person's own calendar day (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3: a window that has not begun has no move to state — it read +0.00%). Asked for a day inside a window, the start close is read however old (closeAsOfInside); a window's own start keeps the 7-day limit.

MK-PF-F-012.name: earliestPurchaseDate
MK-PF-F-012.rule: The earliest purchase date among the holding's purchases, a real calendar day written year-month-day (purchaseDateOnRecord; 31 February is not one). MK-PF-F-013.name: benchmarkTicker
MK-PF-F-013.rule: The market yardstick for a holding, handed its kind (or the holding itself). The class the person set decides first: a bond → AGG; stocks and funds → SPY. Then the class the broker sends, read as the class reader reads it (the broker's own class reader; owner ruling DEC-6614, 2026-10-20: always the class the broker sends): Bonds & CDs → AGG; Stocks / Funds → SPY; any other class it sends (cash, alternatives) decides nothing here. Then a stored class where no kind names a yardstick: a bond → AGG; stocks and funds → SPY. Otherwise by kind: stocks and funds → SPY; fixed income and annuities → AGG; private equity → PSP; hedge funds → QAI; commodities → GLD; crypto → BTC; 529, 401(k), traditional and Roth IRA and HSA → AOR; other → SPY. A kind or class that names no yardstick → SPY. NOTHING when nothing says what the holding is (no kind, no class) — no yardstick, and its comparison refuses.

MK-PF-F-014.name: buildPerformance
MK-PF-F-014.rule: For each holding: price = latest close; market value; cost = what was paid over the purchases whose price paid is on record (paidOnRecord); unrealised gain and return on cost from the functions above, over the same purchases (each nothing where unknown). Bought = its earliest dated purchase (a purchase of 0 shares is none), or the date supplied when no purchase has a date. A PURCHASE WITH NO DATE BESIDE BUYS THE ACCOUNT RECORDED (2026-10-25, FIX-HOLDINGS; owner decision DEC-3656: a buy is neither money in nor money earned): where every dated purchase after the day before the period's start is one of the account's own buy records (that day's purchases are no more shares than its buy, opening or reinvested records of that ticker that day — recordedBuysExplain), the purchase with no date is read as held when the period began, as it is when it stands alone, so the holding is not bought inside the period and those purchases are its trades inside it (read from its trades, below). 100 VTI imported with no date ($95 the evening before the month began, $99 the evening before today, $100 today) and 20 bought today at $100 on the trade sheet: +5.09% = 9,900 ÷ 9,500 × 12,000 ÷ (9,900 + 2,000) − 1, gained $500 (it read no return, and the account's window lost its start). Purchases only typed on the holding, with no buy record, keep the rule of DEC-7216 below. If it was bought ON OR AFTER the period's start day it is capped: its period return is time-weighted from its purchases — the purchases grouped by day (when no purchase has a date, all on the bought day; a purchase with no date beside dated ones gives no return since purchase, and the row is marked as holding an undated purchase, 2026-10-21); the first piece starts at what was paid; a purchase counts from the start of its day (DEC-4439, 2026-10-21): at each later purchase day the piece ends at the shares then held × the close of the previous evening (the last close on or before the day before, on or after that piece's first day; with none, the piece ends at the money it began with), and the next starts there plus what that purchase paid; the last ends at shares held × today's price; the pieces multiplied, − 1 (purchasePieces; one purchase day gives the return on cost; nothing when a share count is missing, a purchase of shares has no price paid on record — a cost per share above 0 — or a purchase with no date sits beside dated ones) — and the yardstick is measured since the first purchase date (nothing when that date is after today, 2026-10-21). Otherwise its period return is the price return over the period (periodReturn, a yearly rate over 2Y), and the yardstick is measured over the same period — unless it is read from its trades (below). Each row also carries the period's own total for the holding and for the yardstick (never a yearly rate). No yardstick (nothing says what the holding is): no yardstick return. Beat-by = the holding's return − the yardstick's (marketGap, the one gap Home's ahead-by reads too); nothing when either is missing. When a holding's prices begin after the period's start (its first price's day, compared as a calendar day, is after the day before the start; and it was not bought inside the period), the yardstick is measured from the holding's first price on record over the same days, and over 2Y made a yearly rate over the very years the holding's own figure is (periodReturnParts) when that span is longer than a year (never for a handed-over first day). For a window name the app does not have there is no start: every row's period return, totals and yardstick return are nothing, and no row is capped. When the caller hands over the window's first day (the Since window, whose first day is the record's), that day is the period's start: each figure is the move from the close on or before the day before it to the latest close, never a yearly rate, and a holding with no dated purchase whose stand-in date is that first day is not capped (it is part of the beginning value). A BOND'S OR CD'S INTEREST (owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19): when the caller hands over the records and the accounts, a holding that is one bond or one CD (it sits in Bonds & CDs, no fund word — ETF, fund, trust, index, portfolio — in its ticker or name, not a Treasury-bill ETF, and the CD type, a 9-character security identifier with a digit as its ticker, a maturity date, a coupon rate or a face value says it is one instrument) has the interest it was paid added: interest = the interest and coupon records (bondInterestInWindow), each the money it moved into the account — plus when it arrived, minus when the record says it left, nothing when its amount is not on record — dated on or after the day its price is measured from (its purchase when capped, the day after its first close when its prices begin after the period's start, else the period's start day) that name it by ticker or holding id — on its own account when the record names an account — or that name no holding and sit in an account that is itself a bond or CD holding only this holding; the period's own total = (1 + the price total) × (1 + interest ÷ its market value) − 1 (the price total alone when there is no interest, or no market value above zero and no start; with a market value of $0, interest ÷ its start − 1 — returnWithInterest), and the period return is that total, made a yearly rate over 2Y exactly as periodReturn makes one (to the power 1 ÷ the years its prices span, when above one), never for a capped holding or a handed-over first day. The row carries that interest; anything that is not one bond or CD, or with nothing handed over, carries none and its return is its price move alone — a fund's distributions are already in its adjusted closes (DEC-4644). WHAT EACH HOLDING WAS WORTH WHEN ITS PERIOD FIGURE BEGAN (its start value, 2026-10-21; owner decision DEC-5068, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0, so a holding that fell to $0 keeps the value it lost): not capped, the shares held when the period began — its purchases dated on or before the day its period figure is measured from, and any with no date on record (heldOnDay, 2026-10-21: shares bought inside the period were not held at its start) — × the close its period figure is measured from (valueAtClose) (the close on or before the day before the period's start, or before a handed-over first day; its first close when its prices begin later) × the contract multiplier, nothing when that close is not above zero; capped, the shares held × the price its return since its purchases is measured from — the money in the last piece ÷ (the growth of the pieces before it × the shares held after the last purchase), from purchasePieces — × the multiplier, which is what was paid for a holding bought on one day, and nothing when that growth is not above zero; nothing wherever its period figure is nothing. Years (2026-10-21) = the years its period return is a yearly rate over — set only where it is one (a fixed window longer than a year whose prices reach back more than a year, not capped), so a screen can write /year and the window's own total beside it; nothing otherwise. WHAT WAS PAID INSIDE THE PERIOD (2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-3656): a row that is not capped and has a period figure, whose holding bought shares after the day its period figure is measured from, carries what was paid for them (read from its trades inside the period, as below: what each day's purchases were paid; nothing when one of them has no price paid on record); one that bought none carries nothing. ITS PATH ACROSS THE WINDOW (2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-1669): every row built together shares one list of days — each day money went into any of these holdings inside the window (a capped holding's purchase days; a holding held before, its purchases dated after its figure began; a holding whose prices begin later, the day after its first close) — and each row with a period figure and a market value carries, on each of those days, what it was worth at the previous evening's close before that day's purchases and after them (holdingPath): held before, the shares held × that close × the multiplier, a purchase counted at that close; joining after its first close, $0 until that day; capped, $0 until its first purchase, then purchasePieces' own values (each purchase at what was paid × the multiplier, the shares held × the latest close on or before the evening before when that close is dated on or after its last purchase day, else the value it began that piece with); with its start (the start value; $0 when capped or joining later) and its end (market value + interest). A row whose pieces do not multiply back to its own period total, to within one billionth, carries no path. ITS TRADES INSIDE THE PERIOD (2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-3656): its account's records of its ticker after the day its period figure is measured from (the account holding it is found; none, none read) — each sale's shares and what it brought in (shares × price × the multiplier, else the cash it moved, cashEffect; unknown with neither), each purchase's shares and what was paid (bought, opened, or a dividend or interest reinvested; unknown without a price above $0). Bought on each day = today's purchases of that day, or, where a sale may have reached a purchase made inside the period (no purchase from before the period is left, or always for a holding bought inside it) or no purchase carries a date (a broker's one total), the larger of that and the records; a purchase made on or before a sale that the records do not cover leaves what was held at the start, and what was paid that day, unknown (a sale takes the oldest purchase first, MK-CF-F-139). Shares held when the period began = today's shares − every share bought since + every share sold since (20 held, 10 sold, 10 left: 20). Its start value, not capped, is that × the close its figure is measured from × the multiplier (it read today's purchases dated on or before that day). The row carries what was paid for shares bought inside the period (for a capped holding, every purchase in it) and what its sales brought in, each only where there were any; a capped holding that held shares when the period began too (sold out, then bought again) carries what those were worth then. Where it is not read from its trades, its path counts sales too, at the previous evening's close; it carries its yardstick's closes on the same days — at the close its period figure begins at (its purchase day's close when capped; the day after its first close when its prices begin later) and each previous evening's — kept only where they give back its own market figure. HOLDINGS SOLD IN FULL INSIDE THE PERIOD (2026-10-22, owner decision DEC-3656): with the records and accounts handed over, every account that holds one of these positions, or none at all, adds a row for each ticker it sold after the day before the period starts and no longer holds — no purchases left, naming its account, its kind taken from the same ticker held in any account handed over, else a stocks-and-funds account's sold holding is a stock or fund and a bonds account's a bond. Its row is read from its trades: 10 held at $100, all sold at $110 for $1,100 — start $1,000, what its sales brought in $1,100. A ROW READ FROM ITS TRADES (2026-10-22, DEC-1669, DEC-4439; widened 2026-10-23, one rule in every window) — a holding sold in full; one bought inside the period that sold some of it or that held shares when the period began; and one held when the period began, its prices reaching back to it, that bought or sold inside it, where the shares it held then, every purchase's price paid and every sale's takings are on record (otherwise it keeps its price move, its gain left out where unknown): its period figure is its own path's pieces multiplied — each purchase in at what was paid, counted from the start of its day; its mirror, a sale out at what it brought in after its fee, at the end of its own day (eventDays: a sale is carried on the day after it, so the piece ends with the shares sold at what they brought in and the shares kept at the sale day's close); nothing held, no piece: 10 held at $100, all sold at $110 → +10.00% beside a gain of $100; 100 held at $95, 10 sold at $98 with a $5 fee the day it closed at $98, $100 today → (8,820 + 975) ÷ 9,500 × 9,000 ÷ 8,820 − 1 = +5.21% (its price move read +5.26%). Its market figure is its yardstick over the very days it was held. A holding sold in full is never made yearly; one held when the period began is, over 2Y, as periodReturn makes one, and so is its market figure, over the same years; the row's own totals stay the window's. Its start, where it held shares when the period began, what those were worth then. 10 bought at $100, 10 more at $110 the next month, the first 10 sold at $120 the month after, $130 today: +30.00% (from the purchase still held it read +18.18%). A SALE'S FEE (2026-10-22, DEC-6873, DEC-6874): what a sale brought in is its shares × price × multiplier (else the cash it moved) less the fee the stored price does not already carry (feeNotInPrice), so the fee comes off once. A HOLDING WITH NO CLOSE OF ITS OWN (2026-10-27, FX-PF): bought inside the period with no close, its own mark stands in for the price — its price on record (priceOnRecord), else, bought today, what was paid a share (paidPerShare) — for its return since purchases, its value, its gain and its return on cost; nothing where neither is on record. Bought inside the period with a purchase whose price paid is not on record, the money paid inside it is unknown, so its gain over the period is unknown. A CD WITH A STATED RATE AND NO PRICES (statedCdRate), held through the whole period — no purchase dated after the evening before it began, no sale inside it: its period figure is (1 + the rate) to the power of the period's days ÷ 365, less 1; its value is its own mark (ownMark) and its start that value ÷ (1 + the period figure), with no path; over 2Y, held more than a year, the yearly rate is shown, with the years. A holding bought inside the window measures its yardstick from the purchase as a day inside the window (R19b), so an old close is read, not refused.

MK-PF-F-015.name: topHoldingConcentration
MK-PF-F-015.rule: Nothing when any holding's value is unknown, or below zero (a short position: a share of the whole has no plain meaning, 2026-10-21). MK-PF-F-020.name: portfolioBenchReturn
MK-PF-F-020.rule: Over the holdings startValues keeps: NOTHING when any of them has no yardstick return — a holding in the person's return with no market figure of its own would leave the market unmatched to the mix (2026-10-21). Each one's value at the start = the start the row carries when it is above zero — what the holding was worth when the period began, from the shares held then (buildPerformance's start value, 2026-10-21: shares bought inside the period were not held at its start) — else its value now ÷ (1 + its own return over the whole period); for a holding worth $0 today, the start the row carries (startValues, 2026-10-21: a holding that lost everything is in the market's average as it is in the person's return); the yardstick returns (over the whole period, never a yearly rate) averaged, weighted by those start values. A holding with no return of its own is left out. Nothing when the starts add to zero or less. Example: A $1,000 → $0 with its yardstick at +10%, B $1,000 → $1,200 with +2% → (0.10 × 1,000 + 0.02 × 1,000) ÷ 2,000 = +6.00%. Example with shares bought inside the period: A held 10 shares at $100 when it began and bought 10 more inside it, now 20 at $121 (own +21%, yardstick +10%), start carried $1,000; B $2,000 → $2,000 with +4% → (0.10 × 1,000 + 0.04 × 2,000) ÷ 3,000 = +6.00% (worked back from today it would be $2,420 ÷ 1.21 = $2,000 and +7.00%). ON THE SAME DAYS, WITH THE SAME WEIGHTS, AS YOUR RETURN (2026-10-22, the lead's decision under DEC-1669 and tenets 1 and 7): where every holding kept carries its path across the window with its yardstick's closes on the same days (buildPerformance), and each path gives back its own row's market figure, the answer is marketSplitAtPurchases instead: the window split at every day money went into or out of a holding — the days your return is split at — and on each piece every yardstick weighted by what that holding was worth when the piece began (a holding bought inside the window weighs nothing before it was bought), the pieces multiplied, − 1. With no money moved inside the window there is one piece, and it is the start-weighted figure above. Example: VTI $10,000 up 10% with the market, $10,000 more bought on Sep 25 with the market flat after: piece 1 (10,000 × 1.10) ÷ 10,000, piece 2 (11,000 + 10,000) ÷ 21,000 → +10.00% (weighed by the starts alone, +5.00%). Rows bought and sold inside the period, nothing held at either end, are in the split for the days they were held, as in your return (2026-10-22). Where shares were sold on a day, that piece sets them beside the market to that day's close — the mirror of a purchase measured from its own day's close — and the rest to the previous evening's (2026-10-22).

MK-PF-F-022.name: factorOverMonths
MK-PF-F-022.rule: Nothing with fewer than two prices. Cut-off = today moved back the given number of months — the same day of that month, or its last day when that month is shorter. Nothing when the first price on record is later than the cut-off — the record does not reach back that far. Start = the last price on or before the cut-off. Factor = latest close ÷ start close; nothing when the start close is zero or less.

MK-PF-F-023.name: lookBack
MK-PF-F-023.rule: Nothing unless the amount is above zero and both funds have a factor (factorOverMonths). Stayed: end value = amount × the factor of the fund it was in; change = end value − amount; percent = (factor − 1) × 100, at full precision. Moved: the same with the other fund's factor. Difference = moved end value − stayed end value.

MK-PF-F-028.name: realizedFromLedger
MK-PF-F-028.rule: Uses buy, opening-position and sale records that name a ticker, with shares above zero, for the ticker and account asked for, in date order, a purchase before a sale on the same day (2026-10-23: 10 bought and 10 sold today match each other); a sale is used only with its price. A purchase with no price paid on record keeps its place in line (2026-10-21, DEC-4643): the shares a sale takes from it are not matched — they are shares whose cost is not on record, listed on the sale — so a sale is never matched past it to a later purchase. A sale is matched to the earliest purchases first, within one account and one ticker. A record's fee counts only when it is a number above zero and the record does not say its price already carries it; otherwise it is 0. A purchase's fee is part of what was paid for its shares: each time a sale takes shares from a purchase, it takes the same share of that purchase's fee still unmatched as the shares it takes are of the purchase's shares still unmatched (10 bought with a $4 fee and 5 of them sold carry $2 of it). A sale's own fee comes off what it brought in, in the share its matched shares are of the shares sold. Gain on a sale = (matched shares × sale price − what those shares cost) × the contract multiplier of the holding asked about (100 for an option unless it states its own; 1 when no holding is named) − the sale's fee on its matched shares − the purchase fees its matched shares carry; the fees are dollars and are not multiplied. All-time = every sale; this year = sales dated in today's calendar year, a sale dated after today read as today's (2026-10-21: its shares already left the holding). Each sale is counted once: sales counted = sales with at least one matched share; sales without a purchase = sales with none matched. Every sale with shares no purchase covers is listed with its date, the shares sold, the shares matched and the gain on the matched part (nothing when none matched). Example: bought 10 at $50, sold 15 at $70 → gain 10 × ($70 − $50) = $200; sales counted 1, sales without a purchase 0; listed: sold 15, matched 10, gain $200. Bought 10 with no price paid on record, then 10 at $50, sold 10 at $70 → the 10 sold are the first 10: no gain counted; sales counted 0, sales without a purchase 1; listed: sold 10, matched 0. With fees: bought 10 at $100, sold 10 at $120 with a $5 fee not in the price → gain 10 × ($120 − $100) − $5 = $195.

MK-PF-F-038.name: periodTotalReturn

Nothing when there are no prices, no latest close, no close at the beginning, or that close is zero or less.

MK-PF-F-039.name: periodReturnParts
MK-PF-F-039.rule: Nothing when there are no prices, or the period's name is not one the app has. End = the latest close. The beginning day = the calendar day BEFORE the period's start date, as the person's own calendar day (both boundary days are inside the period). Start = the last close on or before the beginning day, or the first close on record when every price is later (closeAsOf). Nothing when end or start is missing, or start is zero or less. Total = end ÷ start − 1. Years: 1 for every period except 2Y (1 means it is never turned into a yearly rate). For 2Y (2026-10-21, one rule for a yearly rate on every screen, MK-PF-M-016): the span is measured from the evening the figure starts at — the beginning day, or the first price's day when the prices begin later — to today. When that evening is on or after the 1Y window's own beginning day (a year or less on the calendar), years = 1; otherwise years = the days from that evening to today ÷ 365. The answer is the total and the years.

MK-PF-F-040.name: returnSincePurchases
MK-PF-F-040.rule: A holding bought inside the period, time-weighted from its purchases. Nothing when there is no price today. Every purchase must have a share count that is a real number, and every purchase of more than zero shares a price paid on record (a cost per share above 0 that is a real number — a stored $0 is not on record), or the answer is nothing. Purchases of zero or fewer shares are skipped. Each purchase is placed on its own date when that date is on record (purchaseDateOnRecord); a purchase with no date on record beside a purchase that has one gives nothing (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3: never put on a guessed day); when no purchase has a date, all are placed on the first day handed in. Purchases on the same day are added together: shares added, and paid = shares × cost per share added. The pieces are purchasePieces. A PURCHASE COUNTS FROM THE START OF ITS DAY (owner decision DEC-4439; 2026-10-21): at each later purchase day the piece before it ends at the shares then held × the close of the PREVIOUS EVENING — the last close on or before the day before, taken only when it falls on or after that piece's own first day; with none, the piece ends at the money it began with. The return = the growth of the pieces before the last × (shares held × today's price) ÷ the money in the last piece − 1. With a single purchase day this is today's value ÷ what was paid − 1. 10 shares at $100, 10 more the next morning at $110, close $121: 2,420 ÷ (1,000 + 1,100) − 1 = +15.24%.

MK-PF-F-042.name: windowTotal
MK-PF-F-042.rule: A holding's return over the whole window, never a yearly rate. When the row carries its window total (even an empty one), that total is the answer as written. Otherwise: nothing when there is no return. When the window is longer than one year (years above 1): (1 + the yearly rate) to the power years, − 1. Otherwise the return itself. MK-PF-F-044.name: startValues
MK-PF-F-044.rule: For each holding row, read its return over the window; a row with no return is left out. A row whose return is above −1 (a loss of less than everything) and whose value today is above zero: its value when the window began = the start the row carries when it is above zero (what buildPerformance read from the shares held when the window began × the close its figure is measured from — 2026-10-21, DEC-1669, DEC-3035b, tenet 4: shares bought inside the window were not held then); for a row that carries none, (today's value + the interest it was paid in the window, a bond's or CD's only — owner decision DEC-6212, 2026-10-19) ÷ (1 + the return), because a bond's return holds that interest. Any other row — worth $0 today, or a return of −1 or worse — is kept at the start the row carries (its start value: what buildPerformance read it was worth when the window began; 2026-10-21, owner decision DEC-5068, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0) when that start is above zero, and left out when it is not. The answer is the list of rows kept, each with its return and its starting value. No rows gives an empty list.

A month or more, the line reads: "Prices for this holding go back {months} month(s), so the {label} figure covers {months} month(s) — not {words}." MK-PF-F-051.name: paidOnRecord
MK-PF-F-051.rule: What was paid = Σ shares × cost per share over the purchases with a cost above 0, × the contract multiplier; it also returns the shares counted and the shares held. All three unknown when a purchase has no share count; what was paid is unknown when shares are held and none has a cost on record.

MK-PF-F-052.name: purchaseDateOnRecord
MK-PF-F-052.rule: A purchase date on record: what is stored, read with spaces at the ends ignored, when it begins with a date written year-month-day and that date is a day the calendar has (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts, the app's one reader of a written day) — the answer is that date; otherwise nothing: no date stored, a date written another way, or a day that does not exist, such as 31 February. Unknown is not a date: a missing date is never read as 1 January 1970 or as today.

MK-PF-F-053.name: isBroadIndexOption
MK-PF-F-053.rule: Whether a holding is an option on a broad-based stock index, whose gain IRS Publication 550 (2025) taxes 60% long-term and 40% short-term however long it was held. False for anything that is not an option. For an option: its ticker is read with spaces at the ends ignored and in capitals; its root is the letters at the start (after a leading $ or ^ when there is one) that are followed by the end of the ticker, a space or a digit; true when that root is one of SPX, SPXW, XSP (the S&P 500), NDX, NDXP (the Nasdaq-100), RUT, MRUT (the Russell 2000), VIX (the volatility index), DJX (the Dow) or OEX, XEO (the S&P 100). An option on SPY or on a single company is false.

MK-PF-F-054.name: latestCloseLookup
MK-PF-F-054.rule: A holding's price today, looked up by its ticker: the ticker is trimmed and put in upper case, and the answer is MK-PF-F-009 latestClose of the price history the app holds for it — the close on the latest date; nothing when the app holds no history for that ticker. It changes no amount. The amber box (MK-XS-F-002, the list of what is missing) is handed this one lookup on Net worth (through MK-NW-F-145 netWorthInputs), on Performance and on the account page, so a holding added by hand with no price today is named on all three or on none.

MK-PF-F-055.name: valueAtClose
MK-PF-F-055.rule: What a holding was worth at the close a window figure is measured from (2026-10-21; owner decision DEC-5068, tenet 4: a known $0 is $0, so a holding worth $0 today keeps the start it lost). The close = closeAsOf: the last close on or before the day handed in (a day written year-month-day is read as written; a moment as the person's own calendar day), or the first close on record when the day handed in is before every price. Nothing when the app holds no prices for it, the day is not one the calendar has, or that close is not above zero. Otherwise the shares held (every purchase's shares added up) × that close × the contract multiplier (contractMultiplier) — marketValue at that close: 0 when no shares are held, nothing when a purchase has no share count.

MK-PF-F-056.name: purchasePieces
MK-PF-F-056.rule: The pieces a holding bought inside the window is measured in (owner decision DEC-1669, time-weighted from its purchases; kept apart 2026-10-21 so the value its return is measured from can be read when it is worth $0 today). Every purchase must have a share count that is a real number, and every purchase of more than zero shares a price paid on record (a cost per share above 0 that is a real number — a stored $0 is not on record), or the answer is nothing. Purchases of zero or fewer shares are skipped. Each purchase is placed on its own date when that date is on record (purchaseDateOnRecord); a purchase with no date beside one that has a date gives nothing (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3); when no purchase has a date, all are placed on the first day handed in. Purchases on the same day are added together: shares added, and paid = shares × cost per share added. Nothing when no purchase is left. Walk the days from earliest to latest, starting with shares held 0, money in the piece 0, growth 1. On the first day: money in the piece = what was paid that day. On each later day (owner decision DEC-4439, 2026-10-21: a purchase counts from the start of its day): nothing if the money in the piece is zero or less; take the last close on or before the day BEFORE it (closeDayOnOrBefore) when that close is dated on or after the piece's own first day — then growth = growth × (shares held × that close) ÷ money in the piece and money in the piece = shares held × that close + what was paid that day; with no such close the piece ends at the money it began with — growth unchanged, money in the piece + what was paid that day. After each day, shares held grows by that day's shares. At the end: nothing when the money in the piece is zero or less; otherwise the answer is the shares held, the money in the last piece and the growth of the pieces before it. With a single purchase day the money in the piece is what was paid and the growth is 1. (Its purchases by day are read by purchaseDays, which the holding's path across the window shares — 2026-10-22.)
