MK-PF-F-057.name: feeNotInPrice
MK-PF-F-057.rule: The fee on a buy or a sale that its price does not already carry, in dollars (2026-10-21): the record's fee when it is a number above zero and the record does not say the fee is inside its price; otherwise 0 — no fee on record, a fee that is not a number or not above zero, or a fee the record says is inside its price.

MK-PF-F-058.name: gainOnPartSentence
MK-PF-F-058.rule: The one line for a gain counted on only part of a holding (owner wording DEC-4643, used for what is still held too). The whole part is its count with the holding's own unit word (quantityWithUnit; the bare count when it has none), followed by the word sold for a sale. When the gain is not known, or no unit has a price paid on record: that whole part, then ; what you paid for them is not on record, so no gain is counted. Otherwise: the gain without its sign in money, then loss when it is below zero and gain otherwise, then on, the units counted, of, the whole part, then ; what you paid for the other (the whole count less the units counted) is not on record. For example: $200 gain on 10 of 20 shares; what you paid for the other 10 is not on record.

MK-PF-F-059.name: dayBeforeDay
MK-PF-F-059.rule: The calendar day before a day written year-month-day, written the same way and counted on the calendar; nothing for a day the calendar does not have.

MK-PF-F-060.name: closeDayOnOrBefore
MK-PF-F-060.rule: The close on or before a day, and the day it is from: of the prices whose date is a real calendar day and whose close is a number, the latest dated on or before that day; nothing when there are no prices, the day is not a calendar day, or none is that early.

MK-PF-F-061.name: firstClose
MK-PF-F-061.rule: The first price on record: of the prices whose date is a real calendar day and whose close is a number, the earliest, whatever order they arrived in; nothing when there is none.

MK-PF-F-062.name: calendarDay
MK-PF-F-062.rule: A day written year-month-day that the calendar has, trimmed; nothing for anything else, so a day that does not exist never rolls into the next month.

MK-PF-F-063.name: heldOnDay
MK-PF-F-063.rule: The part of a holding already held on a day: its purchases dated on or before that day, and those with no date on record; the holding itself when every purchase is kept.

MK-PF-F-064.name: purchasesHeld
MK-PF-F-064.rule: The purchases a holding still holds: every purchase except one whose share count is a known number of 0 or less; a purchase whose count is not on record still counts.

MK-PF-F-065.name: firstDatedPurchase
MK-PF-F-065.rule: The earliest purchase date on record among the purchases a holding still holds; nothing when none has a date.

MK-PF-F-066.name: marketGap
MK-PF-F-066.rule: How far ahead of the market or behind it: your return − the market's, at full precision, above zero ahead; nothing when either is missing or not a number.

MK-PF-F-067.name: purchaseDays
MK-PF-F-067.rule: A holding's purchases by day, oldest first: each purchase of more than 0 shares gives its shares and what was paid (shares × cost per share) on its own date, or on the day handed in when it has none. Nothing when a share count is not a number, a purchase of shares has no price paid on record, or a purchase with no date sits beside dated ones; nothing when there is no purchase.

MK-PF-F-068.name: dayAfterDay
MK-PF-F-068.rule: The calendar day after a day written year-month-day, written the same way.

MK-PF-F-070.name: holdingPath
MK-PF-F-070.rule: One holding's path across the window, on the one list of days money went into or out of any holding built beside it; nothing when no plan is handed in. Read from its own trades when it has them (eventPath). Bought inside the window, from its purchases by day (purchaseDays; none, no path): nothing is held before its first purchase; on each later day, before = the shares held × the latest close on or before the previous evening × the contract multiplier when that close is dated on or after its last purchase day, else the value that piece began with; a purchase day adds what was paid × the multiplier; nothing when a later purchase follows a piece worth 0 or less, or a purchase day is not on the list. Held when the window began, or joining when its prices begin: nothing with neither a start nor a joining day, or no count of the shares held when its figure began; then on each day, before = the shares held × the close on or before the previous evening × the multiplier (0 before it joins and on the day it joins), that day's purchases in and sales out, after = the shares then held × that close; nothing when a close is missing or more is sold than was held. Its start = the value read from its trades, 0 when bought inside the window or joining later, else its start value; its end = its value today plus its interest. The path is kept only when its pieces multiplied give back its own window figure to within one billionth. Its yardstick's closes on the same days are kept with it only when they give back its own market figure: the close the window begins at (none for a holding entering later), each previous evening's close (none before it enters; on the day it enters, that day's close when bought inside the window, else the previous evening's), and today's.

MK-PF-F-071.name: returnSplitAtPurchases
MK-PF-F-071.rule: A return split at every day money went in or out, for the holdings handed in together. Undefined when none is handed in or they are not built on one list of days (the caller then weighs by the starts). Starting from what they were all worth when the window began, on each day of the list the piece ends at what they were all worth before that day's money (their befores added), measured only when what it began with was above 0, and the next begins at what they were worth with it (their afters added); the last ends at what they are worth today with their interest (their ends added). When nothing is held after the last day: the pieces multiplied − 1 when some piece was measured and today's worth is 0, else nothing. Nothing when today's worth is below 0. Otherwise the pieces multiplied × today's worth ÷ what the last piece began with − 1.

MK-PF-F-072.name: tradesAfter
MK-PF-F-072.rule: A holding's own trades after a day, as its account records them. Its account is the one holding it, else the account it names; with no account or no ticker there are no trades. Only that account's records of its ticker with a real calendar date and more than 0 shares count; one dated after today is read on today, and only those after the day handed in count. A sale gives its shares and what it brought in: shares × price × the contract multiplier when a price above 0 is on record, else the cash it moved when that is above 0, less any fee not in the price; unknown with neither. A purchase (bought, an opening position, or a dividend, interest or coupon reinvested) adds its shares to its day, and what was paid = shares × price × the multiplier, that day's unknown once a purchase on it has no price above 0. Sales come oldest first.

MK-PF-F-073.name: sharesThroughWindow
MK-PF-F-073.rule: What a holding held and traded inside its window, after the day handed in. Of the purchases it still holds: one with no share count on record leaves the start unknown; one dated on or before that day was held then; one with no date is placed on the day it was bought inside the window when that is handed in, and otherwise is not counted on any day; the rest are grouped by day with their shares and what was paid (shares × cost per share × the contract multiplier; unknown once one has no price paid on record). Its records' purchases are read too when nothing bought on or before that day is still held and it sold inside the window, or when no purchase carries a date and no day is handed in: on each day, where the records count more shares than the purchases, the records' count stands, and what was paid = the purchases' paid + the records' paid for the shares beyond them; where they count fewer on a day on or before the last sale, that day's paid and the start are not known. Each sale adds its shares and what it brought in to its day (unknown once one is unknown). Start = today's shares − every share bought since + every share sold since; nothing when that is unknown or below zero.

MK-PF-F-074.name: marketSplitAtPurchases
MK-PF-F-074.rule: The market on the same days, with the same weights, as the return beside it. Undefined when none is handed in, a holding lacks its yardstick's closes on every day of its path (one more at each end), or they are not on one list of days. The first piece weighs each holding by what it was worth when the window began, each later piece by what it was worth once that day's money was in. In each piece whose weights add to more than 0, each holding with a weight above 0 moves by its yardstick's close at the piece's end ÷ its close at the piece's start (undefined when either is missing or the start close is not above 0); a sale is carried on the day after it, so the shares sold leave at the sale day's own close with the rest (eventDays, 2026-10-23); the piece's growth = the weighted moves added ÷ the weights added. The answer = the pieces' growths multiplied − 1.

MK-PF-F-075.name: soldOutPositions
MK-PF-F-075.rule: The holdings sold in full inside the window: for each account handed in that holds one of the positions handed in, or holds none, every ticker it sold (a sale of more than 0 shares, dated after the day handed in, a date after today read as today) that it no longer holds, in ticker order. Each becomes a holding with no purchases, marked sold out, naming its account, carrying what the same ticker is in any account handed in (its kind, class, the class's source, the broker's type, its cash flag, label, name and multiplier), or else a stock or fund in a stocks-and-funds account and a bond in a bonds account, and nothing said otherwise.

MK-PF-F-076.name: firstEvent
MK-PF-F-076.rule: The first day a holding read from its trades bought or sold anything: the earliest day with shares bought or sold above 0; nothing when there is none.

MK-PF-F-077.name: eventPath
MK-PF-F-077.rule: A holding's path read from its own purchases and sales, on the list of days, starting from what the shares held when the window began were worth. A sale is handed in on the day after it (eventDays, 2026-10-23), so it counts at the end of its own day. On each day while it holds shares, before = the shares held × the latest close on or before the previous evening × the contract multiplier when that close is dated on or after the day the piece began, else the value the piece began with; with nothing held it is 0. On a trade day: nothing when a purchase has no price paid on record, or a sale has no amount on record, sells while nothing is held, or sells more than is held; the part sold = the shares sold ÷ the shares held, at most all of them; the piece ends at the part kept at that evening's value plus what the sale brought in; after = the part kept at that evening's value plus what was paid; the shares held move by those bought less those sold, and the next piece begins there. Its start = the value when the window began; its end = the value handed in.

MK-PF-F-078.name: yardstickOn
MK-PF-F-078.rule: A holding's yardstick on the days of its path, each read as the close on or before a day: first the close the window begins at, none for a holding that enters later or when no beginning day is handed in; then for each day of the list, none before the holding enters, on the day it enters that day's own close for a holding bought inside the window and otherwise the previous evening's, and on every other day the previous evening's; then today's latest close. Each of these closes is read however old (closeAsOfInside): they are days inside the window, not its start (R19b).

MK-PF-F-079.name: eventDays
MK-PF-F-079.rule: The days a holding's trades count on: a purchase of more than 0 shares counts on its own day, a sale of more than 0 shares on the day after it. On one day the shares bought add up and what was paid adds up, and the shares sold and what they brought in add up likewise; one amount not on record leaves that day's amount unknown.

MK-PF-F-080.name: recordedBuysExplain
MK-PF-F-080.rule: Whether a holding's dated purchases after the given day are all the account's own recorded buys. Every purchase of the holding dated after that day is read, grouped by its day: if any of them has an unknown share count, no. At least one such day must exist. Then, on each such day, the shares those purchases hold must be no more than the shares the account's buy records of that ticker bought that day. Yes only when all of that holds; buildPerformance then reads an undated purchase beside them as held before them.

MK-ST-F-080.name: isDay
MK-ST-F-080.rule: True only when the value is text written exactly as four digits, a dash, two digits, a dash and two digits (year-month-day) AND that day exists in the calendar (2026-02-29 and 2026-02-31 are false; 2024-02-29 is true). Anything else is false: a number, nothing at all, or a date with a time written after it.

MK-ST-F-081.name: timeWeightedReturn
MK-ST-F-081.rule: Works from the daily record, which holds one value per account per day, taken after that day's money moved; the previous usable day stands for the evening before. Days after the last day asked for, and days not written as year-month-day (isDay), are ignored. Each measured account has its own line of values, from its first recorded day to its last. The total on a day = the values that day of the measured accounts whose line covers that day. An account that has ever held a priced security must have a value on that very day, or the day is not used at all; any other account (a typed or cash balance) keeps its last earlier value until its next one. THE BEGINNING = the latest recorded day on or before the start day whose total can be formed with at least one account in it; with none it refuses (the start is not recorded). The last day asked for must be in the record and its total formed, or it refuses (the end is not recorded). It refuses when a deposit or withdrawal on a measured account that is not cash has no year-month-day date, when shares were moved on any day after the beginning up to the last day (naming the first such day), and when a deposit, withdrawal or transfer with no amount on record is dated after the beginning up to the last day (naming the first such day), and when interest, a dividend or a coupon with no amount on record is on a measured account, cash or not, dated after the beginning up to the last day (naming the first such day and its kind — 2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3), and when a record the app could not name sits on a measured account that is not cash, dated after the beginning up to the last day (naming the first such day, the broker's word for it and its amount). A VALUE BELOW ZERO (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 1): when the beginning's total, or any later usable day's total, is below minus half a cent, it refuses, naming that day (the value is below $0) — never read as $0. THE PIECES: from the beginning, take each later usable day in order. Money in on that day, account by account: an account there now but not on the previous usable day joined the record: it brings in the money added to it that day when there is any (it was worth nothing the evening before, so that money is its base — DEC-4439), otherwise its whole value; one there before but not now takes out its last value (it left); a cash account brings in its change in value less the interest credited to it after the previous usable day up to this day (cash earns only interest); any other account brings in its deposits (plus) and withdrawals (minus) dated after the previous usable day up to this day, and if one of those is dated before this day it refuses, naming that day (money moved on a day with no recorded value). THE DAY'S LINK (owner decision DEC-4439, 2026-10-11: money that moves on a day counts for that whole day): the base = the previous usable day's total + money in. When the base is more than half a cent, the growth so far is multiplied by this day's total (a total within half a cent below zero read as zero) ÷ the base, and the measured period starts at the previous day if it has not started yet — or at this day when the previous total was half a cent or less (the first money's day). When the base is half a cent or less: if it is below minus half a cent, or this day's total is more than half a cent either way, it refuses, naming the day (nothing to grow from), and says when more was taken out than the previous total plus the money added; otherwise nothing is measured for that piece. When no piece was measured it refuses (nothing invested). THE RETURN = the pieces multiplied together − 1, as a share at full precision (not a percent, and never turned into a yearly rate here), with the day the measured period started. It never falls back to another method. ALONG WITH IT, THE PIECES BETWEEN THE DAYS MONEY MOVED: a new piece starts on each day money went in or out by more than half a cent — the piece before it ends the evening before — and each piece's growth is its days' links multiplied together, less 1; a piece with no link measured is not listed. The pieces come back in order, each with its first and last day, and multiplied together (1 + each) less 1 they are the return. A refusal has no pieces.

MK-ST-F-082.name: movementsOf
MK-ST-F-082.rule: Sorts a household's records, for the accounts being measured, into money moving in or out, interest, and days shares were moved. Each record's date is its first ten characters. A deposit or withdrawal on a measured account with NO amount (missing or not a number) is not money in or out at all: its day goes on the list of days with an amount missing, and the return refuses there; the same for a transfer with no amount that crosses the edge of the measured accounts (one side measured, the other not). That list is handed back only when it has a day on it. Interest, a dividend or a coupon on a measured account with no amount (missing or not a number) is not counted at all: its day and kind go on the list of earnings with no amount, handed back only when it has one, and the return refuses there (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3: unknown is not zero). Any other missing or unreadable amount counts as zero. Every amount is read by the one rule for a stored amount (2026-10-21): when the record says which way the money went (in or out), its amount without a sign, that way; otherwise its kind's own way with the sign it was stored with — a deposit plus, a withdrawal minus, so a withdrawal written as a negative amount becomes money in and a deposit written as a negative amount (a reversal) money out. A deposit on a measured account is that money in, a withdrawal that money out; a deposit the broker sent with a minus is stored saying it went out, and is money out. A transfer is money out of its first account when that account is measured, and money into its second account when that one is measured, so a transfer between two measured accounts appears as both. Shares moved (a transfer in kind): nothing when both accounts named are measured, or neither is, or when only one account is named and it is not measured. Otherwise it is money into or out of the measured account at what the shares were worth — the record's amount when above zero, else shares × price: in when they arrive in the measured account (or, with one account named, when the record says in), out when they leave (or the record says out). When the direction is neither in nor out, or the worth is not above zero, the day goes on the list of days shares were moved instead. A transfer that names only one account and says which way it went (a broker's journal, in or out) is money into that account when it says in and money out when it says out, when that account is measured. Interest on a measured account that was not reinvested is interest (its amount, read by the same rule). A record the app could not name (a record carrying the broker's own word for an activity the app does not know, with an amount or shares) on a measured account goes on the list of records not named, with its day, that word and its amount without a sign; that list is handed back only when it has one on it. Every other kind of record is ignored. Each movement keeps its own day; the time-weighted return counts it for that whole day (DEC-4439, 2026-10-11).

MK-CF-F-286.name: monthBeforeAnyRecord
MK-CF-F-286.rule: True when the month shown comes before anything was recorded: no saved month-end record, no income and no expense is dated in it or in an earlier month (each date read as its local day's year and month), or nothing is recorded at all. False otherwise.

MK-NW-F-186.name: accruedFrequencyAssumed
MK-NW-F-186.rule: One sentence — 'How often it pays is not entered, so the estimate takes it as once a year.' — said only where the interest built up is an estimate (accruedInterestCaveat gives its note) and how often the bond pays, once or twice a year, is not entered. Nothing otherwise.

MK-CF-F-287.name: isRecordOfLot
MK-CF-F-287.rule: Whether an opening record was written for this purchase: by the purchase's identifier when the record carries one; otherwise — a record written before the identifier was stored — when the record's date, shares and price paid are exactly the purchase's own.

MK-CF-F-288.name: openingRecordsHeld
MK-CF-F-288.rule: A holding's own opening records in one account: the records of purchases already owned, typed or imported, never a linked account's; matched to the holding by its identifier when the record carries one, otherwise by its ticker, capitals ignored.

MK-CF-F-289.name: purchaseRecordsFollowEdit
MK-CF-F-289.rule: The records once the holding editor is saved: a purchase added gets its opening record (openingRecordsOf); a purchase changed has its record's date, shares and price paid rewritten from it, and the record takes the purchase's identifier; a purchase removed has its record removed. Each record serves one purchase (isRecordOfLot, among openingRecordsHeld). Records of buys and sales are never touched.

MK-CF-F-290.name: purchaseRecordsAfterHoldingRemoved
MK-CF-F-290.rule: The records once a holding is deleted: its opening records in that account (openingRecordsHeld) are removed — except a record naming only a ticker that another holding still in the account also has; every other record, buys and sales included, stays.

MK-CF-F-291.name: purchaseRecordsFollowReimport
MK-CF-F-291.rule: The records once a holdings file is imported again into an account, holding by holding: with no record of that ticker in the account, its opening records are written (openingRecordsOf); with buys and sales only, nothing is added; with opening records, those are removed and one record is written for the shares the file holds less the shares the account's own buys less sales explain, at the price paid of the file's first purchase — none when that leaves no shares, and the file's purchases as they are when its share count is not on record (totalShares). Buys and sales are kept.

MK-CF-F-292.name: optionTradesOnTheWayIn
MK-CF-F-292.rule: Once, as records come into the store: each buy or sale typed by hand, on an account built by hand, with no shares-per-contract on it, for a holding traded in contracts (tradeMultiplierOf gives more than one share a contract), with shares and a price on it, takes that multiplier; where the account keeps its own cash figure, the cash moves by what it should have moved and did not — shares × price × (the multiplier less one), out for a buy, in for a sale. Every other record, and a linked account's cash, is left as it is; the number of records changed is handed back beside them.

MK-PF-F-081.name: heldQuantity
MK-PF-F-081.rule: A quantity as held: its whole part with a comma between each three digits, its decimals exactly as held — never cut or rounded — and a minus sign kept.

MK-PF-F-082.name: priceOnRecord
MK-PF-F-082.rule: A holding's own price on record — its last price, the broker's mark or the price typed — when that is a number of zero or more; nothing otherwise.

MK-PF-F-083.name: paidPerShare
MK-PF-F-083.rule: What was paid a share over every purchase: the price paid on record (paidOnRecord) ÷ (the shares held × the shares in one contract, contractMultiplier) — only when every share held has a price paid on record; nothing when a purchase has no price paid or no share count.

MK-PF-F-084.name: ownMark
MK-PF-F-084.rule: A holding's own mark where no close is on record: its price on record (priceOnRecord); else the price its value was last built at — its value ÷ (its shares, totalShares, × the shares in one contract, contractMultiplier) — when the value is a number and shares are on record; nothing otherwise.

MK-PF-F-085.name: statedCdRate
MK-PF-F-085.rule: The yearly rate a CD held as a holding states: for an individual bond or CD (isIndividualBondOrCD) whose own name or ticker and kind make it a CD (bondInfo), the coupon rate entered when it is a number of zero or more — zero is a rate; nothing for anything else, or for a rate never entered.

MK-CF-F-293.name: over65Shown
MK-CF-F-293.rule: Who is 65 or older, as the filing question shows it: the answer on record (just me, both, or neither); else just me when this year less the person's birth year is 65 or more; else nothing chosen — the spouse's age is never asked.

MK-CF-F-295.name: debtLoad
MK-CF-F-295.rule: What the debts weigh against the income, for the Debts tab. Debt-to-income, given only when a debt is entered and the income before tax is above zero: the minimum payments a month (minimumDebtService) against the income before tax a month — the year's gross (totalGrossAnnual) ÷ 12 — read by debtToIncome, for a homeowner when any debt is a mortgage. The student loans, given only when something was borrowed: the amounts borrowed added up; each loan with a rate and a term above zero adds its monthly repayment and its total interest (loanPayment); the repayment's share of the income before tax a month, nothing when that income is zero. A typed figure that is not a number counts as zero. The amount borrowed is the setup loans owed today and not yet in Debts (setupStudentLoans), so a loan that starts later is not counted. The student loans now take every setup loan not already in Debts, owed or starting later (setupLoansSplit); when none is owed yet and some start later, the month the first one starts is handed back too. The amount borrowed is every setup loan, owed or later, whether or not it is in Debts; and it says whether all of them are already debts in Debts (as a debt).

MK-CF-F-297.name: freqNotRecognised
MK-CF-F-297.rule: Whether an earner's pay frequency is one the pay-frequency table does not hold, so the year's pay is no figure and the refusal is said instead.

MK-CF-F-299.name: setupStudentLoans
MK-CF-F-299.rule: The student loans entered in setup that are owed today and not yet a debt in Debts (setupLoansNotEntered): their amounts added up, and how many there are.

MK-CF-F-300.name: loanStartsOn
MK-CF-F-300.rule: A setup loan's first month paid out: the earliest of its months, each one to twelve, in its year, written year-month; nothing when the months or the year are not entered.

MK-CF-F-301.name: setupLoansSplit
MK-CF-F-301.rule: The setup loans not already in Debts (setupLoansAll), split at this month: owed — a first month paid out on or before this month, or none entered; later — a first month after this month.

MK-CF-F-302.name: setupLoanSentences
MK-CF-F-302.rule: One sentence for each setup loan that starts later — its amount and name, the month and year it starts, not counted until then — then one for each owed loan with no start month entered, saying it counts as owed today. A loan named only 'student loan' is not named twice.

MK-CF-F-303.name: setupLoansNotEntered
MK-CF-F-303.rule: The setup loans owed today and not already in Debts: the owed part of setupLoansSplit.

MK-CF-F-304.name: setupLoansAll
MK-CF-F-304.rule: Every student loan entered in setup with an amount above zero that is not already a debt in Debts. A debt is the loan's when it carries that loan's place in the list; failing that, an unmatched student-loan debt whose name is the loan's (capitals and punctuation ignored) or whose balance is the loan's amount, rounded to the dollar. Each loan keeps its place, name, amount, rate and term when above zero, and its first month paid out (loanStartsOn).

MK-CF-F-305.name: setupLoanDebts
MK-CF-F-305.rule: Each setup loan owed today and not in Debts (setupLoansNotEntered), as a student-loan debt: its amount as the balance, its rate when entered, and its monthly payment from the rate and term when both are entered (loanPayment) — no payment otherwise; marked with the loan's place in the setup list. Each is named with '(from setup)' after its name, carries no monthly payment, and is marked as having no repayment start known.

MK-CF-F-306.name: payFrequencyOf
MK-CF-F-306.rule: A pay frequency as the screens read it: nothing saved, or blank, is monthly; anything else is itself.

MK-CF-F-307.name: isPayFrequency
MK-CF-F-307.rule: Whether a pay frequency (payFrequencyOf) is one of the five in the pay-frequency table.

MK-CF-F-308.name: payPeriodsAYear
MK-CF-F-308.rule: Pay periods a year for a frequency, from the one pay-frequency table (isPayFrequency); nothing for a frequency the table does not hold.

MK-CF-F-309.name: periodsOf
MK-CF-F-309.rule: Pay periods a year for a profile's wage: paid by the hour, the hours a week entered × 52 — nothing when no hours are entered; otherwise the table's periods for its frequency (payPeriodsAYear).

MK-CF-F-310.name: repairHourlyTakeHome
MK-CF-F-310.rule: Once, on a profile saved before the fix: a wage paid by the hour, saved as a gross worked back from a take-home, whose gross a month is still the one the old migration made (to within half a cent) — that gross, from the take-home a month × 12 plus the year's 401(k), grossed up at the rate typed or else through the tax tables — goes back to the take-home typed, and the take-home is converted again with the hours (convertTakeHomeMode). Any other profile is left as it is.

MK-CF-F-311.name: PAY_FREQUENCIES
MK-CF-F-311.rule: The one pay-frequency table: pay periods a year — hourly 2,080, weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, annually 1.

MK-PF-F-086.name: staleStartClose
MK-PF-F-086.rule: The close a window cannot start from: the last close on or before the day (closeDayOnOrBefore) when it is more than START_CLOSE_DAYS calendar days before it, with its day; nothing when that close is near enough, or there is none. A series of values the person typed, marked as typed by hand is never too old: nothing (R19a).

MK-PF-F-087.name: START_CLOSE_DAYS
MK-PF-F-087.rule: The longest a window's start may reach back for its close: 7 calendar days. It is for market closes only; values typed by hand have no limit.

MK-PF-F-088.name: valuedByYouWords
MK-PF-F-088.rule: For a series of values the person typed, marked as typed by hand: the words 'valued by you on' and the day of the last value on or before the start (closeDayOnOrBefore), as the screen writes a day; nothing for a market series, or with no value before the start.

MK-CF-F-313.name: wageRefusalOf
MK-CF-F-313.rule: The refusal for a wage entered that cannot be read, for the person and for a partner who earns: a wage typed above zero whose pay frequency is not in the one table gives 'Pay frequency not recognised — open Base pay to choose one.'; one paid by the hour with no hours a week entered gives 'Hours a week not entered — your hourly pay is not counted until it is.'; otherwise nothing.

MK-PF-F-089.name: closeAsOfInside
MK-PF-F-089.rule: The close for a day inside a window: the last close on or before it (closeOnOrBefore), however old, else the first close on record (firstClose); nothing with no prices. The limit on how old a close may be is for a window's start only (R19b).

MK-PF-F-090.name: staleWindowStart
MK-PF-F-090.rule: For a window: the close it would start from, with its day, when that close is too old (staleStartClose, read on the evening before the window's first day, startDateFor); nothing when the window has no start or its start close is near enough.

MK-NW-F-187.name: heldBondInterest
MK-NW-F-187.rule: The bonds and CDs held inside an account, each with the year of interest it pays, by the one bond rule (DEC-2748c: face × rate). An account that is itself a bond is read whole elsewhere: nothing here. For each holding that is an individual bond or CD (isIndividualBondOrCD): its face is the face entered, else, quoted per $100 of face, its quantity; it is read by bondInfo and yearlyInterestNow on its own face, rate and maturity. Matured (isPastMaturity): it pays nothing. No rate, or no face: the year is not known, and the reason says which.

figures_checked_by_hand.2748: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-2748c that this rule follows

MK-CF-F-316.name: bondWhy
MK-CF-F-316.rule: The words beside a bond's interest line: the rate (asPercent) 'coupon on' the face; the rate 'on' the balance; or, with no face, the rate 'coupon — face value not entered, so' and the words handed in.

MK-CF-F-315.name: debtsEntered
MK-CF-F-315.rule: Whether any debt is entered: a debt in Debts, or a student loan entered in setup that is not already one, owed or starting later (setupLoansSplit).

MK-CF-F-314.name: setupEntered
MK-CF-F-314.rule: Whether anything is entered for the month, part by part, so the set-up doors show only when nothing is: pay read (a wage read, salaryAnnual above zero, a monthly pay table, self-employment, or retirement income); the wage refusal (wageRefusalOf); an inflow (pay read, a refused wage, retirement income now, a logged income, or any source the income summary counts, incomeSummary); an expense logged; a budget (the planned monthly expenses of the budget as counted, theBudgetCounted, above zero); a debt (debtsEntered, or debts from the sign-up answers, debtsFromOnboarding); and entered when any of inflow, expense, budget or debt is.

MK-NW-F-188.name: howReturnCalculated
MK-NW-F-188.rule: How the Return was calculated, in words, from the pieces the time-weighted return is made of: nothing when there are no pieces or no Return. One piece: no money went in or out, so Return is how much the value changed, then the Return. Two to four pieces: money went in or out on (pieces − 1) days, the count and its word written by plural, so the dates are split there into that many pieces, then each piece's growth in order, then the words multiplied together before rounding and the Return. Five or more: the same opening, then each piece's growth is measured and the pieces are multiplied together, before rounding, to make the Return. Every percent is written by the caller's writer.

MK-CF-F-318.name: biggestOutLine
MK-CF-F-318.rule: The biggest amount going out of a month, as its row prints it: of the month's rows, only those going out are read — not the money coming in, not a row not set, not a payment not entered, and only where the printed amount is below zero; the one with the most negative printed amount wins, the first of equal ones kept. It gives that row's name and its printed amount; nothing when no row goes out.

MK-NW-F-229.name: dayOrNull
MK-NW-F-229.rule: A date as a row keeps it. Anything that is not text gives nothing. The text, with spaces at its ends cut off, must be four digits, a dash, two digits, a dash, two digits, optionally followed by a time part that starts with T; anything else gives nothing. The day is the first 10 characters. It is read as year, month and day, and must be a day that exists on the calendar: the year, month and day of that calendar day must come back exactly as written. A real day is returned as written; otherwise nothing.

MK-NW-F-230.name: wasGiven
MK-NW-F-230.rule: Whether a text was given at all: yes only when the value is text and, with spaces at its ends cut off, is not empty. A missing value, a number, or text of only spaces gives no.

MK-NW-F-231.name: instantOf
MK-NW-F-231.rule: The moment a time-stamp names, as a count of milliseconds, read with its own time zone so two stamps written in different time zones are put in their true order. A time-stamp that cannot be read counts as moment 0, the earliest possible.

MK-NW-F-232.name: oneHoldingSpelling
MK-NW-F-232.rule: One spelling for a holding: a missing name, or a name of only spaces, gives nothing. Otherwise the name with spaces at its ends cut off, in capital letters, so a lower-case and an upper-case spelling are one holding.

MK-NW-F-233.name: addRows
MK-NW-F-233.rule: Saves new rows after the rows already on record, which are kept unchanged. Numbering starts from the larger of the number of rows on record and the highest row number on record (a row number that is not a number counts as 0); each new row gets the next number up, one by one. Every new row is stamped with the one save time given. For each new row: if it names a row to replace, that row must be one that stands today (the same reading as MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce, over the record including rows already added in this save), or the save stops with a message that nothing can replace it; and if the row it replaces was typed by the account holder, the new row must also be typed, or the save stops. The holding name is put in its one spelling (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling). The date is read as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull reads it; the settlement date is read the same way, except a missing settlement date stays missing as given. On a purchase, a sale or a transfer, shares given with a minus sign are saved as the same number without it. Where a date (or settlement date) was given but cannot be read as a day, the date is left blank and the text given is kept beside it (judged given by MK-NW-F-230 wasGiven). A value row that does not replace another is put in a set of values: the account's own value row (no holding) starts a new set named by its own row number, and each holding's value row after it in the same save joins the latest set started for that account; a holding's value row with no account value row before it in this save stops the save with a message. The answer is the full record with the new rows at the end.

MK-NW-F-234.name: rowsInForce
MK-NW-F-234.rule: The rows that count today: every row whose number no other row names as the row it replaces, and that is not itself marked as a removal. A row is dropped from the answer the moment any row in the record names it as replaced, whatever that row's own standing.

MK-NW-F-235.name: firstRowOf
MK-NW-F-235.rule: Builds a lookup that, given a row number, finds the row it began as: start at the row with that number, and while it names a row it replaces that is on record, step to that row; a row already visited stops the stepping, so a loop of corrections cannot run forever. Gives the row reached, or nothing when the row number is not on record.

MK-NW-F-236.name: rowAsItStands
MK-NW-F-236.rule: The row that stands today for a row number, however many times it was corrected. First the row it began as is found (the same reading as MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf); where the number is not on record the answer is nothing. Otherwise, among the rows in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce), the first one whose own beginning is that same row is the answer; where none is in force (it was taken away) the answer is nothing.

MK-NW-F-237.name: sameNumber
MK-NW-F-237.rule: Whether two amounts are the same. When either is missing, they are the same only when both are missing. Otherwise they are the same when the size of their difference is no more than EPS (one billionth).

MK-NW-F-238.name: sortArriving
MK-NW-F-238.rule: Sorts what arrives from a broker or a file into rows to save and events to ask the account holder about. First, keys: an event (a purchase, sale, dividend, interest payment, deposit, withdrawal, transfer, fee, split or other broker word, that does not replace a row) with a readable date and no key of its own is given a key made of its source, kind, date, holding, shares without a minus sign, price, amount, account reached and whether it arrives, plus its count among rows alike in this delivery for that account (so two alike in one delivery are two). The record already holds an account and key where some row carries it and either a row in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) carries it or no row of the account holder's that takes a row away (typed by the account holder, not by an answer) carries it; a key that only rows the account holder took away still carry counts as not held, so the row goes on to the later steps. A row whose account and key the record already holds is not saved: where the row standing for it today is not typed by the account holder, not taken away, and the arriving row now carries another date, other shares, another price, or (on a split) another ratio, it becomes a question (why: ratio, else date, else price) unless that question was already answered (the answers of MK-NW-F-269 eventAnswers); otherwise it is dropped silently. A row with no key, or a new key, goes on. Next, each remaining event that matches an event on record from another source (MK-NW-F-270 sameEventElsewhere), on the same day and, where it has shares, at the same price, is left out and that record row is claimed. Last, for each remaining row in order: for an event with a readable date, if no in-force match on the same day exists and a match is among rows the account holder took away (removed by a typed row, not by an answer about a list, and not first typed by the account holder), it is a question (why: taken away), asked only if not already answered and if the account holder has not already answered "mine is correct" to a list's question about that purchase taken away for this account, holding and day (MK-NW-F-294 removalKept); either way it is not saved. Otherwise, matches from another source: if any was already answered mine, or this arriving event was answered mine before (by MK-NW-F-268 arrivingKey), it is left out unasked; if any match's difference was already answered about a list (MK-NW-F-266 listAnswered), it is left out; if a match not yet answered exists, that row is claimed and it is a question (why: price when on the same day, else date). Then a correction from the same source: an in-force row not claimed and not sent again under its key in this delivery, of the same source, account, kind, holding, day and shares at another price, and with no other row of this delivery matching it exactly, is claimed and becomes a price question if not already answered; either way the row is not saved. For a transfer with a holding and shares: against the record plus the rows chosen to save so far, if this row reports shares arriving and a transfer of the same holding and shares, within NEARBY_DAYS (five days, by MK-NW-F-267 daysFromOneDateToAnother) and naming this account as the one reached, is already there, it is left out; if this row names the account reached and that account already holds a matching arrival not typed by the account holder, a row taking that arrival away is saved first. Every row not left out is saved. The answer is the rows to save and the questions.

MK-NW-F-239.name: rowsNotYetSaved
MK-NW-F-239.rule: The rows not yet in the record: exactly the rows to save that MK-NW-F-238 sortArriving gives for the same record and arriving rows; its questions are dropped.

MK-NW-F-240.name: placedOn
MK-NW-F-240.rule: Where a row sits in time: its own date where it has one; otherwise the day part (the first 10 characters) of the time it was saved. Only the order of reading uses this; the row's date stays blank.

MK-NW-F-241.name: valueRows
MK-NW-F-241.rule: The rows for one account's values on one day, to be saved together. First, one value row for the account itself with no holding: its amount is the uninvested cash, with the broker's stated total and a typed value beside it, each blank where not given. Then one value row per holding listed, in the order listed, each with the holding's name, shares, price, and its value as the amount (blank where not given), and the price's own day where one is given. Every row carries the same account, date and source. With no holdings given, only the account's own row.

MK-NW-F-242.name: valueBatchesOf
MK-NW-F-242.rule: Every set of values saved for one account, read from the value rows in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce), so a corrected row is read in its place. One set per account value row with no holding. Its holdings are the in-force holding value rows carrying the same set number, each with shares, price, value (the row's amount) and price day, blank where not given. Cash is the account row's amount and the typed value is its typed value. The set's number is the account row's set number, or its own row number where it has none. Its date and source are the account row's; its save time is the save time of the row it began as (MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf). It is marked typed when any row of the set was typed by the account holder. Its total is blank where any holding's value is blank, or where both cash and the typed value are blank; otherwise cash (blank counts as 0) plus the typed value (blank counts as 0) plus every holding's value.

MK-NW-F-244.name: valuesNow
MK-NW-F-244.rule: What the screens show today for one account: of every set of values (MK-NW-F-242 valueBatchesOf), the one that wins when they are compared two at a time by the rule for which set to read (of two sets: a dated one wins over an undated one; the later date wins; on one date, one given by a broker, a file or the account holder wins over the price feed's, then one the account holder typed wins, then the later save time as MK-NW-F-231 instantOf reads it, then the higher set number). With no sets, nothing.

MK-NW-F-245.name: valuesLastGiven
MK-NW-F-245.rule: The latest values given by a broker, a file or the account holder for one account, never the price feed's: the sets of values (MK-NW-F-242 valueBatchesOf) whose source is linked, file or typed, compared two at a time by the rule for which set to read (of two sets: a dated one wins over an undated one; the later date wins; on one date, one given by a broker, a file or the account holder wins over the price feed's, then one the account holder typed wins, then the later save time as MK-NW-F-231 instantOf reads it, then the higher set number). With none, nothing.

MK-NW-F-246.name: valuesOn
MK-NW-F-246.rule: What an account was worth on one day: the sets of values (MK-NW-F-242 valueBatchesOf) dated exactly that day, compared two at a time by the rule for which set to read (of two sets: a dated one wins over an undated one; the later date wins; on one date, one given by a broker, a file or the account holder wins over the price feed's, then one the account holder typed wins, then the later save time as MK-NW-F-231 instantOf reads it, then the higher set number). Undated sets belong to no day. With none, nothing.

MK-NW-F-247.name: valuesThatDiffer
MK-NW-F-247.rule: On one day, a value the account holder typed and a later differing one from a broker or a file, handed back as pairs to ask about. Of the account's sets of values (MK-NW-F-242 valueBatchesOf), the typed ones with a date are kept only where no other typed set on the same date was saved later. For each such typed set, every set that is not typed, is given by a broker, a file or the account holder, has the same date, was saved later (moments by MK-NW-F-231 instantOf), and whose total differs (MK-NW-F-237 sameNumber, so a blank total against a known one differs) is paired with it, unless the account holder already answered that pair: an in-force typed fact row of this account whose values-answered note names the typed set and the given set. The answer is every such pair; with none, an empty list.

MK-NW-F-248.name: answerValuesQuestion
MK-NW-F-248.rule: The rows to save for the account holder's answer about a typed set of values and a broker's set (the pair named by both set numbers). If the record is given, the latest in-force answer to this pair was theirs, and the answer now is mine: a typed fact row noting the pair and the answer mine, then the account holder's own values of that day saved again as typed (MK-NW-F-241 valueRows, with the typed set's date, cash, stated total, typed value and holdings). Otherwise, if the record is given and the pair is no longer a difference (read by MK-NW-F-247 valuesThatDiffer over the record without any fact rows that answer this pair), nothing is saved. Otherwise a typed fact row with no date noting the pair and the answer; with the answer mine, that row alone; with the answer theirs, that row followed by the broker's figures of that day saved as typed by the account holder (MK-NW-F-241 valueRows with the given set's date, cash, stated total, typed value and holdings).

MK-NW-F-250.name: statedTotalGap
MK-NW-F-250.rule: The broker's own stated total minus the total the set's rows add up to. Blank where either the stated total or the added-up total is blank.

MK-NW-F-251.name: oldestLotFirst
MK-NW-F-251.rule: The order purchases are listed and sold in. Dates are compared as written, with a missing date counted as empty text, so a purchase with no date comes before every dated one; then the older date first. On the same date (or both undated), the one whose first row number is lower comes first.

MK-NW-F-252.name: walkHolding
MK-NW-F-252.rule: Walks one holding (in its one spelling, MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling) through every account. Events read: in-force rows (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) of that holding that are a split, a purchase, a sale, or a transfer with more than 0 shares. Each event's day is its date; an undated purchase counts as empty text, so it is first; any other undated event takes the day of the save of the row it began as. Where a last day is given, events after it are skipped. Order: by day; on one day a split, then purchases, then transfers, then sales; then by the number of the row each began as. A purchase becomes a lot with its shares (blank counts as 0), price, date, the first date it was given with, its source, the day a list said it was still held, a split count of 1, and whether it was first typed by the account holder; a purchase from a broker's history that a list already counts is kept aside as shown, not held. A split with a ratio (blank counts as 1; 0 or less is skipped) multiplies the shares and split count and divides the price of every held or shown lot in that account whose starting day is before the split's day: the day it arrived by transfer, else the day a list said it was still held, else for a lot the account holder entered with a date before the day it was entered the entry day, else its date, else the entry day. A transfer that reports shares arriving from outside adds a lot of those shares with no date, its price only where given, arriving that day. A sale or a transfer out takes its shares (blank counts as 0) as follows. First, from each purchase it names, up to the named shares and what is left, only pieces of that purchase in this account dated by the sale's day. Next, where rows of that holding that were taken away list shares of this sale to be asked about (added up over every such row, by the row the sale began as), and some of the sale is left: the shares asked are the smaller of what is left and those listed shares; of them, as many as the held lots of this account arrived or dated by the sale's day still have free (not yet taken by this sale, less the shares already waiting in this account, never below 0) wait for the account holder's answer, when more than EPS; the rest of the shares asked are counted beyond the record, and none of the shares asked are sold from another purchase. Then, for what is left: from the shown history lots of this account dated by the sale's day whose list is not before the sale (a sale on the list's own day is read as already in the list), oldest first (MK-NW-F-251 oldestLotFirst), only shares that list no longer states; a lot an answer kept to show is used only by a sale saved after it or one it names. Then the held lots that could have been sold: in this account, arrived or dated by the sale's day, not on a list dated on or after the sale, with shares not yet taken. If none could and the sale is before a list: where more than one listed lot dated by the sale's day exists and one has no date, the rest wait for the account holder's answer; where one or more exist, the oldest is named as sold from and its shares sold before the list grow by the rest, which counts as attributed; with none, the rest are counted as before the list. Else, if more than one lot could and one has no date, and either shares already wait for an answer in this account or the rest is less than all shares free (less EPS), the rest, up to the free shares less those waiting, waits for an answer. Else the lots are taken oldest first, never taking shares already waiting. Taken shares leave their lots; on a transfer to another account they arrive there as the same purchases, with their dates and prices, arriving that day, and any shares not found plus waiting shares arrive there as a lot with no date. For each sale or transfer out it records the lots taken from (named first), the shares beyond the record (what is left plus the shares asked that could not wait, when over EPS), the shares waiting, the shares before the list and the shares attributed. It returns the lots with more than EPS shares, those records, and every lot.

MK-NW-F-263.name: sharesThatDisagree

MK-NW-F-273.name: answerEventQuestion
MK-NW-F-273.rule: The account holder's answer about an arriving event ('theirs', 'mine' or 'both'), as rows to save. The record is optional; none counts as an empty one. FIRST, with a record, where the answer is 'mine', the last answer saved for this pair (MK-NW-F-269 eventAnswers) was 'theirs', and the event on record still stands (MK-NW-F-236 rowAsItStands): two rows. One is that row again with the date, price and amount the event on record had when the question was asked (and its ratio, where it had one), saved as typed, replacing the row as it stands, marked as changing the date, price and ratio. The other is a typed fact remembering the pair with the answer 'mine'. OTHERWISE the question is asked again: with a record, of the record with every fact naming this pair left out, through MK-NW-F-238 sortArriving with the arriving row alone, keeping the question with the same pair; with no record, the question as asked is used. No such question (it was settled since): nothing to save. A fact to remember the answer is made for the account and holding of the event on record: no date, typed, carrying the pair and the answer. 'MINE': only that fact. Where the event on record is a purchase and the arriving date reads as a real day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull), the fact also keeps the date over the list (the first piece of the pair, up to its first upright bar, then that day), and, where the question was about a price, keeps the price over the list (that day, then the size of the arriving shares, 0 where none, then the arriving price). 'BOTH', or any answer about an event the account holder took away: the fact, with the answer written as 'both', and the arriving row itself, saved beside the other. One change to that arriving row: where the question is about a purchase the account holder took away and the arriving purchase is counted in a list, it is saved no longer counted in that list, so it holds its shares again — unless a purchase in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) of the same account and holding, not counted in a list, on the same day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull) and with the same shares (the size of the arriving shares) still holds them, when it is saved as it arrived. 'THEIRS': the event on record is saved again as typed, replacing it, no longer taken away, its date as given dropped, with the arriving date; the arriving settlement date, else its own, else blank; the arriving price, else its own; the arriving amount, else its own; the arriving fee, else its own; the arriving ratio and the arriving reference where there are such; marked as changing the date, price, settlement date and ratio. Then the fact. Then, where the event is a purchase, every other purchase in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) in the same account and holding that a list states as still held, is not typed, is not already counted in a list, is under the same date as the event on record, and holds no more shares than it plus EPS (any number where the event on record has no shares; a lot with no shares counting as 0), is saved again as typed, replacing it, with the arriving date, the arriving price (else its own), and an amount of its shares times the arriving price (its own amount where there is no arriving price or it has no shares), marked as changing the date and price.

MK-NW-F-275.name: besideTheList
MK-NW-F-275.rule: Sets the tax lots a broker's or a file's list states beside the purchases still held, so that each lot is held, the same purchase stated differently, or not held. A lot is UNDER a purchase when: the lot's date reads as a real day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull) and the purchase's first date or its date as it stands is that day; or the lot's date does not read as a day but was given (MK-NW-F-230 wasGiven) and the purchase's row as it stands (MK-NW-F-236 rowAsItStands) keeps exactly that text as its date as given; or the lot has no date at all and the purchase has no date, no first date and no date as given, and is not a broker's average. Each purchase can be matched once: when matched it leaves the pool. In each pass the lots are read in list order and the first purchase in the pool that fits is taken. PASS ONE: a lot under a purchase with the same shares (MK-NW-F-274 sameShares) and the same price (MK-NW-F-237 sameNumber, or either price blank) is held. PASS TWO, of the lots left: a lot under a purchase with the same shares, whatever the price, is held. PASS THREE, of the lots still left: a lot under any purchase differs from it (one purchase, two share counts). PASS FOUR, of the lots still left: a lot whose date reads as a day and a dated purchase with the same shares no more than NEARBY_DAYS (5) days away (MK-NW-F-267 daysFromOneDateToAnother) differ (one purchase, two dates). A lot left after all four passes is not held. The answer is the held pairs, the differing pairs, the lots not held, and the purchases left in the pool, which the list does not state.

MK-NW-F-277.rule: What a broker's update or a file's list does to the purchases of one holding of one account: rows to save, and questions for the account holder. SETUP. The holding is written one way (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling); The still-held day is the list day read as a real day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull). Where there is a still-held day and the record has, in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce), a sale, a purchase, a split or a transfer of more than 0 shares in this account and holding dated after it, the list is read as of that day: the purchases still held, the shares on record and the shares waiting for an answer are all taken up to the still-held day; otherwise over everything. The purchases still held are MK-NW-F-253 openPurchases. Only listed lines with more than 0 shares count; those marked as an average are average lines, the rest are tax lots. A listed line is saved as a purchase in this account and holding with its own date, shares and price, the given source, an amount of shares times price (blank with no price), the still-held day where there is one, and marked as a broker's average where the line is one. A question carries its kind, the purchases in question and their shares added up, the lines it states and their shares added up, everything the list stated, the list day, the source, the holding's gap as it stands when the question is made, and a signature: unless one is given, the kind (written 'list' for the kinds 'typed' and 'not-listed'), the purchases' first row numbers sorted and joined by commas, the lines' dates sorted and joined by commas, and the listed shares less the shares on record, all four joined by an upright bar. THE HOLDING'S GAP starts as all the counted listed shares added up less the shares on record (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord, up to the still-held day where the list is read as of it). The answers kept are the kept-over-list texts on every fact in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) the account holder typed for this account and holding, each with the holding's gap saved with it where that is a number; where answered questions are to be included, there are none. A signature is COVERED where an answer kept carries it and either has no gap saved (an older answer) or a gap the same shares (MK-NW-F-274 sameShares) as the holding's gap as it then stands, so a change elsewhere that moves the record against the list is asked again. At the end every question whose signature is covered is dropped. EARLY STOPS. Where the questions this update's history already asks include one about a split ratio for this holding: no rows and no questions. Where sales are still waiting for the account holder to say which lot they sold (the unassigned shares of MK-NW-F-254 sharesTakenBy, or when read as of the still-held day those of this account in the walk of the holding up to that day by MK-NW-F-252 walkHolding, added up, are more than EPS) and the shares on record (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord) are the same (MK-NW-F-274 sameShares) as all the counted listed shares added up: nothing saved and nothing asked. TERMS. EVERYTHING is every purchase in force in this account and holding that is not already counted in a list; the holding was EVER HELD where that or the purchases still held are not empty. A listed line was TAKEN AWAY where any row of the record is a typed purchase in this account and holding that was taken away, not by an answer, dated on the line's day. The last list day is MK-NW-F-264 lastListDay. WHEN THERE ARE TAX LOTS, OR NO AVERAGE LINES. Case two (the first list over the broker's own history): where no list was taken in before, there is a still-held day and at least one lot, everything is not empty, no lot was taken away, no purchase still held arrived by a transfer, and every row of everything is not typed, has no still-held day, and is dated on or before the still-held day (no date counting as earliest): each of those rows is saved again in the given source, replacing itself, marked as counted in the list of the still-held day; then every lot is saved; and it stops. Otherwise the lots are set beside the purchases still held (MK-NW-F-275 besideTheList). KEPT AWAY: each lot not held that was taken away and matches, by the same date and the same shares (a purchase with no shares counting as 0), a purchase the account holder took away and kept away when the history sent it again (MK-NW-F-293 keptAwayByEvent, each such purchase used once) is answered: it leaves the lots not held and its shares come off the holding's gap. Then the shares of every lot not held that is LATER (defined below) come off the holding's gap, since such a lot is a new purchase, not a gap. PRICES OF THE HELD PAIRS, skipping a pair whose row no longer stands, whose lot has no price, or whose purchase arrived by a transfer: where the row is typed, its first row was typed too, and no fact in force for this account and holding already records this lot price for the purchase's first row number, a fact recording that list price (the lot price divided by, then multiplied by, the splits) is saved. Case five: where the row has no price and was not typed, it is saved again with the lot price times the splits as its price and its shares (0 where blank) times that as its amount, replacing it. Else, where the purchase has a price that is not the same (MK-NW-F-237 sameNumber) as the lot price: for a row that was not typed this is a price difference; for a typed row, the broker's figure is the price of the latest version of that purchase that was not typed and not taken away, divided by the splits, or else the price in the latest fact in force recording a list price for that purchase; it is a price difference only where such a figure exists and is not the same as the lot price. A price difference is dropped where this update's history already asks about a purchase of the same date and shares, or about a purchase under the same date and price, or the account holder already kept their own price for that date, those shares and that price. SALES THAT EXPLAIN A SMALLER LOT. The waiting sales are those of MK-NW-F-254 sharesTakenBy whose shares before the list plus shares attributed are more than EPS, with those two added together. A differing pair is explained where its row stands, was not typed, has a still-held day, did not arrive by a transfer, and the waiting sales dated on or before that still-held day and first saved after the row was written add up to more than EPS and to the same shares (MK-NW-F-274 sameShares) as the purchase's shares less the lot's shares. Each explained pair's row is saved again, replacing it, with a still-held day of the day before the earliest waiting sale dated on or before its still-held day (that date less 86400000 milliseconds). WHAT IS LEFT. The unanswered pairs are the differing pairs not explained whose pair signature ('pair', the purchase's first row number, the lot's date, the lot's shares less the purchase's shares) is not covered, leaving out a pair where the account holder kept their date over the list for that purchase and the lot's day and the shares are the same. A purchase the list does not state and a lot not held with the same shares are both set aside where this update's history asks about that purchase under the lot's day, or the account holder kept their date for that day. Unanswered pairs whose purchase this update's history asks about are dropped from the questions to come. OWN ENTRIES are the purchases the list does not state that the account holder entered themselves and that stand as typed; the REST are the other purchases the list does not state. A lot is LATER where its date reads as a day, it was not taken away, and either a list was taken in before and the lot is dated after it, or a purchase in force in the broker's history, not typed, counted in the list of that same day and dated that day, holds the same shares. Case one: never held and no lot taken away: every lot not held is saved. Case three: no differing pairs, no own entries, at least one of the rest and one lot not held, no lot taken away, and every one of the rest is a broker's average, not typed, not arrived by a transfer: each of the rest is marked replaced (MK-NW-F-276 replacedPurchase) and the lots not held are saved. Otherwise: one question per unanswered pair, of the kind 'typed' where the purchase is typed and 'not-listed' where not, with its pair signature. Then case four: where there are none of the rest, every lot not held is later, and either a list was taken in before or there are no own entries: with no unanswered pairs the lots not held are saved, else any lots not held become one 'not-listed' question; and any own entries become one 'typed' question. Where case four does not apply but something is left (the rest, lots not held, or own entries), one question about all of them: 'removed' where a lot not held was taken away, else 'typed' where any of those purchases is typed, else 'not-listed'. Last, any price differences left become one 'price' question whose signature is 'price' and each purchase's first row number with its lot price. WHEN THERE ARE ONLY AVERAGE LINES. They are added into one line with no date: the shares added up, and a price of the total cost divided by those shares (blank where any line has no price). Never held and no typed purchase of this holding taken away (not by an answer): the line is saved. Never held but one was taken away: a 'removed' question. Shares on record not the same as the line's shares: a 'count' question over all the purchases still held, its signature 'count' and the line's shares less the shares on record. Otherwise, where the line has a price: the earlier figure is the latest fact in force not typed that states an average (its price and shares), else the latest broker's average purchase in this account and holding that is not typed and not by an answer (its price and shares). Where there is no earlier price, at least one purchase still held is the account holder's own entry standing as typed, and every purchase still held has a price: the typed cost is the purchases' shares times their prices, added up, divided by the line's shares; where it differs from the line's price by 0.005 or more, a 'price' question over the purchases still held, its signature 'price', 'average', the shares and the price, and nothing is saved. Otherwise, where there is no earlier price, no earlier shares, or other shares: a fact stating the new average price and shares is saved, unless the earlier price exists and is the same (MK-NW-F-237 sameNumber). Where the shares are the same and the prices differ by 0.005 or more: a 'price' question over the purchases still held, its signature 'price', 'average', the shares and the price.

MK-NW-F-278.name: answerListQuestion
MK-NW-F-278.rule: The account holder's answer to a question about a list, as rows to save. The question is first asked again of the record as it stands: MK-NW-F-277 purchasesFromList with everything the list stated (else the lines in question), the question's own source and list day where it kept them (else those given), no history questions, and answered questions included only when the answer is that the list is correct; the question with the same signature is kept. None: nothing to save. 'MINE IS CORRECT': one typed fact for the account and holding keeping that signature over the list, together with the holding's gap the question carries (the shares the whole list states less the shares on record), where it carries one — so the answer covers its difference only while the holding stays that far apart. 'THE LIST IS CORRECT': the still-held day is the list day read as a real day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull). The waiting sales are those of MK-NW-F-254 sharesTakenBy with unassigned shares, shares beyond the record, or shares before the list of more than EPS, each named by the row it began as (MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf). In what follows a purchase's SHARES ALREADY SOLD are its row's shares (0 where blank) less its shares still held divided by its splits. A COUNT QUESTION over any purchase that is not a broker's average: the gap is the listed shares less the shares on record. A gap above EPS: one undated purchase of the gap with no price and no amount, in the given source, marked as a broker's average and as an answer, with the still-held day where there is one; nothing else. Otherwise the shortfall is taken from the purchases in order: first those the account holder raised by hand (standing as typed but not their own entry), then oldest first (MK-NW-F-251 oldestLotFirst), skipping those whose row no longer stands or that arrived by a transfer, until the shortfall is no more than EPS. From each, the smaller of its shares and the shortfall is taken. What stays is the shares kept (its shares less those taken, divided by its splits) plus the shares already sold; above EPS the row is saved again typed with those shares and an amount at the row's price (blank with no price), else taken away, either way replacing it as an answer. With a still-held day, the shares taken (divided by the splits) are kept to show as a typed purchase on the row's date and price (amount blank with no price), counted in that day's list, as an answer, naming the waiting sales where there are any. A PRICE QUESTION STATING ONE AVERAGE LINE: each purchase in question that is a broker's average and not typed, and also, where there is exactly one purchase in question, it has no date and its shares are the same (MK-NW-F-274 sameShares) as the line's, that one purchase, is saved again typed at the line price times its splits, with an amount of its shares (0 where blank) times that, as an answer (skipped where its row no longer stands or the line has no price); then a typed fact keeping the signature, and a fact in the question's source stating the average price and shares. ANY OTHER PRICE QUESTION: each purchase in question is paired with the listed line in the same place; where its row stands and that line has a price, it is saved again typed at the line price times its splits, with an amount of its shares (0 where blank) times that, marked as changing the price. EVERY OTHER QUESTION: the gap is the shares on record less the listed shares, never below 0, taken from the purchases oldest first (MK-NW-F-251 oldestLotFirst). For each purchase in question whose row stands: where its shares arrived by a transfer, a typed transfer row of this account that brought them from outside the record is taken away as an answer, and otherwise one typed transfer row dated the still-held day ends those shares here, naming the purchase they came from and its shares, marked as restated and as an answer. Any other purchase is saved again typed with only its shares already sold, where more than EPS, and their amount at its price (blank with no price), else taken away, either way as an answer; and the part of the gap taken from it, divided by its splits, where more than EPS and there is a still-held day, is kept to show as a typed purchase on the row's date and price, counted in that day's list, as an answer, naming the waiting sales. Then every listed line is saved as a purchase in the given source with its date, shares and price, an amount of shares times price (blank with no price), the still-held day where there is one, marked as an average where it is one, and naming the purchase it stands for: the purchase in question, not arrived by a transfer, whose date or first date is the line's day; or, where there is exactly one purchase in question and one listed line, that purchase.

MK-NW-F-279.name: differsFromGiven
MK-NW-F-279.rule: Where what the account holder is about to enter for a row differs from what a broker or a file gave, for the confirmation the account holder sees before saving. The row as it stands (MK-NW-F-236 rowAsItStands); none: an empty list. Every version of the row (all rows leading back to the same first row, MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf) that was not taken away is read, and the figures given are those of the latest version that was not typed. Where there is none and the row is a purchase, the latest fact in force for the account and holding recording a list price for this purchase's first row number stands in: the row as it stands with that price times its splits (MK-NW-F-280 splitByOf). Still none: an empty list, as the row is the account holder's own entry. For a purchase with a holding the splits are MK-NW-F-280 splitByOf, else 1. The figures given are shown as the date (blank where none), the price divided by the splits, the shares times the splits, and the amount. The shares held now are those of the purchase still held that began as this row (MK-NW-F-253 openPurchases), else the row's shares times the splits, else blank. For each of date, price, shares and amount that the change names, a line carries the figure given, the figure entered (blank where the change leaves it blank), the holding and the shares held now; it is kept only where the two differ: two numbers by more than EPS, anything else by not being identical. Where the row is a purchase with a holding and at least one line was kept, the change is tried on a copy (MK-NW-F-281 correctRow, as typed, stamped 9999-12-31T00:00:00.000Z): each sale in force in the same account and holding whose gain (MK-NW-F-261 saleGain) is not the same (MK-NW-F-237 sameNumber) on the record and on the copy adds a sale-gain line with both figures, the sale's shares and its row number; and where the shares on record (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord) are not the same on the two, a shares-held line with both figures.

MK-NW-F-280.name: splitByOf
MK-NW-F-280.rule: How many shares each first share of a purchase has become through the splits since it was bought. The purchase is traced back to the row it began as (MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf; its own number where nothing leads back). In the walk of its holding over the whole record (MK-NW-F-252 walkHolding), the purchase still held that began as that row and did not arrive by a transfer is found; failing that, any purchase still held that began as that row. Its split count is the answer; with no such purchase, 1.

MK-NW-F-281.name: correctRow
MK-NW-F-281.rule: Corrects a row: the old row stays in the record, and a new row carrying the change names it. The row as it stands (MK-NW-F-236 rowAsItStands) is read. REFUSED, with the record left as it was and a sentence saying why: there is no such row or it was taken away; the row was typed and the change does not come from the account holder; a date or settlement date in the change was given (MK-NW-F-230 wasGiven) but does not read as a real day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull); the row is a value and the change would put it on another day. OTHERWISE: for a purchase with a holding whose change names a price or shares, the splits since are MK-NW-F-280 splitByOf, else 1; where they are not 1, a price entered is multiplied by them and shares entered are divided by them, so the row is saved as bought. The new row is the old row with the change laid over it, in the given source, replacing the old row. Where the change comes from the account holder, the marks of an answer's row are dropped (saved by an answer, the purchase it stands for, the sales it was kept for) and the row records which figures were changed: every figure the change names except the taken-away mark and the list of sales to ask about. A change naming a date drops the date as given; one naming a settlement date drops the settlement date as given. TWINS: where the account holder changes a purchase's price or date (and it is not a removal), every other purchase in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) in the same account and holding, of another first row, dated the same as the old row, where one of the two is a list's tax lot (a still-held day, not counted in a list) and the other a history row (counted in a list, not by an answer), is saved again as typed, replacing it: with the new date where the change names one, and with the price entered times that twin's own splits (MK-NW-F-280 splitByOf) and an amount of its shares times that price (its own amount where it has no shares) where a price was entered, marked as changing whichever of price and date the change named. The new row and its twins are added (MK-NW-F-233 addRows) at the given time.
