MK-NW-F-282.name: removeRow
MK-NW-F-282.rule: Takes a row away. Where the row as it stands (MK-NW-F-236 rowAsItStands) is a purchase with a holding, the account holder can always take it away: in the walk of that holding (MK-NW-F-252 walkHolding), each sale or transfer out that took shares from a purchase that began as the same row (MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf) is listed by the row it began as, with those shares added up, where more than EPS. Where any is listed, it is a correction that marks the row taken away and carries that list of sales to ask about (MK-NW-F-281 correctRow), so the shares they took become a question of which purchase they came from. Otherwise it is a correction that marks the row taken away (MK-NW-F-281 correctRow). Either way it is from the given source at the given time, with every refusal that function makes.

MK-NW-F-283.name: splitsBetween
MK-NW-F-283.rule: How many shares each share of one holding in one account became through its splits between two days: every split in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) for that account and holding that has a date and a ratio above 0, dated after the start day (any date where there is no start day) and on or before the end day, dates compared as text; their ratios multiplied together, starting from 1. With no such split, 1.

MK-NW-F-284.name: activityOf
MK-NW-F-284.rule: The activity of one account, every purchase shown once as it was bought, the dated lines oldest first, with adjustment lines so that the shares add up. ROOT of a purchase: the row it began as (MK-NW-F-235 firstRowOf), then, where that row stands for another purchase, that purchase's first row, and so on until a row stands for nothing or is met again. OTHER ACTIVITY: the rows in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) of this account, or reaching it by a transfer, that are not values, facts or purchases, and are not restated transfers. PURCHASES: every purchase row of the account, in force or not, is grouped under its root. In a group with no row in force where some version was taken away by the account holder (typed, not by an answer), each dated version marks its holding and date as taken away. A group is left out where: its root was saved by an answer and is counted in a list; its root was saved by an answer, stands for nothing and replaces nothing; some version is a history row (counted in a list, not by an answer) and the root's holding and date are marked taken away; some version was taken away by the account holder (typed, not by an answer, with no figures marked changed) and nothing is in force; or nothing is in force and no version came by an answer. Otherwise the line starts from the root's shares and price as bought: where a version has a still-held day, its shares are divided and its price multiplied by the splits (MK-NW-F-283 splitsBetween) from the root's date to that day, else they are as saved. The date starts as the root's. Each other version in record order, skipping removals and an answer's rows counted in a list, then works on it: a typed version with figures marked changed sets the date where it changed the date and the price (as bought) where it changed the price, and marks the line corrected; else a version standing for another purchase sets the date, and the price (its own as bought, else the one so far). The row shown is the latest version in force, else the root. Where that row or the root is a list's tax lot (a still-held day, not typed, not counted in a list) and the shares are known, the shares sold before the list from every lot in the holding's walk (MK-NW-F-252 walkHolding) of this account that began in this group are added back, where more than EPS. The line is the row shown with that date, price and shares, and an amount of shares times price (else the row's own amount); it counts as a lot where the root or the row shown is a list's tax lot, and as corrected only where it was corrected and the root was not typed. Lines of one holding are joined into a group where their root and shown dates share a day, or neither has any date at all; joined groups chain. In each group the lots are shown where there are more lots than other lines, or no other lines, or where some lot was corrected and no other line was; else the other lines are shown. ORDER: dated lines by date, then by row number; undated lines after them, by row number. ADJUSTMENTS, for each holding shown: a running count over that holding's shown lines and its splits in force (dated, ratio above 0), in date order with a split first on its own day: a split multiplies the count by its ratio; a purchase adds its shares; a sale from this account and a transfer out of it (not arriving) take theirs away; a transfer into this account, or arriving in it, adds them; blank shares count as 0. Then the save moments of every row of this account and holding saved by an answer, or typed with the shares marked changed, are put in time order (MK-NW-F-231 instantOf). For each moment, the shares on record (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord) with the changes up to and including that moment, less those with the changes before it only, is that moment's change; where it is more than EPS either way it becomes one adjustment line of those shares: where the account holder corrected the count themselves, dated by the moment's own day and worded 'the account holder corrected the count'; else dated by the latest counted-in-list or still-held day among that moment's rows of the holding (blank where none) and worded 'the account holder accepted the broker's list'. Last, the shares on record less the running count less all those changes, where more than EPS either way, is one undated line worded 'held before the record begins'. The lines and the adjustments are returned together in the same order.

MK-NW-F-285.name: factsOf
MK-NW-F-285.rule: The facts on record for an account (no holding) or one of its holdings (written one way, MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling): every fact in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) for it, read in the order saved (by moment, MK-NW-F-231 instantOf, then by row number). Each named fact takes the latest value given, except that once the account holder has typed a fact, a later one that was not typed does not replace it. A blank or empty value is skipped and changes nothing. Nothing found: no facts.

MK-NW-F-202.name: equalOrBothBlank
MK-NW-F-202.rule: Whether two amounts are the same. Where either is blank: true only when both are blank. Otherwise true where the size of their difference is no more than EPS (one billionth).

MK-NW-F-203.name: isGiven
MK-NW-F-203.rule: Whether a day of values was given by the broker, a file or the account holder: true for every source except the price feed.

MK-NW-F-204.name: lastGivenBy
MK-NW-F-204.rule: The latest values given, not worked out from the price feed (MK-NW-F-203 isGiven), dated on or before a day. Of the given value days with a date on or before that day, the one with the latest date wins; on the same date, the one saved latest wins, save stamps compared as text, a later or equal one replacing the one before. Where none is dated on or before that day, the given value days with no date stand in: the one saved latest wins, a later or equal stamp replacing the one before. None of either: nothing.

MK-NW-F-205.name: priceFeedValues
MK-NW-F-205.rule: The price feed's values for each account with holdings on record, as rows to save. ACCOUNTS: every account that a purchase or transfer in force (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) with a holding belongs to. An account is skipped when it is not among the account holder's accounts, when its balance is not built from its holdings, or when its facts on record (MK-NW-F-285 factsOf, for the account itself) say it was removed. HOLDINGS: every holding of a row in force in the account or reaching it, whose shares on record today (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord) are more than EPS; none: the account is skipped. THE DAY is the latest of the last price days in the price cache for those holdings; no price days: skipped. Where one of the account's value days (MK-NW-F-242 valueBatchesOf) given by a broker, a file or the account holder (MK-NW-F-203 isGiven) is already on that day: skipped. The last given values on or before the day are MK-NW-F-204 lastGivenBy. EACH HOLDING: its shares on record up to the day; its close on or before the day (MK-PF-F-034 closeOnOrBefore); its multiplier is that of the account's position for the holding (MK-PF-F-031 contractMultiplier: a bond quoted per hundred of face counts a hundredth), except an option, where it is 1 because its shares already count every share in its contracts, and 1 with no position. With a close: the price is the close and the value is shares times close times multiplier; where the close is old (MK-PF-F-086 staleStartClose) the close's own day is kept beside it as the price's day. With no close: the price last given for the holding, else blank, and the value last given only where its shares are the same as now (MK-NW-F-202 equalOrBothBlank), else blank. Holdings with no more than EPS shares are dropped; none left: skipped. The cash and the typed value are those last given, else blank. Where the latest price-feed values already on that day (the one saved last, stamps compared as text) have the same cash, the same typed value, the same number of holdings, and for each holding the same shares, price and value (MK-NW-F-202 equalOrBothBlank): skipped. Otherwise the rows for that day are made by MK-NW-F-241 valueRows, in the price feed's name. The count of shares is never changed.

MK-NW-F-226.name: fileValues
MK-NW-F-226.rule: An imported account's values on the list day it is given (MK-NW-F-288 importedListDay works it out for the caller), saved as the file's. An account with no positions, whose balance is not built from its holdings and which has a balance given (MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber), holds one value: where its label, written one way (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling), gives a holding name, the rows are made by MK-NW-F-241 valueRows for the account on the list day, source 'file', cash 0, with that one holding, no shares, no price and the balance as its value. Otherwise each position with a holding name (written one way, MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling; none: skipped) gives one holding: its multiplier is MK-PF-F-031 contractMultiplier; its lots' shares are added up (each by MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber, a blank counting as 0); its shares are that total times the multiplier for an option, and the total itself for anything else; its price is the last price given (MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber, blank where not given); its value is the total of the lots' shares times the price times the multiplier, blank with no price. The rows are made by MK-NW-F-241 valueRows for the account, dated by the list day given (blank where none), source 'file', with the cash balance given as its cash (blank where not given).

MK-NW-F-227.name: fileFacts
MK-NW-F-227.rule: An imported account's facts, as the file's import saves them. For each position with a holding name (written one way, MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling; none: skipped): its face value and coupon rate where not blank, its maturity date and price quote where given and not empty, and, for an option with a shares-per-contract figure, that figure. Where any of these is present, one undated fact row in the source 'file' for the account and holding carries them; where none is, nothing.

MK-NW-F-228.name: moveOldCopies
MK-NW-F-228.rule: What a phone already holds, moved onto the master record once, for every account typed by hand or made from a file that does not yet carry the move's own mark (an account moved before the mark counts as moved where the record already holds what the phone shows); an account linked to a broker is never moved. For each account moved: what is held now is each holding's tax lots exactly as the phone shows them, one purchase per lot with its shares (an option's contracts times its shares a contract), its price paid (a bond's per $100 quote as a hundredth) and its date, blank where none; the shares on record equal the phone's. Each past sale on the phone is saved on its own date with the gain the app shows today, read once from the app's realized-gain reading as the Performance tab reads it; it names a purchase of exactly the shares it sold, saved for it with no date, marked as behind a sale before the record, and priced so the sale's gain equals the app's. Dividends, interest, deposits, withdrawals, fees and transfers keep their own rows and dates; shares moved between two moved accounts are saved as purchases of the account they left and the transfer names them. What the old copies cannot explain is marked as a fact on the holding and listed to be asked once. An imported account's values are saved on the file's day only while the account still is as the file left it; traded or edited since, no file value is saved and a fact says so; an undated file stays undated. An account deleted before the move is saved and marked removed. A row the account holder typed before the move ran is not saved twice. Old daily values are never moved.

MK-NW-F-189.name: abs
MK-NW-F-189.rule: A number the broker sent, as its size without its sign: a number given as text is read as a number first, and a minus sign is dropped, so a sale sent as minus five shares is five. Nothing comes back when the broker sent nothing, or when what it sent does not read as a finite number.

MK-NW-F-190.name: dateAsSent
MK-NW-F-190.rule: A date the broker gave. Where it reads as a calendar day (the same reading as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull) it is cut to that day. Where it does not read as a day but is text with something other than spaces in it, it is kept exactly as sent, so the record can keep it and ask about it. Otherwise (missing, empty or only spaces, or not text) it is nothing.

MK-NW-F-191.name: sharesPerContract
MK-NW-F-191.rule: How many shares one contract of an option stands for, read by the sync's one rule (MK-XS-F-106, the sync's option reader, asked as if for one contract). The broker's option symbol is passed in when it is an object; anything else is passed as an empty symbol. A symbol the broker marks as a mini option gives 10 shares a contract; every other option, including an empty symbol, gives 100. Should that reading give nothing, the answer is 100.

MK-NW-F-193.name: eventRow
MK-NW-F-193.rule: One broker activity as one row of the record. The sync's ledger (MK-ST-F-012, the ledger's row reader, read with a negative amount meaning money out) is given the activity's word, amount, units, price, trade date (blank when the broker sends none), ticker and description, and says what the activity is and which way it went. The activity is an option when it carries an option symbol or an option type. Its reference is the key it is handed (the caller hands the sync's key for the activity, made from its content; the key it is finally saved under is chosen after, by MK-NW-F-289 activityRefs). Its date is the trade date and its settlement date the settlement date, each blank where not sent; the phone's date is never used. Its holding is the option symbol's ticker for an option (else the ledger's ticker), the ledger's ticker otherwise, written the one way (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling). For an option the ledger's units are contracts: shares are units times the shares a contract (MK-NW-F-191 sharesPerContract); anything else uses 1, so shares are as the ledger read them. Where the broker sent an amount, the price is the ledger's price divided by the shares a contract (for an option the ledger's price is then a contract's price; anything else divides by 1). Where the broker sent no amount, the price is the broker's own price, already per share, times how the holding's price is quoted: for an option that is 1; for anything else it is the factor the caller hands for the holding (a hundredth for a bond quoted per hundred dollars of face, 1 otherwise), and where the caller hands nothing (the quote is not clear) the price is blank, never guessed. Missing shares or price stay blank. The amount is the ledger's amount rounded to 2 decimal places, blank when the broker sent no amount. The fee is its size without a sign (MK-NW-F-189 abs). First, an activity that is a split the record can size (MK-NW-F-287 splitOf) becomes that split row. Otherwise, by what the ledger says it is: a buy or a reinvested purchase becomes a purchase through MK-NW-F-265 historyPurchaseRow; a sale or a return of capital becomes a sale through MK-NW-F-258 saleRow; either one with no holding or no shares is kept as an other row. A dividend or capital gain distribution is a dividend row, and interest an interest row, unless the money went out, which is kept as an other row. A fee, tax withheld or margin interest is a fee row, unless the money came in, which is kept as an other row. Cash in or cash out is a withdrawal when the money went out, a deposit when it came in, and where the ledger gives no direction a deposit for cash in and a withdrawal for cash out. Securities in are a transfer that arrives; securities out are a transfer naming no account they go to, so the shares leave the record; either with no holding or no shares is an other row. A transfer between the account holder's own accounts is a transfer row that arrives when the money came in. Anything else (a sweep, a corporate action such as a split that could not be sized, an option's expiry or exercise, a word the ledger does not know) is an other row, counted in nothing. Every row carries the account, the holding, both dates, the source as linked, the reference and the broker's own word; a cash row carries shares and price only where they are known.

MK-NW-F-194.name: brokerUpdateToRecord
MK-NW-F-194.rule: One broker update, as the three things the record takes. The day of the list is the broker's own date of its last successful holdings update, read as a day by MK-NW-F-286 dayOfInstant (a stamp with a time is read on the phone's own clock); blank where the broker gives none. The account is also read once by the sync (MK-XS-F-102, the sync's account reader), given that same date or, where there is none, 1970-01-01, for its cash and how each bond is quoted. How each holding's price is quoted is taken from this update's positions as the sync reads them, by the position's place in the list; for a holding this update does not list, from the record's own fact for that holding. The events: each activity is first turned into one row (MK-NW-F-193 eventRow), handed the sync's key for the activity, made from its content, and the factor for its holding's quote — a hundredth for a bond quoted per hundred dollars of face, nothing where the quote is not clear, and 1 otherwise and for no holding. Then the key each one is saved under is chosen (MK-NW-F-289 activityRefs), and each event carries its chosen key. None when the broker sends no activities. Each position the sync can read (MK-XS-F-105, the sync's position reader) is a holding, its name written the one way (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling). Its list of purchases is the broker's tax lots, each with its purchase date as sent (MK-NW-F-190 dateAsSent), shares and cost per share times the sync's figure for how its price is quoted, when at least one tax lot has a quantity above 0 (a missing quantity counts as 0); otherwise it is one line of the broker's average, undated, with the position's shares and cost per share times that same figure. Either cost is blank where none is given or the quote is unclear. The list is kept only when the position's shares are above 0. Its value is shares times price times the sync's figure for how its price is quoted (MK-PF-F-031 contractMultiplier, 1 where the sync has no matching position, read by the position's place in the list), and blank where there is no price or the quote is unclear. Each option position the sync can read (MK-XS-F-106, the sync's option reader) that has a name (MK-NW-F-192 optionName) is a holding with shares equal to its contracts times its shares a contract; when those shares are above 0 its list is one undated average line priced at the broker's average purchase price divided by the shares a contract (blank where there is none); a short option is valued but not listed. Its value is the sync's value of the option and its price the broker's price. When the broker sent a list of positions at all, every holding still on the record for this account (a purchase or transfer row in force, from or to this account) that the broker left out, and of which the record still holds more than EPS shares (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord), gets an empty list, meaning it is no longer held. The cash is the sync's cash balance, and blank when the broker sent no cash balance; the stated total is the broker's total balance, blank where none. The values are built from the account, the day of the list, the source as linked, the cash, the stated total and the holdings (MK-NW-F-241 valueRows). The values are left out, and nothing else changes, when the record already holds a linked batch of values for this account on the same day with the same cash, the same stated total and the same holdings in the same order, each with the same name, shares, price and value; two figures count as the same when both are blank or they are no more than EPS apart. It hands back the events, the lists, the values and the day of the list.

MK-NW-F-195.name: readImport
MK-NW-F-195.rule: An imported file read once, through the import's own account builder (MK-XS-F-219) and value-only builder (MK-XS-F-221), given an empty institution and name and a fixed time of 1970-01-01 that nothing here reads. The file's rows are walked in order against the account's holdings in order: a row is a held holding when the next unmatched holding has the row's ticker (or its symbol trimmed and in capitals where there is no ticker) and its first lot has exactly the row's shares; every other row is set aside. If not every one of the account's holdings was matched, it stops with an error naming how many there were and how many were found. The set-aside rows are then walked against the value-only accounts in order: a row matches when the next value-only account has the row's label (or its symbol where there is no label) and a balance exactly equal to the row's value. If not every value-only account was matched, it stops with an error the same way. Every set-aside row that is not value-only is a cash row. It hands back the held rows, the value-only rows, the cash (the account's cash balance when there is at least one cash row, otherwise nothing, never $0) and the account's balance.

MK-NW-F-197.name: unitsOf
MK-NW-F-197.rule: A file holding's units as the record counts them: where the file gives a shares-per-contract figure, the holding's quantity times that figure (an option's contracts become shares); otherwise the quantity as given.

MK-NW-F-198.name: costPerUnit
MK-NW-F-198.rule: A file purchase's price per unit as the record counts units. When the file's cost per share is not above 0 (the import writes 0 where the file gives no cost) the answer is nothing, never $0. For a bond or CD quoted per $100 of face value, it is the cost per share divided by 100, because its units are dollars of face. Otherwise it is the cost per share as given.

MK-NW-F-199.name: fileToRecord
MK-NW-F-199.rule: One imported file, as the rows of the record. The day of the list is the file's own date read as a day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull); blank where the file states none, and then the account holder needs to be asked a date. The file is read once (MK-NW-F-195 readImport) into held rows, value-only rows and cash. Every purchase is marked as the broker's average only when the file's cost column heading contains average or avg, in any capitals. The file has values only when it has a value column. Each held row becomes one purchase line under its holding name (MK-NW-F-196 fileHoldingName): its date read as a day, blank where missing; its units (MK-NW-F-197 unitsOf); its price (MK-NW-F-198 costPerUnit); rows of the same holding are listed together in file order. A value-only row (a value with no quantity) is held by its own account, never by this one. The values are built (MK-NW-F-241 valueRows) for the account on the day of the list, source file, with the cash and a stated total that is the file's stated total less the sum of the value-only rows' values (blank where the file states no total), from each held row only (its name, its units, its last price or blank, and its value only when the file has a value column). Each value-only row that has an account given for it, matched by its place among the value-only rows, gets its own values built the same way for that account: the day of the list, source file, cash 0, and one holding with its name and its value, with no shares and no price; a value-only row with no account given gets none. A fact row, undated and from the file, is made for each held or value-only row that is in the bonds class or has a face value, a coupon rate, a maturity date or a shares-per-contract figure; it belongs to the value-only row's own account where one is given, otherwise to this account; it carries only those of face value, coupon rate, maturity date, how its price is quoted and shares per contract that the file gives, and a row left with none is dropped. A holdings file carries no events. It hands back no events, the lists, the values, the value-only accounts' values, the facts, the day of the list, and whether a date must be asked (when the day is blank).

MK-NW-F-200.name: sameJson
MK-NW-F-200.rule: Whether two lists of values or facts read the same: both are written out as text in full, and they are the same only when the two texts are exactly equal, so the same items in another order read as different.

MK-NW-F-201.name: fileRowsToSave
MK-NW-F-201.rule: The rows to save for one imported file, and the questions for the account holder. The file is read into rows (MK-NW-F-199 fileToRecord), with the accounts given for its value-only rows (and an empty account name where no account is given). A set of one account's values is saved only when it is not already on the record: it counts as already there when the record holds, for that account, a batch from a file, not typed, on the same day as the list, with exactly the same cash and stated total as the set's own first value row, no typed value, and holdings that read the same (MK-NW-F-200 sameJson) as the set's holding values, each with its name written the one way, its shares, its price and its value (blank where missing). The value-only accounts' values are taken two rows at a time (the account's own row and its one value), each pair checked that way. A fact is saved only when no fact in force from a file for the same account and holding already carries the same facts (MK-NW-F-200 sameJson). Where no account is given for the file itself, it hands back only the value-only accounts' values not yet saved and the new facts that belong to a value-only account, with the day of the list, whether a date must be asked, and no questions. Otherwise its events go through MK-NW-F-238 sortArriving against the record, and the ones to save are added to a copy of the record (MK-NW-F-233 addRows). For each holding's list, MK-NW-F-277 purchasesFromList is run on that copy for this account, source file, with the day of the list and the event questions, and its purchase rows and its questions are gathered. Then every holding with a purchase in force in this account on that copy (MK-NW-F-234 rowsInForce) that the file does not list is set against an empty list by MK-NW-F-277 purchasesFromList, the same way, and only its questions are kept, so it is asked about and its shares stay until answered; it is not asked when none of its purchases are still held (MK-NW-F-253 openPurchases), or when the file has a day and every purchase still held is dated after that day. It hands back the rows to save in this order: the events, the purchases, this account's values (unless already there), the value-only accounts' values (unless already there), the new facts; and the day of the list, whether a date must be asked, the event questions and the list questions.

MK-NW-F-206.name: same
MK-NW-F-206.rule: Whether two amounts the account holder gave are the same: true when both are missing; false when only one is missing; otherwise true when they are no more than EPS apart (one billionth), so an edit that changes nothing saves nothing.

MK-NW-F-207.name: givenNumber
MK-NW-F-207.rule: A number the account holder typed: nothing when the box was missing or left empty, or when what it holds does not read as a finite number; otherwise that entry read as a number.

MK-NW-F-208.name: dateAsGiven
MK-NW-F-208.rule: A date as the account holder gave it. Where it reads as a calendar day (the same reading as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull) it is cut to that day. Where it does not read as a day but is text with something other than spaces in it, it is kept exactly as given. Otherwise (missing, empty or only spaces, or not text) it is nothing.

MK-NW-F-209.name: valuesAreTyped
MK-NW-F-209.rule: Whether an account's values and purchases are the ones the account holder gives: true when there is an account and it is neither linked to a broker (source connected) nor made from an imported file (source imported); false when there is no account.

MK-NW-F-210.name: lotRef
MK-NW-F-210.rule: The key a tax lot the account holder typed carries: the words typed-lot, then the account's id, then the lot's id, joined by colons, so a later edit or removal of that lot finds its row.

MK-NW-F-211.name: txnRef
MK-NW-F-211.rule: The key a transaction the account holder recorded carries: the words typed-txn, a colon, then the transaction's id, so deleting it finds its row.

MK-NW-F-213.name: lotRow
MK-NW-F-213.rule: One tax lot as a purchase row. The holding is the position's ticker written the one way (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling). Shares a contract are MK-PF-F-031 contractMultiplier for an option, and 1 for anything else. The lot's shares and cost per share are read as typed numbers (MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber). No row is made when there is no holding name, no shares, or shares of 0 or less. The price is the cost per share times the unit price factor (MK-NW-F-212 unitPriceFactor), blank where no cost was typed. The row is a purchase for the account and holding, dated by the lot's purchase date as given (MK-NW-F-208 dateAsGiven), with shares equal to the typed shares times the shares a contract, that price, an amount equal to those shares times the price (blank where the price is blank), the source as typed, and the lot's key (MK-NW-F-210 lotRef).

MK-NW-F-214.name: accountValueRows

MK-NW-F-215.name: factRow
MK-NW-F-215.rule: A bond's or CD's own details as one fact row. It reads only the change it is given when there is one, otherwise the whole account. Of face value, coupon rate, maturity date, purchase date, amount paid, the date the CD was bought, and accrued interest, it keeps each one that is present and is neither missing nor empty. When at least one is kept, the answer is one undated fact row for the account, with no holding, the source as typed, carrying those details; when none is kept, nothing.

MK-NW-F-216.name: rowOfLot
MK-NW-F-216.rule: The purchase on the record a tax lot stands for. It looks only at purchase rows in force for this account. If exactly one of them carries the lot's key (MK-NW-F-210 lotRef), that row is the answer. Otherwise the lot is turned into the purchase it would be (MK-NW-F-213 lotRow); if it makes no row, the answer is none. Otherwise it takes the purchases of the same holding with the same date (both blank counts as the same) and the same shares and price (MK-NW-F-206 same). Of those, the ones that are not part of a broker's or a file's list are preferred; if there are none such, all of them are used. Exactly one gives that row; more than one gives many; none gives none.

MK-NW-F-217.name: transactionRow
MK-NW-F-217.rule: One transaction the account holder recorded as one row, on its own date (MK-NW-F-208 dateAsGiven), carrying its key (MK-NW-F-211 txnRef) and the source as typed. The account is the transaction's account, the holding its ticker written the one way (MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling), blank where none. Shares a contract are the transaction's multiplier when it is above 0, otherwise 1. Shares are the size of the typed shares, without a sign, times that; the price is the typed price as given (an option's price is per share); the amount and the fee are each the size of the typed figure without a sign. Any of these not typed as a number (MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber) is blank. A buy is a purchase whose amount is the typed amount, or else shares times price, or blank where there is no price. A sale goes through MK-NW-F-258 saleRow. A buy or sale with no holding or no shares is an other row. A dividend is a dividend row; interest or a coupon is an interest row. A deposit is a withdrawal row when its direction is out, else a deposit row; a withdrawal is a deposit row when its direction is in, else a withdrawal row. A fee is a fee row. A cash transfer is a transfer row with no holding, naming the other account as where it goes when one is named. A transfer of shares in kind with no holding or no shares is an other row; coming in, it is a transfer that arrives; going out to a named account it goes through MK-NW-F-259 transferRow; going out with no account named, the shares leave the record. Opening cash is the first value row (MK-NW-F-241 valueRows) with that cash on that date, with the transaction's key, and nothing when no amount was typed. An opening position gives nothing here (MK-NW-F-223 openingRow writes it). Any other type is an other row. Cash rows carry shares and price only where they are known.

MK-NW-F-221.name: lotsFollow
MK-NW-F-221.rule: Each tax lot of a holding before and after an edit, matched by the lot's id. Where the edit changed the holding's name (the names written the one way, MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling, differ), the lots are not matched: every lot before is taken out as if the holding had gone (this same reading from the before holding to no holding), then every lot after that makes a purchase (MK-NW-F-213 lotRow) is saved as a new purchase together (MK-NW-F-218 arrive), and where its reference is already used by a row of this account on the record, the new holding's name is added to the end of its reference after a colon, so the two are not taken for one. Otherwise, a missing before or after counts as no lots. A lot only in the after list becomes a new purchase (MK-NW-F-213 lotRow), where it makes one. For a lot in both: if after the edit it makes no purchase, the purchase it stood for (MK-NW-F-216 rowOfLot) is removed (MK-NW-F-220 remove), when exactly one was found. If before and after make purchases with the same date (both blank counts as the same), the same shares and the same price (MK-NW-F-206 same), nothing is done. Otherwise the purchase it stood for is found: none found means the new purchase is added; more than one found means nothing is changed and a problem is written saying more than one purchase of that holding matches the tax lot that was changed; one found is corrected (MK-NW-F-219 correct) by what the edit changed, measured from what the lot made before the edit (or, where it made no purchase before, from the purchase found), so a purchase part of which was sold since keeps the part sold: the date becomes the new date where the edit changed it and the purchase found is not already on that date; where the edit changed the shares, the purchase's shares move by the same number of shares (its shares plus the lot's shares after less the lot's shares before, a missing count read as 0); where the edit changed the price and the purchase found is not already at that price, the price becomes the new price and the amount becomes the purchase's shares (as now corrected) times that price, blank where no price is given; otherwise, where only the shares changed and the purchase has a price, the amount becomes the corrected shares times its price. Nothing is written when nothing differs. A lot only in the before list is taken out: more than one matching purchase writes a problem saying more than one purchase of that holding matches the tax lot that was taken out, one is removed, none does nothing. Last, the new purchases are saved together (MK-NW-F-218 arrive).

MK-NW-F-224.name: typedChangeToRecord
MK-NW-F-224.rule: What the account holder entered, saved into the record, starting from a copy of the record with no questions and no problems. An account added: only when its values are typed (MK-NW-F-209 valuesAreTyped), its value and fact rows (MK-NW-F-222 typedAccountRows) are added (MK-NW-F-233 addRows), and then every tax lot of every holding that makes a purchase (MK-NW-F-213 lotRow) is saved together (MK-NW-F-218 arrive). An account changed: only when its values are typed after the change. When the change touched the balance, the value-as-of date or the cash, its value rows (MK-NW-F-214 accountValueRows) are added; the bond or CD details in the change itself (MK-NW-F-215 factRow) are added where there are any. When the change touched the holdings and the account's values were also typed before it, each holding found before or after, by its position id, has its lots followed (MK-NW-F-221 lotsFollow). An account removed: one undated fact row, source typed, marking the account removed. An account unlinked: one such fact row marking it unlinked, and also removed unless it is kept as a typed account. A holding added, changed or taken away: its lots are followed from no holding, from before to after, or to no holding. A transaction recorded: where it is a transfer of shares that is not marked as coming in, names a holding (written the one way, MK-NW-F-232 oneHoldingSpelling) and gives no share count (MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber), the shares moved are all the shares the record holds of that holding in the account they leave (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord, with no day), when those are more than EPS, and no shares per contract is applied to them again. It is then turned into a row (MK-NW-F-217 transactionRow); a value row is added straight to the record, any other row is saved through the arrival pass, and no row does nothing. A transaction deleted: every row in force carrying its key (MK-NW-F-211 txnRef) is removed (MK-NW-F-220 remove). Savings moved: only when the amount is above 0, one deposit with no holding, on the date given, carrying the amount, the source as typed and a key made of the words typed-savings, the account id and the time written, is saved through the arrival pass. It hands back the record, the questions and the problems.

MK-NW-F-243.name: theLater
MK-NW-F-243.rule: Of two sets of values, the one to read. A dated one wins over an undated one. Between two dates, the later date wins (dates compared as written, year first). On the same date, one given by a broker, a file or the account holder wins over one from the price feed; then one the account holder typed wins over one not typed; then the later save time wins (moments read by MK-NW-F-231 instantOf); at the same save time, the one with the higher set number wins.

MK-NW-F-286.name: dayOfInstant
MK-NW-F-286.rule: The day of the broker's last update. Anything that is not text, and text that is only a plain day (four digits, a dash, two digits, a dash, two digits, with spaces at its ends allowed), is read as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull reads it, a missing value counting as nothing. Any other text carries a time, so it is read as one moment in time; where it cannot be read as a moment, it is read as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull reads it. A moment is turned into its calendar day on the phone's own clock, so the same moment written with any time zone gives one day: the year, then the month, then the day of the month, the month and the day each written with two digits, joined by dashes.

MK-NW-F-287.name: splitOf
MK-NW-F-287.rule: A split the broker sends as an activity, as a SPLIT row, only where the activity says enough to know how many shares each share became. The activity's word is read in capitals. The activity says split where that word contains SPLIT, or where the ledger called it a corporate action (or the word itself is CORPORATE_ACTION) and the description holds the whole word split, in any case. The answer is nothing when the activity does not say split, when there is no holding, or when the date does not read as a real day (MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull). The units are read as a number; nothing when they are not a finite number or their size is at most 1e-9. The split is a reverse split where the word or the description contains reverse, in any case; nothing when that disagrees with the sign of the units (a reverse split must take shares away, any other split must add them). The shares held are the shares on record for that account and holding up to the day before the split's day (the split's day less 86400000 milliseconds, written as a day in universal time), so a split dated that day is not counted twice (MK-NW-F-262 sharesOnRecord); nothing unless more than 1e-9 shares are held. The ratio is the shares held plus the units, divided by the shares held; nothing unless the ratio is more than 1e-9 and differs from 1 by more than 1e-9. The row saved: the account, the holding, kind SPLIT, the date as given, the settlement date as given or blank, the ratio, source linked, the key it is handed as the reference, and the ledger's source word.

MK-NW-F-288.name: importedListDay
MK-NW-F-288.rule: The day an imported account's values are from: the file's own date, never the day of the import. The given day is the account's value-as-of date read as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull reads it. Where the account says that date came from the file, the given day is the answer (nothing if it does not read as a real day). Where the account says the date did not come from the file, or there is no given day, the answer is nothing. Otherwise, for an account saved before it said which: with no last-synced time, or one that cannot be read as a moment in time, the given day is the answer. Else the import days are the last-synced time's calendar day on the phone's own clock and its first 10 characters as written; where the given day is one of the import days, the answer is nothing (blank, and asked), otherwise the given day.

MK-NW-F-289.name: activityRefs
MK-NW-F-289.rule: The key each activity of one broker update is saved under, one key for each activity in the order the broker sent them. The rows already saved for this account from the linked broker that carry a key are read. First, each activity whose broker id is already a saved key is given that id; each id goes to one activity only. Then each activity left gets a key made from its own content (the account, then what the activity says, as the sync reads it): the first activity alike in this update gets that key as it is, and each later one alike gets it followed by a bar, a hash mark and its number among the alike ones. Where a row was already saved under that key and the key is not yet given out, the activity takes it. Otherwise, a saved row takes the activity over when its key is a broker id (not a content key, which starts with the account and a bar), is not yet given out, is not an id this update sends, and the row is the same event as the activity's draft row: the same kind, the same holding, the same date, and the same shares (the size of the draft's shares), price and amount — each the same when their difference is no more than one billionth, or both not given. That row's key is given to the activity. Otherwise the activity gets its new content key. No key is given out twice.

MK-NW-F-290.name: movedMark
MK-NW-F-290.rule: The key of the mark the move leaves on an account it moved: the words moved-from-phone, a colon, then the account's id.

MK-NW-F-291.name: lotsOf
MK-NW-F-291.rule: A holding's tax lots as the phone shows them, in the order they are kept. Only lots whose shares, read by MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber, are above zero are kept; a lot with no shares given is left out, and a holding with no lots gives none. Each lot gives: shares = its shares × the shares a contract it is handed (the multiplier); date = its purchase date as MK-NW-F-229 dayOrNull reads it (nothing when that is not a real day); price = its cost per share, read by MK-NW-F-207 givenNumber, × MK-NW-F-212 unitPriceFactor of the holding — nothing when no cost per share was given.

awaiting_id.note: Rules written 2026-10-20 for functions that have no identifier yet. The build issues each one its identifier from moneykeel_function_register.json; then each entry moves under rules with that identifier, and build-outside-test-cards.py --reread records its fingerprint. Never hand-type an identifier here. 2026-10-21: the build issued identifiers (moneykeel_function_register.json); every entry in a Net worth, Performance or Cash flow family moved under rules. The entries still here are engine and sync functions (MK-ST, MK-XS), which build-outside-test-cards.py does not card unless they are named in its ALSO_CARDED list, so under rules they would stop the build as rules for a function that is not tested; each carries the identifier the register issued it.

bondQuoteBasis.rule: How each linked bond's price is quoted, from the broker's own total of the account, in exact decimals to the cent. Each holding is worth quantity × price, or what was paid when it has no price. A holding is a bond here when it is an individual bond or CD with a quantity above zero and a worth. No bond: no answer for any holding. As a share: every holding at its worth plus the options and cash; per $100 of face: each bond at its worth ÷ 100, the rest as before. The one that equals the broker's total (a total above zero; the sync hands in no total when the broker's is not in US dollars) is every bond's answer, the share reading first. When neither does, or there is no total: per $100 of face for a bond whose entered face value equals its quantity, unclear otherwise. A holding that is not a bond has no answer.

unitWorth.rule: What one unit at one price is worth: one hundredth for a bond quoted per $100 of face value, one for everything else.

holdingName.rule: What a gap calls a holding: its readable name when its ticker is a 9-character security identifier with a digit in it (a bond's or CD's) and it has a name; otherwise its ticker, else its name, else the words A holding.

brokerClassOf.rule: What the broker says a holding is, or nothing (owner ruling, 2026-10-20: "always the class broker sends"). Cash when the broker's cash-equivalent flag is true. Otherwise the type it sent, capitals and spaces at the ends ignored: a broker code that names a class — common stock, preferred stock, ADR, ETF, open-end fund, closed-end fund or mutual fund → Stocks / Funds; bond or CD → Bonds & CDs; crypto, precious metals, warrant or right → Alternatives. Otherwise the words of an import file's type column, the first that matches in this order: cash, money market or sweep → Cash; option, crypto, precious metal, commodity, warrant, right or future → Alternatives; equity, stock, share, ETF, fund, ADR or closed end → Stocks / Funds; fixed income, bond, CD, certificate of deposit, Treasury, T-bill, muni or municipal → Bonds & CDs. Nothing for a blank type or one that names none of these (unit, structured product, when issued).

typedValueOnItsDate.rule: For a typed balance whose as-of date is a real day no later than today, walk back over recorded days from the latest one to the as-of date. Stop at a day without the account, with holdings for it, or holding a different value than the one replaced. Each day passed gets a newer row with the new value. Returns each day moved, oldest first, with old and new value.

unnamedActivityOf.rule: A record the app could not name is an ADJUSTMENT carrying the broker's word (its own field, or the note "broker word: …") with a non-zero amount or shares. It gives the word and the unsigned amount (none when only shares).

typedValueDatedBack.rule: Only for a save carrying value_as_of. It calls typedValueOnItsDate with the account before and after, and moves the daily net worth and daily cash-plus-investments totals by the same amount on each day moved.

moneyIntoAccount.rule: The one rule for a signed amount on a stored record (2026-10-21): the money it moved into its account, plus in and minus out. No amount on record (missing, empty or not a finite number) gives nothing. When the record says which way the money went — IN, it arrived in this account; OUT, it left — the answer is its amount without a sign, that way. Otherwise its kind decides, keeping the sign the amount was stored with: a deposit, sale, dividend, interest or coupon is plus the amount; a withdrawal, buy, fee, debt payment or transfer (out of the account it is written on) is minus the amount; any other kind gives nothing. Example: a broker's deposit of −$500, stored as $500 with direction OUT, is −$500; a typed deposit of −$500 with no direction is also −$500.

amountNotOnRecord.rule: True for a deposit, withdrawal, transfer, dividend, interest, coupon or fee whose amount is not on record (moneyIntoAccount gives nothing): its money is unknown, never $0 (DEC-3523 tenet 3). A buy, sale or share transfer is never one: its money is its shares × price or what the shares were worth.

fixStoredMoney.rule: Gives a money record saved before 2026-10-21 the direction the broker reports for it, and its real $0 (2026-10-21). Only a record that came through the link, states no direction, and is a deposit, withdrawal, transfer, dividend, interest, coupon or fee is looked at. Each fix the sync hands back (from a broker activity already stored: its account, day, kind, ticker, its size to the cent or nothing when the broker sent no amount, and the way the money went when the broker's sign says) is used once, on the first such record with the same account, the same day (first ten characters), the same kind and the same ticker (none counts as empty), whose stored size equals the fix's size within half a cent (the stored size read without a sign) — or, when the record holds no amount, whose fix's size is exactly 0. A matched record takes the fix's direction when the fix has one, and the amount 0 when it held no amount and the broker sent 0. Every other record is returned unchanged; with no fixes the list itself is returned.

refetchMarkKey.rule: The key under which the one-time full re-fetch for signs is marked as done for one linked account, beside that account's cursor: the word refetch, a colon, and the broker's account identifier. The sync reads the whole history of a linked account whose mark is not the current marker (signs-2026-10-21), and writes the mark when it has read the whole history; the mark is saved only with the sync that read it, so an account that could not be reached is re-read the next time.

lotCostOnRecord.rule: Whether what was paid for a purchase is on record: its cost per share is a number, finite and above zero. A missing cost is not on record, and neither is a stored $0 — what a blank cost in the holding editor saved, and what a sync wrote for a missing cost until 2026-10-20 — so it is never read as a real $0 (owner decision DEC-6627, tenet 4).

figures_checked_by_hand.6627: not a figure: the number of the owner decision DEC-6627 that this rule follows
figures_checked_by_hand.4: not a figure: tenet 4 of the MoneyKeel tenets (DEC-3523)

tradeFeeOnRecord.rule: The broker's fee on a buy or a sale, as the sync keeps it on the record, and whether the stored price already carries it (2026-10-21). Not a buy or a sale, or no fee sent (nothing, or not a number): nothing is kept. Otherwise the fee kept is the size of the broker's figure, its sign dropped, to the cent, worked in exact decimals. With no cash figure from the broker, a cash figure of zero, or no share count or a count of zero: the fee is not inside the price (the stored price is then the broker's own price). Otherwise the fee is inside the price (the stored price is the cash ÷ the shares), unless the broker sent a price, the fee is not zero and the cash, its sign dropped and to the cent, equals the shares (sign dropped) × that price to the cent — that cash was counted before the fee, so the fee is not inside the price. Example: 10 sold at $120 with a $5 fee and $1,195 of cash → fee $5, inside the price; the same sale reported with $1,200 of cash → fee $5, not inside the price.

figures_checked_by_hand.10: the worked example's shares sold — an example, not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.$120: the worked example's price — an example, not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.$5: the worked example's fee — an example, not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.$1,195: the worked example's cash after the fee: 10 × $120 − $5 — an example, not a figure the code holds
figures_checked_by_hand.$1,200: the worked example's cash before the fee: 10 × $120 — an example, not a figure the code holds

fixStoredFees.rule: Gives each buy or sale stored from a linked broker before the sync kept fees the fee the broker reports for it now, and whether its price already carries it (2026-10-21). With no reported fees: the records unchanged. A record is left as it is when it was not stored from a linked broker (the person typed it), it already holds a fee (a stored 0 included), or it is not a buy or a sale. Otherwise it takes the first reported fee not yet used whose account, kind, day (the record's date read to the day), ticker (none on either counts as the same) and share count (equal to within a billionth of a share) match; a reported fee with no share count matches nothing. Each reported fee is used once. A record nothing matches is left as it is.

buildDayFromAccounts.rule: Today's record of what each account holds, from the accounts as they stand, for the date handed in, marked observed and stamped with the time it was written. For each holding with a ticker and with shares above zero (the shares of its purchases added up, a missing count as 0): its worth = the value its account's balance was last built from, when the account's total is built from its holdings and that value is a number; else shares × the broker's last price, × one hundredth for a bond quoted per $100 of face value; with no last price, what was paid over its purchases with shares and a cost on record (a cost per share above zero), shares × cost per share added up, × the same one hundredth for such a bond; with neither, the value the account's balance was last built from. A holding whose worth is none of these is not known, and its WHOLE account is left off the day — never written as worth $0. Each holding kept is recorded with its shares, its price (nothing when none), its worth, in US dollars, under its ticker. Each account kept is recorded with: its cash = the uninvested cash stored on it, else the whole balance of a cash account (0 when none), else 0; the total its broker stated = the balance of a linked account (nothing when none), nothing for an account added by hand; the value typed = the balance of an account added by hand that is not cash and has no holdings (nothing when none), else nothing.

figures_checked_by_hand.$100: the face-value base a bond is quoted per (MK-XS-I-068); the code holds it as one hundredth

withArticle.rule: A phrase with its article in front, trimmed. A phrase on the list of words that take no article (interest, for one) comes back alone. One starting with a number takes an when the number begins with 8, or is 11 or 18, and a otherwise. A first word on the list said with a takes a, one on the list said with an takes an; a first word of two to five capital letters is an abbreviation said letter by letter, and takes an when its first letter is said with a vowel sound; any other takes an when it starts with a vowel, else a.

recomputeBalances.rule: Each account's balance rebuilt from its holdings, for an account whose total is built from them; a linked account, and one whose total is typed, is left as it is. Each holding's value now = its shares × today's latest close on record (marketValue) when the price history holds one; else what was paid over its purchases with a price paid on record; else the value it had; else 0. The account's balance = its uninvested cash (0 when missing) + its holdings' values added up.

partsShown.rule: Rows in whole dollars that add up to their printed total. A row that is not a number counts 0. The total = the rows added up, rounded to the dollar; each row is rounded down, and the dollars still missing go one each to the rows with the largest part of a dollar left over (the first row wins a tie), so no row is more than a dollar from its exact value and a row that is a whole number of dollars never moves.

monthShown.rule: A month's rows as printed: the rows of money in, settled to whole dollars that add to their total (partsShown), and the rows of money out likewise; what came in = the first total, what went out = the second, the surplus = the first less the second, so the rows add up to the surplus on the screen. When the month refuses, what went out and the surplus are no figure. Each kind of row's printed amounts are also added up by kind.

flowShown.rule: A month in three figures as printed: what came in and what went out, each rounded to the dollar, and the surplus = the first printed less the second, so the three add up on the screen.

chainShown.rule: A running balance as printed, month by month: the start rounded to the dollar; each month's End = the exact running balance rounded to the dollar; its In = its money in rounded, moved down or up by a dollar when that leaves the printed In, Out and End more than a dollar apart; its Out = its In less the change in the End printed, so each End printed is the End before it plus that month's In less its Out, as printed.

monthYearShown.rule: A whole month written as the dates are, without the day: the month's short name, then the year; nothing when either is missing.

buildDatedGrid.rule: The dated in and out grid: twelve months from this one. Money in is placed where it lands: each earner's wages as they land (wagesLandingByMonth); tips, self-employment, a bonus in its month, a signing bonus now, each vest with a value in the year and month its date names (equityByMonth for each year the twelve months span — a vest after them is listed as later, and a vest with a year but no month, or no date, is in no month and is listed apart with its reason: "vest month not entered" when its year is one of the twelve months' years, "vest date not entered" when it has no date) and other income by its own rhythm (monthly, yearly, quarterly or once), each less that month's rate in force; rental and investment income (investment income only when it is paid to the bank) less that rate unless the person gave a rate of their own; benefits in the months they are paid; family support; scholarships and loan money in their months, on their day when given; retirement income in its dated rows when handed in, else the flat monthly amount less the rate. The tax on interest and dividends that are reinvested comes out of the pay, or the first taxed income, that month. Money out: each once-in-a-while bill that names a month, in its months (its year when it has one), on its due day — a day past the end of a shorter month is that month's last day; a once-in-a-while bill that names no month has no date and is carried in the everyday expenses, a twelfth a month, as the budget counts it; then everyday expenses = the month's planned spending less those bills, so the bills add to the month's planned spending; one-off items a plan adopted; each debt, in each month, what it asks for that month (paymentInMonth, the one rule This month's plan asks too): its required payment from the month of its first payment to the month of its payoff, and a debt due in full its whole balance in the month it is due, while a balance is owed; a debt whose payments start after the twelve months, or that falls due after them, is listed as later. Anything outside the twelve months is listed as later. Each month: In, Out, In − Out, and the running balance from the starting balance (0 when none is handed in).

daysInMonth.rule: How many days the month has in that year, from the calendar: 28 or 29 for February (29 in a leap year), 30 or 31 for the others.

yearMonthOf.rule: What a typed date names, read from its start: four digits are the year; a dash and one or two digits after them are the month, when 1 to 12 (no month otherwise). Nothing at all (no date) when it does not start with four digits.

datedBillsIn.rule: The bills of one month of the table that fall on a date of their own: every bill item that is not a debt and not regular money — a once-in-a-while bill in its month, or a one-time item a plan created. Never the everyday expenses, a bill that names no month, or a debt payment. Nothing for no month.
